readme.markdown:
# Betterleaks Cloud - GitHub & S3 Secret Scanner

Cloud-hosted [Betterleaks](https://github.com/betterleaks/betterleaks) v1.3.1 for hunting leaked API keys, wallet private keys, and credentials anywhere on GitHub, in cloned git repos, or in S3 / R2 / MinIO buckets. Optional live validation probes each detected secret against the vendor API to flag which ones are still active.

Available as an [Apify Actor](https://apify.com/anshumanatrey/betterleaks-cloud). $0.05 start + $0.05 per repo scanned + $0.30 per live-validated key, each 10% less on Apify's Scale plan and 20% less on Business (the start fee excepted). No install, no CLI, flat JSON output.

---

## What does it do?

Scans a GitHub org, user, repo, pull request, issue, gist, action workflow, or S3 bucket for leaked credentials. Built on Betterleaks (the Gitleaks successor, maintained by the original Gitleaks author Zachary Rice + co-maintainers from Red Hat, Amazon, RBC). Every Betterleaks CLI flag is exposed as an input field. When you enable validation, each finding is probed live against the vendor API and tagged `valid`, `invalid`, `revoked`, `unknown`, or `error`.

## How is it different from running Betterleaks locally?

| | Local Betterleaks CLI | This actor |
|---|---|---|
| Setup | Install Go binary, set up GitHub token, configure shell | Paste a JSON input |
| Scope | One target at a time | github / git / s3 modes + our `global_github` mode (Code Search picks repos) |
| Validation cost | Your machine's HTTP egress | Apify-managed, parallel workers |
| Output handling | stdout JSON, parse yourself | Dataset records, filterable views |
| Schedule | cron + DIY | Apify Schedules built-in |
| Cost | Your laptop's electricity | $0.05 actor start + $0.05 per repo scanned |

## How is it different from our gitleaks-github-secret-scanner actor?

| | gitleaks-cloud | betterleaks-cloud (this) |
|---|---|---|
| Engine | Gitleaks 8.x | Betterleaks 1.3.1 (Gitleaks successor) |
| Live validation | not supported | yes (opt-in) |
| Source types | github + git only | github, git, s3, dir, stdin, global_github |
| Pricing | $0.01 + $0.02 per repo | $0.05 + $0.05 per repo + $0.30 per live-validated key |
| Best for | Volume scanning, low cost per scan | Premium scans where "is the secret still live?" matters |

## When should I use it?

- Auditing your own GitHub org for secrets that slipped into commits
- Bug bounty hunting where you want to validate keys live before reporting
- Pre-acquisition security check on a target company's GitHub footprint
- Continuous monitoring on a schedule, alerting on any new live-validated finding
- Forensics: tracing which dangling commit on which PR ref leaked a credential
- Scanning a Cloudflare R2 / AWS S3 bucket someone shared publicly

## What does it cost?

Pay-per-event:
- $0.05 per actor start
- $0.05 per repo scanned (in github / git / global_github modes)
- $0.01 per finding pushed to the dataset
- $0.30 per **live-validated** secret (only when validation is on AND status returns `valid`)
- $0.005 per Code Search query (only in `global_github` mode)

Typical scans:

| Scenario | Cost |
|---|---|
| Scan 1 small repo, 1 finding, no validation | $0.11 |
| Scan 1 big repo, 30 findings, no validation | $0.40 |
| Scan an org with 25 repos, 50 findings, no validation | $1.80 |
| 25-repo global search for `rzp_live_` | $1.93 |
| 100-repo scan, 200 findings, 10 live-validated | $10.05 |

Compare to GitGuardian Enterprise at ~$5000/year flat. Per-comprehensive-scan with this actor is 300-500x cheaper.

## Which modes can I scan in?

| Mode | What it scans | Required input |
|---|---|---|
| `github` | A specific GitHub org / user / repo / PR / issue / gist (you choose) | `target_url`, `github_token` recommended |
| `global_github` | All of GitHub by keyword - we add this layer via Code Search | `global_search_query`, `github_token` required |
| `git` | A single git clone URL with full history | `target_url` |
| `s3` | AWS S3, Cloudflare R2, MinIO, or any S3-compatible bucket | `target_url`, S3 creds (or `s3_anonymous` for public) |
| `dir` | A tarball / zip URL - we download, extract, scan filesystem | `dir_source_url` |
| `stdin` | Raw text content you paste in | `stdin_content` |

## Which GitHub resources can it scan in `github` mode?

All 12 surfaces betterleaks supports, selectable via `include` / `exclude`:

- `repos` (default), `forks`
- `prs`, `pr-comments`
- `issues`, `issue-comments`
- `actions`, `action-artifacts`
- `discussions`
- `releases`, `release-assets`
- `gists`

You can also filter by `since` / `until` dates, exclude repos by glob pattern, or target specific GitHub Actions workflow files.

## Does it find leaks that were deleted from current files?

Yes. Betterleaks scans the full git history. A secret that was committed and then deleted in a later commit still appears in the history and gets detected. The `Commit` field on each finding tells you which commit introduced the leak.

You can also enable advanced `--log-opts` pass-through to use git pickaxe (`-S secret_string`) for targeted historical searches.

## Is the secret validated against the live vendor API?

Optional - off by default to keep scans fast. Set `validation: true` and Betterleaks fires HTTP requests against the vendor API for each finding using the rule's built-in CEL validator.

Output fields:
- `ValidationStatus`: `valid` (still active), `invalid` (rejected), `revoked` (explicitly disabled), `unknown` (couldn't determine), or `error`
- `ValidationReason`: human-readable why
- `ValidationMeta`: vendor-specific metadata. For a GitHub PAT, this includes `username`, `name`, and granted `scopes`. For Stripe, the test/live mode + account info.

Note: validation only fires for rules that ship with a `validate` CEL clause in their TOML. Not every detected secret type has one (the upstream rule set is expanding over time).

You can also tune validation behavior:
- `validation_timeout` (per-request HTTP timeout)

readme.markdown:
# UFCalendar Fight API — agent skill

An installable skill that teaches a coding agent how to reach the
[UFCalendar Fight API](https://www.ufcalendar.com/developers) — the MMA Fight Data API
behind our [MCP server for UFC data](https://www.ufcalendar.com/developers/ufc-mcp-server)
and [MMA MCP server](https://www.ufcalendar.com/developers/mma-mcp-server): UFC, PFL,
OKTAGON, BKFC and RIZIN events, full fight cards, results, per-round stats,
fighter careers, judges' scorecards, UFC rankings history since 2013 and
per-country broadcast rights — over REST, the two SDKs, or the MCP server at
`https://api.ufcalendar.com/mcp`.

## Install

```bash
npx skills add UFCalendar/fight-api-skill
```

Or copy it in by hand:

| Agent | Where |
|---|---|
| Claude Code | `.claude/skills/ufcalendar-fight-api/` (project) or `~/.claude/skills/ufcalendar-fight-api/` (global) |
| Cursor | paste `SKILL.md` into a rule under `.cursor/rules/`, keep `references/` beside it |
| Codex | reference `SKILL.md` from `AGENTS.md`, keep `references/` beside it |

The skill is plain Markdown — `SKILL.md` plus four reference files. Nothing
executes.

## Contents

- `SKILL.md` — access in 60 seconds, base URL and envelope, the endpoints that
  answer the common questions, the don'ts, and when to use MCP vs REST vs SDK.
- `references/endpoints.md` — every endpoint and parameter. **Generated** from
  the OpenAPI document; do not edit by hand.
- `references/conventions.md` — envelope, pagination, errors, rate headers,
  tier gates, webhook signature verification.
- `references/mcp-clients.md` — copy-paste config for Claude Code, Cursor,
  Codex, Claude.ai and ChatGPT.
- `references/sdk.md` — Python and TypeScript quickstarts.

## Access

Every account gets the **free plan** (1,000 requests a month, no card, never
expires); the key self-serves at <https://www.ufcalendar.com/account/api?trial=1>.
Paid plans start at $19/month. `GET https://api.ufcalendar.com/v1/plans` answers with no
credential at all, so an agent can evaluate the API before anyone signs in.

Odds are the UFCalendar consensus line only (no book identities; information
only, not betting advice). Fighter images are Creative Commons and
must be shown with their credit. Not affiliated with UFC, Zuffa, TKO or any
promotion.

MIT licensed.

# Browserless MCP Server

MCP (Model Context Protocol) server for [Browserless.io](https://browserless.io) — expose the Browserless smart scraper API to LLM clients like Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code, and Windsurf.

## Quick Start

Get an API token from [browserless.io](https://browserless.io) (free tier available), then point your MCP client at the hosted server:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "browserless": {
      "url": "https://mcp.browserless.io/mcp?token=your-token-here"
    }
  }
}
```

No local install — see [Configuration](#configuration) for per-client snippets.

## Tools

| Tool                       | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `browserless_smartscraper` | Scrape a single webpage and return its content as markdown or HTML. Handles JavaScript-heavy pages and anti-bot measures automatically. For content across multiple pages, use `browserless_crawl`; to list a site's URLs, use `browserless_map`.                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `browserless_search`       | Search the web using Browserless and optionally scrape each result. Supports web, news, and image search with geo-targeting and time filters.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `browserless_map`          | Discover and map all URLs on a website. Scans via sitemaps and link extraction. Returns URLs with optional titles and descriptions. Useful for site audits and content discovery.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `browserless_crawl`        | Crawl a website and scrape every discovered page. Supports depth control, path filtering, sitemap strategies, and configurable scrape options. Returns scraped content and metadata for each page.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `browserless_performance`  | Run Lighthouse audits on any URL. Returns category scores inline and saves the full JSON report outside the conversation: a local path (stdio) or authenticated single-use download URL (HTTP). Download to disk and inspect only needed fields with `jq`; files expire after 15 minutes or when the MCP session ends. Optionally filter by category, emulate a mobile or desktop device, supply a custom Lighthouse config, or supply performance budgets. |
| `browserless_function`     | Execute custom Puppeteer JavaScript on the Browserless cloud. The function receives a `page` object and optional `context`; return `{ data, type }` to control the payload and Content-Type.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `browserless_export`       | Export a webpage via the Browserless `/export` API. Fetches the URL and returns its native content (HTML, PDF, image, etc.) with automatic content-type detection.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `browserless_agent`        | Drive a persistent browser session via a ReAct loop: snapshot the page, plan, batch interactions (click, type, scroll, evaluate, etc.), and re-snapshot. Uses ref-based selectors derived from snapshots, supports multi-tab workflows, screenshots, captcha solving, live URLs, and file upload/download (captured downloads auto-surface as handles; bytes never enter context).                                                                          |
| `browserless_skill`        | Load an on-demand recipe for a non-trivial page mechanic (shadow DOM, cookie consent, modals, captchas, dynamic content, snapshot misses, screenshots, tabs). Companion to `browserless_agent`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `browserless_profiles`     | List the authentication profiles saved for the current token, with cookie and origin counts. Pass a profile's name as `profile`

…

# Hexadata Tools — business validation MCP server for AI agents

[Hexadata Tools](https://apify.com/hexadatalabs/business-validation-tools-mcp) is a remote MCP server (Streamable HTTP, hosted on Apify) with **15 deterministic tools** that an AI agent should call instead of guessing: check digits, official tables and official calculations. No LLM inside: the same input always gives the same answer, nothing is stored, and you pay per call ($0.005 per single call, $0.002 per item in batches; invalid input is free).

## Tools

| Tool | Use this when… | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `validate_tax_id` | you need to check a company/taxpayer ID from MX, ES, AR, CL, CO, BR, GB, US, IT, FR, DE, PE, CA, AU or IN (RFC, NIF/CIF, CUIT, RUT, NIT, CNPJ/CPF, UK VAT, EIN, Partita IVA, SIREN/SIRET, USt-IdNr, RUC, BN, ABN/ACN, GSTIN) | official check-digit algorithms |
| `validate_vat_eu` | you need to confirm an EU VAT number is registered (reverse charge) | VIES (European Commission) |
| `validate_iban` | you need to validate an IBAN and split bank/branch/account | ISO 13616 + IBAN registry |
| `lookup_lei` | you need the legal entity behind an LEI, or the LEI of a company name | GLEIF |
| `lookup_postal_code` | you need city/region/coordinates for a postal code in 120+ countries (Mexico with colonia/municipio/estado) | GeoNames (CC BY) |
| `validate_bank_account` | you need to verify a Mexican CLABE (with bank name), a US ABA routing number or a SWIFT/BIC | Banxico SPEI list, ABA rules, ISO 9362 |
| `normalize_phone` | you need a phone number in E.164 with country and line type | libphonenumber |
| `validate_email_domain` | you need to know if an e-mail is well-formed and its domain receives mail (MX, disposable, free provider) | DNS + open blocklist |
| `get_fx_rate` | you need an official exchange rate for a date (30+ currencies, cross rates) | ECB, Banxico FIX |
| `business_days` | you need to add/count business days or list public holidays in 200+ countries | Nager.Date, Mexican LFT art. 74 |
| `lookup_industry_code` | you need a NAICS, NACE, CPV or SCIAN code for an activity, or its hierarchy | Census, Eurostat, EU Publications Office, INEGI |
| `lookup_hs_code` | you need a customs tariff code (US HTS 10 digits, EU CN8) and the US duty rate | USITC, Eurostat |
| `get_vat_rates` | you need the standard and reduced VAT/GST rates of 35 countries for a date | TEDB + national laws (versioned table) |
| `lookup_sat_catalog` | you need a Mexican CFDI 4.0 catalog value (product key, unit, CFDI use, tax regime, payment form/method…) | SAT official workbook |
| `calc_payroll_mx` | you need Mexican ISR withholding, employment subsidy, IMSS per branch, Infonavit and net pay for a salary | DOF, INEGI, Ley del Seguro Social (2026 tables) |

## Connect in one step

Direct server URL (Streamable HTTP):

```text
https://hexadatalabs--business-validation-tools-mcp.apify.actor/mcp
```

Authentication: `Authorization: Bearer <APIFY_TOKEN>` (free Apify account with monthly credit, or an x402 prepaid token bought with USDC, no account needed).

Or through the Apify MCP server, next to any other Actor:

```text
https://mcp.apify.com?tools=hexadatalabs/business-validation-tools-mcp
```

### Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf, VS Code (JSON config)

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "hexadata-validation": {
      "url": "https://hexadatalabs--business-validation-tools-mcp.apify.actor/mcp",
      "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer <APIFY_TOKEN>" }
    }
  }
}
```

### Claude Code

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http hexadata-validation https://hexadatalabs--business-validation-tools-mcp.apify.actor/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer <APIFY_TOKEN>"
```

## Example prompts

- "Validate these supplier tax IDs: MX EKU9003173C9, ES B12345674 and BR 11.222.333/0001-81, and tell me which are malformed."
- "Is IE6388047V registered for VAT, and what company is it?"
- "Check this IBAN before I pay: DE89 3704 0044 0532 0130 00. Which bank code is it?"
- "Which SAT product key and unit should I use to invoice software development services in Mexico, and what does a 20,000 MXN monthly salary cost the employer in 2026?"
- "What is the HTS code and US duty rate for stainless steel kitchen sinks, and the VAT rate in Germany today?"
- "Add 10 business days to 2026-12-18 in Mexico and list the holidays skipped."

## Pricing

$0.005 per single-item call, $0.002 per item when a call carries 2–500 items. Items answered with `INVALID_INPUT`, `UNSUPPORTED_COUNTRY` or `SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE` are never charged. 1,000 IBAN checks in batches ≈ $2; 100 Mexican payroll calculations ≈ $0.20.

## Links

- Actor page and full documentation: https://apify.com/hexadatalabs/business-validation-tools-mcp
- All Hexadata Actors: https://apify.com/hexadatalabs
- Issues and feature requests (new countries, catalogs, code systems): the Issues tab of the Actor.

# Gitleaks Cloud - GitHub API Key Hunter & Secret Scanner

Cloud-hosted gitleaks for hunting leaked API keys, tokens, and credentials across GitHub - 30+ services including Indian fintech.

Available as an [Apify Actor](https://apify.com/anshumanatrey/gitleaks-github-secret-scanner). Pay-per-event. The lightweight cheaper tier; sibling `betterleaks-cloud` adds live vendor-API validation.

# Browser MCP by [Agent360](https://agent360.dk)

**The browser tool that can stop and ask you.** A 2FA code, a CAPTCHA, a choice only you can
make: it asks on your own screen, then carries on in the same signed-in Chrome.

It drives the Chrome you are already signed into: no login step to fail, no API key to wire
up, no fresh profile that is a stranger to every account you have. Up to 20 agents at once, each
in its own colour-coded tab group. 40 tools, MIT, runs on your machine.

→ **[What it can and cannot get past](https://browsermcp.dev/docs/capability-matrix/)** - every
wall, marked *measured*, *by design*, *not yet*, or *won't*. Including the ones we have not fixed.

▶ **[Watch the 15-second film →](https://browsermcp.dev/film.mp4)**

Browser MCP gives Claude Code (and MCP clients that run local servers, such as Cursor and VS Code agent mode) control of your actual Chrome: your cookies, your sessions, your 2FA. So it works on CAPTCHA, 2FA and anti-bot sites where Playwright and Puppeteer get blocked - because it's *you* browsing.

The killer move: it hits a login wall, opens your Gmail, reads the verification code, and continues the sign-in. There is no email API to set up. Operate platforms with no API, QA your own web app end-to-end, or work dashboards, LinkedIn and Reddit at human pace - with you approving the sensitive steps.

40 tools. Auto-clicks the reCAPTCHA v2 checkbox, with a human fallback for the rest. Multi-session color-coded tab groups. **MIT, free, and it runs on your machine - no account, no telemetry, nothing sent to us.**

## The whole thing, in four steps

**Rather not do it by hand?** Paste this to your AI assistant - Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, VS Code, Windsurf, Cline - and it sets itself up:

> Set up Browser MCP for me. Read https://browsermcp.dev/llms-install.md and follow it for whichever AI client you are running in. One step only I can do - tell me which one, and wait for me. When I confirm, call `browser_list_tabs` to prove both halves are talking.
>
> If you cannot open URLs: `npx @agent360/browser-mcp install`

It reads the same guide the four steps below spell out by hand. One step stays yours either way: Chrome will not let an extension install itself, so you load it once.

**1 - Install the Chrome extension.** One click from the [Chrome Web Store](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/agent360-browser-mcp/jdehgalffmffhfhmmhaokfbfnafnmgcl); Chrome keeps it updated. No store? See the unpacked install below.

**2 - Add the MCP server.** Paste this in a terminal. Required - the extension does nothing on its own:

```bash
claude mcp add --scope user browser-mcp -- npx @agent360/browser-mcp@latest
```

**3 - Restart Claude Code.** That is what starts the server. The extension shows no badge until step 4 - the server only takes a port the first time your agent actually uses the browser. A green badge with the number of connected agents appears then; nothing on the icon before that is normal. (The icon itself never changes colour - it is the badge that turns green.)

**4 - Say this, to check it worked.** Paste it to Claude Code:

> Open example.com and take a screenshot.

You get an image back instead of *"I don't have browser access"*. **That's it - you're running.** → [What else to say](#youre-in-now-what)

Using Cursor, VS Code, Codex or Windsurf? Same server, that client's own config - the prompt at the top handles it, or see [browsermcp.dev/docs](https://browsermcp.dev/docs/install-cursor/). Everything below is the long version.

## The long version - install, step by step

> **Browser MCP is two halves and you need both:** a **Chrome extension** (drives the browser) and a **local MCP server** (what your agent actually talks to). Installing only the extension - e.g. straight from the Chrome Web Store - leaves it stuck on *"Not connected"*, because there is no server for it to reach. Chrome cannot install the server, and npm cannot install the extension. Hence two steps.

### Step 1: Register the MCP server with Claude Code

```bash
claude mcp add --scope user browser-mcp -- npx @agent360/browser-mcp@latest
```

That is Claude Code's own MCP command, so the entry lands in the config Claude Code actually reads. `--scope user` makes it available in every project.

Want the extension files on disk for the unpacked install in Step 2? Also run:

```bash
npx @agent360/browser-mcp install
```

It copies the extension to `~/.browser-mcp/extension/` and **prints that path in the terminal - copy it.** (It also registers the server with Claude Code, Codex, VS Code and Cursor if it finds them.)

### Step 2: Load the extension in Chrome

> Chrome won't let extensions install themselves from npm - you load it manually one time. To **update** later, re-run the install command and reload it (see [Keeping it updated](#keeping-it-updated)). Prefer the [Chrome Web Store](#chrome-web-store-no-developer-mode-auto-updating-extension) install if you'd rather have the extension auto-update.

1. **Open Chrome** and type `chrome://extensions` in the address bar
2. **Toggle "Developer mode"** ON (top right corner)
3. **Click "Load unpacked"** (top left, next to "Pack extension")
4. **Navigate to `~/.browser-mcp/extension/`** and click "Select"
   - On Mac: Press `Cmd+Shift+G` in the file picker, paste `~/.browser-mcp/extension/`, press Enter
   - On Windows: Paste `%USERPROFILE%\.browser-mcp\extension\` in the address bar (Windows is not yet verified: our automated tests do not pass there)
   - On Linux: Type `~/.browser-mcp/extension/` in the path field
5. **Restart Claude Code** so it picks up the new MCP server

That's it. The Browser MCP icon will appear in your toolbar, and 40 browser tools are now available in Claude Code.

### Alternative: Manual zip download (no npm)

If you don't want to use npm, download the extension directly:

1. [Download the extension zip](https://github.com/Agent360dk/browser-mcp/releases/latest) (`agent360-browser-mcp-<version>.zip`) from the

readme.markdown:
# CloudBrowser MCP Server

Give ChatGPT, Claude and your AI agents a real browser. CloudBrowser runs Chrome in the cloud. Your assistant opens a browser, navigates, reads pages, clicks, types and takes screenshots, and you can watch live or take over at any time.

- **Endpoint:** `https://mcp.cloudbrowser.ai` (Streamable HTTP)
- **Auth:** OAuth, sign in with your CloudBrowser account
- **Website:** https://cloudbrowser.ai/mcp
- **Official MCP Registry:** `ai.cloudbrowser/mcp`

## What you can do

- Open cloud Chrome browsers in your CloudBrowser account and connect to them.
- Navigate, read page content, find elements, click, type, run scripts and take screenshots.
- Save browser sessions and resume them later.
- Start a remote desktop to watch the browser live or take over.
- Detect CAPTCHAs. Login and verification walls stay with you.

## Connect

The server uses OAuth. Your client opens a browser window, you sign in with your CloudBrowser account and approve access. You do not copy an API key.

### Claude (claude.ai and Claude Desktop)

Open **Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector**, enter `https://mcp.cloudbrowser.ai` and select **Connect**.

### Claude Code

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http cloudbrowser https://mcp.cloudbrowser.ai
```

Then run `/mcp` in Claude Code and authenticate `cloudbrowser`.

### Codex CLI

```bash
codex mcp add cloudbrowser --url https://mcp.cloudbrowser.ai
codex mcp login cloudbrowser
```

### Cursor

Add this to `~/.cursor/mcp.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "cloudbrowser": { "url": "https://mcp.cloudbrowser.ai" }
  }
}
```

### VS Code

```bash
code --add-mcp '{"name":"cloudbrowser","type":"http","url":"https://mcp.cloudbrowser.ai"}'
```

### Gemini CLI

```bash
gemini mcp add --transport http cloudbrowser https://mcp.cloudbrowser.ai
```

### ChatGPT and other clients

Add a custom connector (in ChatGPT, developer mode) with the URL `https://mcp.cloudbrowser.ai`. Any client that supports Streamable HTTP and MCP OAuth works.

## Tools

The server advertises 20 tools. Your client gets the current schemas from `tools/list`.

- **Workspace:** `browser_workspace`, `resume_saved_session`
- **Browser lifecycle:** `open_browser`, `close_browser`, `get_browsers`, `start_remote_desktop`, `stop_remote_desktop`
- **Saved sessions:** `get_saved_sessions`, `remove_saved_session`
- **Connections:** `connect_to_browser`, `disconnect_browser`, `get_connected_browsers`
- **Page work:** `navigate_to_url`, `get_page_content`, `click_element`, `type_text`, `get_elements`, `take_screenshot`, `evaluate_script`, `detect_captcha`

## Authentication and account

OAuth 2.1 with PKCE and dynamic client registration. Sign in with your CloudBrowser account. Scope: `browser:control` (`openid email` optional). Developers can send their own account token instead: `Authorization: Bearer <your CloudBrowser API token>`. Keep the token in your client's secret settings, never in a prompt.

You need a CloudBrowser account. Browser usage follows your CloudBrowser plan.

## Links

- Website: https://cloudbrowser.ai
- MCP setup page: https://cloudbrowser.ai/mcp
- Native client packages (Claude Code, Gemini CLI and more): https://github.com/CloudBrowser-AI/skills
- Privacy policy: https://cloudbrowser.ai/privacy

## About this repository

This repository is the public home of the hosted CloudBrowser MCP server. It holds this setup guide and the registry metadata (`server.json` for the official MCP Registry, `glama.json` for Glama). The server runs as a hosted service at `https://mcp.cloudbrowser.ai`. Its source code is not in this repository.

Found a problem or have a question? Open an issue.


```python
from inspeximus import Inspeximus

m = Inspeximus("memory.json")
m.remember("The staging database is db-3.internal", key="staging-db")
m.remember("The staging database is db-7.internal", key="staging-db")   # a correction
m.recall("which staging database")[0]["text"]   # 'The staging database is db-7.internal'
m.revert("staging-db")                            # and it is reversible, on purpose
```

`memory.json` is a name, not a format: a new store is a SQLite file. Read it through `inspeximus` or the
`sqlite3` module, never with `json.load` or `cat`.

  
  

| | What you get |
|---|---|
| **A correction that holds** | `remember(key=...)` retires the old value by key. Restating the stale text does not bring it back; `revert()` does, as a recorded decision. |
| **Erasure you can prove** | `forget_subject()` removes every record about a person, leaves a signed content-free tombstone, and `erasure_certificate()` lets a third party check it with no private key. For authorship, the third party pins your public key (`expected_pubkey`) and witnesses the anchor. It covers this store only. |
| **What the agent knew when it acted** | A signed, hash-chained action ledger; `matches()` binds a retained transcript to its entry. |
| **When it happened** | RFC 3161 timestamps, and a check whether the authority was on the EU trusted list on that date. |
| **Evidence an auditor can read** | `inspeximus compliance` labels the evidence by article; export as a draft-sharif-agent-audit-trail-04 file. |
| **Any agent, one line** | MCP server for Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Codex and Cline; adapters for LangChain, LangGraph, ADK and more. |

---

## Why inspeximus

Use it when the agent runs for days and the facts it holds will change under it, and when
somebody can later ask what it knew and what it erased. That is the whole design brief.

| You have | Reach for |
|---|---|
| An agent that keeps confidently repeating a value you already corrected | `remember(key=...)`: the correction wins, the restatement does not bring the old value back, `revert()` is a recorded decision |
| A right-to-erasure request, or an auditor asking what the agent knew when it acted | `forget_subject()` with `erasure_certificate()`; the signed action ledger with `matches()` |
| Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Codex or Cline, and no memory between sessions | the MCP server, one config line |
| A framework (LangChain, LangGraph, ADK, Hermes, Haystack) and no way to prove a memory write happened | the adapters and the receipt chain |

**agno is the one that is not ours.** It ships an official integration example in its own
cookbook, [`cookbook/11_memory/integrations/inspeximus_integration.py`](https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/blob/main/cookbook/11_memory/integrations/inspeximus_integration.py),
merged in [agno#10146](https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/pull/10146) on 2026-09-20, alongside
`mem0`, `zep`, `memori` and `dakera`. Their own README describes it as *"inspeximus for
corrections that stay corrected."* We did not write that file's home and we do not maintain
it, which is exactly why it is worth listing: it is one integration a reader can check
without taking our word for anything. The same holds for [agmi](https://github.com/tech4biz-yasha/agmi),
an agent-memory integrity scorecard whose maintainer merged our three-row adapter,
[`agmi/adapters/inspeximus_rows.py`](https://github.com/tech4biz-yasha/agmi/blob/main/agmi/adapters/inspeximus_rows.py),
in [agmi#1](https://github.com/tech4biz-yasha/agmi/pull/1) after reproducing it himself.

Not the right tool when you want a hosted service with a dashboard, a knowledge graph over
documents, or the highest score on a conversational-recall benchmark. mem0, Zep and cognee lead
there, and the [comparison page](https://dancenitra.github.io/inspeximus/compare.html) says where
each of us wins and where we do not.

## The receipts

We measured the one thing the others do not publish: **how often a corrected fact comes back.**

Each system was run on its own native configuration, same task, same 30 trials:

| system | keeps the correction | resurrects the old value |
|---|---|---|
| **inspeximus** | **100%** | **0%** |
| Graphiti 0.x (Neo4j + OpenAI) | 86.7% | 13.3%  <sub>95% CI [3.3, 26.7]</sub> |
| mem0 2.0.11 (OpenAI native) | 53.3% | **46.7%**  <sub>95% CI [30.0, 63.3]</sub> |
| inspeximus, guard disabled | 0% | — <sub>the control: this is what the guard is doing</sub> |

<sub>n = 30 per system. mem0 measured at **2.0.11** (2026-07); mem0 is now on 2.0.18 and we have not
re-run it — the version is stamped rather than the claim being restated as current. Full method,
raw arrays and the re-runnable harness:
[RAMR](https://github.com/DanceNitra/ramr) · `echo_resistance_backends_result.json`</sub>

> **Read the Graphiti row correctly — its echo defense did not fail.** Our own raw output records
> `echo_attributable_flips: 0` out of **26** corrections that were extracted correctly before the echo
> ran. Graphiti's bi-temporal invalidation held every one of them. The 13.3% above is four *pre-echo
> extraction misses* — the correction never made it into the graph — which is a different failure from
> the one this table is about. Stated as the mechanism rather than the headline: on echo-attributab

readme.markdown:
# Hexadata MCP — official data sources as tools for AI agents

Hexadata publishes [Apify Actors](https://apify.com/hexadatalabs) that turn official registers and public portals into clean JSON. Every Actor is also an **MCP tool**: any MCP client (Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf, custom agents) can call it through the [Apify MCP server](https://mcp.apify.com), with no code to deploy.

This repository holds the connection instructions, a ready-to-use `server.json` for MCP registries, and example prompts. The tools themselves run on Apify and are billed per result (no results, no cost).

## Tools

| Tool (Actor) | What it returns | Source | Price |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [eu-tenders-ted-scraper](https://apify.com/hexadatalabs/eu-tenders-ted-scraper) | EU public tenders: contract notices, awards, buyer, deadline, value, CPV | TED Search API (EU Publications Office) | $5.00 / 1,000 |
| [sam-gov-opportunities-scraper](https://apify.com/hexadatalabs/sam-gov-opportunities-scraper) | US federal contract opportunities: solicitations, sources sought, awards, NAICS, set-asides | SAM.gov public daily extract (GSA) | $5.00 / 1,000 |
| [us-healthcare-providers-npi-scraper](https://apify.com/hexadatalabs/us-healthcare-providers-npi-scraper) | US clinics, hospitals, pharmacies, practices by specialty, city, ZIP | NPPES NPI Registry API (CMS) | $1.50 / 1,000 |
| [uk-companies-house-scraper](https://apify.com/hexadatalabs/uk-companies-house-scraper) | UK companies, new incorporations, SIC codes, officers (your free Companies House key) | Companies House API | $2.00 / 1,000 + $1.00 / 1,000 detail requests |
| [mexico-business-directory-denue](https://apify.com/hexadatalabs/mexico-business-directory-denue) | Mexican businesses from INEGI's DENUE: activity, size, address, GPS | INEGI DENUE API | $2.00 / 1,000 |
| [occ-mundial-jobs-scraper](https://apify.com/hexadatalabs/occ-mundial-jobs-scraper) | Mexican job listings with salary, company and work mode | OCC Mundial | $1.50 / 1,000 |
| [seccion-amarilla-business-scraper](https://apify.com/hexadatalabs/seccion-amarilla-business-scraper) | Mexican yellow-pages businesses: phone, WhatsApp, website, hours | Sección Amarilla | $5.00 / 1,000 |

All tools share the same field conventions (`id`, `title`/`name`, `url`, `country`, `publishedAt`, `scrapedAt`), an `onlyNewSinceLastRun` mode for scheduled runs, and a `maxResults` cap that bounds the cost of every call.

## Connect in one step

Add the Apify MCP server to your client with the tools you want. Use one Actor:

```text
https://mcp.apify.com?tools=hexadatalabs/eu-tenders-ted-scraper
```

or several, comma-separated:

```text
https://mcp.apify.com?tools=hexadatalabs/eu-tenders-ted-scraper,hexadatalabs/sam-gov-opportunities-scraper,hexadatalabs/uk-companies-house-scraper
```

Authentication: sign in with OAuth on first use (the client opens apify.com), or send your Apify token as `Authorization: Bearer <APIFY_TOKEN>`. Running tools needs an Apify account; a free account includes monthly credit.

### Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf (JSON config)

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "hexadata": {
      "url": "https://mcp.apify.com?tools=hexadatalabs/eu-tenders-ted-scraper,hexadatalabs/sam-gov-opportunities-scraper,hexadatalabs/us-healthcare-providers-npi-scraper,hexadatalabs/uk-companies-house-scraper,hexadatalabs/mexico-business-directory-denue,hexadatalabs/occ-mundial-jobs-scraper,hexadatalabs/seccion-amarilla-business-scraper",
      "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer <APIFY_TOKEN>" }
    }
  }
}
```

### Claude Code

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http hexadata "https://mcp.apify.com?tools=hexadatalabs/eu-tenders-ted-scraper,hexadatalabs/uk-companies-house-scraper" --header "Authorization: Bearer <APIFY_TOKEN>"
```

### VS Code (`.vscode/mcp.json`)

```json
{
  "servers": {
    "hexadata": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://mcp.apify.com?tools=hexadatalabs/sam-gov-opportunities-scraper",
      "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer ${input:apify-token}" }
    }
  }
}
```

The configurator at [mcp.apify.com](https://mcp.apify.com) generates the snippet for any client; the Apify CLI can also install it (`apify mcp install cursor`).

## Example prompts

- "Which contract notices for road maintenance were published on TED in Poland and Czechia this week, and which close before December 15?" → `eu-tenders-ted-scraper`
- "Find small-business set-aside solicitations for IT services in Virginia posted since Monday." → `sam-gov-opportunities-scraper`
- "List the physical-therapy clinics in ZIP codes starting with 787 with phone numbers." → `us-healthcare-providers-npi-scraper`
- "Which software companies were incorporated in Manchester in the last 7 days, and who are their directors?" → `uk-companies-house-scraper` (pass your Companies House key in `apiKey`)
- "Give me 50 dental clinics in Monterrey with coordinates." → `mexico-business-directory-denue`

Every Actor description and input field starts with "Use this when…", so agents pick the right tool and fill the input without extra prompting. Set `maxResults` in the prompt ("at most 100") to bound the cost.

## From code instead of MCP

The same Actors are available through the Apify API and client libraries:

```python
from apify_client import ApifyClient
client = ApifyClient("<APIFY_TOKEN>")
run = client.actor("hexadatalabs/eu-tenders-ted-scraper").call(run_input={"searchQueries": ["software"], "countries": ["DE"], "maxResults": 100})
items = client.dataset(run["defaultDatasetId"]).list_items().items
```

Each Actor's README has curl, Python and Node examples plus scheduling and webhook notes.

## Legal and data

Hexadata Actors use official APIs or public portals, respect their terms, and exclude personal data unless you opt in (for example `includeOfficers` on Companies House or `includeContacts` on SAM.gov). Attribution to the source is included in every item (`source`).

readme.markdown: The most advanced MCP memory server. Period. Hybrid search (BM25 + jina-embeddings-v5 RRF + cross-encoder rerank) · 100+ languages · Temporal Knowledge Graph · Query-aware ranking · Corpus origin detection · Agent/persona disambiguation · Topic tunnels · AAAK compression (5-10x token savings) · GraphRAG · Chunked RAG · Auto-Compaction · Auto-Classification · Memory Capsules · HTTP API · Signed automatic updates · Single binary · Zero API calls --- ## Why AI coding assistants forget everything between sessions. MemoryPilot gives them persistent, searchable memory with project awareness, semantic understanding, and automatic knowledge organization. Built-in AAAK compression and memory capsules reduce token consumption by 5-10x when loading context. Every memory is auto-classified with the right importance, kind, and TTL on insert. The database compacts itself automatically — zero maintenance. Install MemoryPilot One-liner install for Cursor, Claude Desktop, VS Code, Windsurf, Claude Code, Codex and ChatGPT. Single Rust binary, zero runtime dependencies. Install the latest release → How it works The 9 pillars — hybrid search, temporal knowledge graph, GraphRAG, AAAK compression, auto-classification, self-healing — explained end to end. Read the architecture → ## Benchmarks ### LongMemEval-S (ICLR 2025) — Academic Standard Evaluated on the 470 answerable questions of [LongMemEval-S](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.10813) (ICLR 2025; the 30 abstention questions are left out, as the official retrieval protocol does). Turn-level index, ~50 sessions per haystack. **What the score measures.** `R@5` here is session-level `recall_any@5`: a question counts as a hit when at least one of the top 5 retrieved turns belongs to one of its gold sessions. It is a retrieval metric, not answer accuracy, and a question that needs several sessions counts as a hit as soon as one of them is found (300 of the 470 questions have more than one gold session). For scale: a plain BM25 over turns, with no embeddings, scores about 93% on the same metric and 74% on `recall_all@5`. These figures were measured with v4.2 (multilingual-e5-small); the current default model has only been measured on a 100-question slice (see v4.6 below). #### Retrieval scores (same metric family, setups differ) | System | R@5 (recall_any, session level) | Notes | Source | |--------|--------------------------------:|-------|--------| | **MemoryPilot v4.2 (adaptive rerank)** | **99.1%** | 470 questions, ~900 ms/query on an M-series Mac | This repo, `--benchmark-longmemeval` | | **MemoryPilot v4.2 (rerank off)** | **98.7%** | 470 questions, ~28 ms/query with `MEMORYPILOT_CROSS_RERANK=off` | This repo, `--benchmark-longmemeval` | | MemPalace v3.3.3 (hybrid) | 98.4% | 450 held-out questions after tuning on 50; 96.6% raw on 500 | MemPalace v3.3.3 release notes | | agentmemory v0.9 | 95.2% | 500 questions (abstention included), all-MiniLM | [github.com/rohitg00/agentmemory](https://github.com/rohitg00/agentmemory) `benchmark/LONGMEMEVAL.md` | | mcp-memory-service v10.34.0 | 80.4% | labelled R@5; hit definition not stated | [v10.34.0 release notes](https://github.com/doobidoo/mcp-memory-service/releases/tag/v10.34.0) | #### Answer accuracy (a different metric: an LLM reads the retrieved context and a judge grades the answer) | System | QA accuracy | Setup | Source | |--------|------------:|-------|--------| | Mem0 (cloud) | 94.4% | Mem0's own suite, top-200 retrieval | [mem0.ai blog](https://mem0.ai/blog/benchmarked-openai-memory-vs-langmem-vs-memgpt-vs-mem0-for-long-term-memory-here-s-how-they-stacked-up) | | Zep / Graphiti | 63.8% / 71.2% | gpt-4o-mini / gpt-4o as reader, GPT-4o judge | [arXiv 2501.13956](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.13956), Table 2 | | MemoryPilot | not measured | an end-to-end QA run is planned | | > All figures are published by their own authors, none was reproduced independently, and the two tables cannot be compared with each other. On session-level recall MemoryPilot posts the highest published local score, by a margin smaller than the gap between this metric and a plain BM25 baseline. The protocol to settle a comparison: same 470 questions, same hardware, every system run by the same script, reporting `recall_any@5`, `recall_all@5`, turn-level evidence recall and end-to-end QA accuracy with a fixed reader and judge. #### Detailed view — MemoryPilot vs MemPalace (closest local competitor) | Metric | MemoryPilot v4.2 (rerank off) | MemoryPilot v4.2 (adaptive rerank) | MemPalace v3.3.3 | Delta vs MemPalace | |--------|---------------------------------|------------------------------------|------------------|--------------------| | **R@5** | **98.7%** | **99.1%** | 96.6% raw / 98.4% hybrid | +2.5% vs raw / +0.7% vs hybrid | | **R@10** | **99.6%** | **99.4%** | ~97%¹ | +2.6% vs raw | | **NDCG@10** | **95.1%** | **96.0%** | Not published | MemoryPilot publishes | | **MRR** | **93.6%** | **94.9%** | Not published | MemoryPilot publishes | | **Avg search latency** | ~28 ms (`MEMORYPILOT_CROSS_RERANK=off`) | ~900 ms (the default) | N/A | search call only, models warm | > ¹ Validated with the full 470-question evaluation set (after dropping the 30 abstention questions) in two modes: hybrid retrieval with the rerank off (BM25 + cosine RRF, `MEMORYPILOT_CROSS_RERANK=off`, ~28 ms/query) and the default adaptive cross-encoder rerank (`MEMORYPILOT_CROSS_RERANK=adaptive`, jina-v2-multilingual, fusion weight 0.45, ~900 ms/query, suitable for benchmarks and high-stakes recall). readme.markdown:
# Ekwo OS

**Ekwo** is open source accounting, ready to use on **[Ekwo Cloud](https://cloud.ekwo.ai)**: the web application for your invoices, your bank statements, your VAT returns and the electronic invoices your country uses, in your own instance, with an account opened in a minute. **Ekwo OS** is the free and open source core it runs on, under AGPL-3.0: install it on your own Supabase project and own your accounting data, forever.

Built and maintained by **Ekwo**. Ekwo OS is a schema, the rules of each country as data, and the tools — a command line and an MCP server — with which you, your accountant and the AI agent you choose work in the same books, each with their own access. Ekwo reads any supplier invoice, in any language, with the AI model you choose, and every entry is posted on your confirmation. What Ekwo is, and its limits: [DISCLAIMER.md](DISCLAIMER.md).

*From an empty Supabase project to a prepared VAT return, for two countries
side by side. How it was recorded: [`docs/demo/`](docs/demo/).*

**Try it on your own books.** Already using Claude? [Start with
Claude](docs/start-with-claude.md) goes from a free Supabase project to your
own books taken over, questioned and your next VAT return prepared, in about
twenty minutes. Or open the same books in the web application,
[Ekwo Cloud](https://cloud.ekwo.ai).

---

## Why Ekwo

> The long version — financial autonomy for every business, accounting as a
> commons, a network rather than a vendor — is in [MANIFESTO.md](MANIFESTO.md).

**The data belongs to the business, and the work of keeping the books can be
done by software the business also owns.** So the whole accounting core is
open, the data sits in a Postgres database you control, and the interface is
designed for machines as much as for people. Supabase gives the schema a REST
API for free, and an MCP server sits on top of it, so an AI agent can book a
purchase, match a payment or prepare a VAT return on your own data — as you,
under your own row level security, without the data leaving your account.

What ships today:

- **The core** — schema, posting rules, taxes, reports, financial statements,
  as migrations you apply to a database you control.
- **A country pack for every country listed below**, each a versioned set of
  data with a year of books that proves it.
- **`ekwo`, the command line** — one command installs everything on your own
  Supabase project; the same tool then keeps books from a terminal.
- **The MCP server**, hosted at `https://mcp.ekwo.ai/mcp` or run locally with
  `npx @ekwo-ai/mcp`, so any AI agent can operate the books.
- **Modules** for fixed assets, budgets, corporate income tax and electronic
  invoicing.
- **The compass of the company** — `financial_analysis()` reads, from the
  posted entries, the aggregates a country pack defines (revenue, equity,
  cash, receivables, payables…), or, in a country whose pack defines none,
  thirteen of them read by account type through the generic framework, so that days of cash, net margin, current
  ratio, equity ratio, days of sales and of purchases outstanding and growth
  come from the books with nothing to set up. The Analysis screen of Ekwo
  Cloud and the `financial_analysis` tool of the MCP server read it;
  [`docs/analysis.md`](docs/analysis.md) says how, and how a pack adds the
  section.
- **Format libraries** under MIT — the files administrations, banks and
  e-invoicing networks exchange, written and read.

Who it is for: a company that wants to keep its own books with an AI at the
keyboard, and a founder who wants to know, from those books, how long the cash
lasts and how fast customers pay; an accounting firm that runs several
companies inside one installation; a developer who needs a real double-entry
core with tax rules as data rather than as code; and anyone who wants to leave
a proprietary system with the books intact.

## What is in this repository

A double-entry accounting core for Postgres. There is no server to run:
Supabase turns the schema into a REST API with an OpenAPI description, and row
level security decides who sees what.

- **Double entry, enforced by the database.** An entry cannot be posted unless
  it balances, and a locked period refuses writes at the trigger — not in a
  form validator.
- **Documents and entries are two layers.** An invoice answers to EN 16931 and
  Peppol; an entry answers to the chart of accounts. Keeping them apart keeps
  both honest.
- **Country rules are data.** A tax points at the ledger accounts it posts to
  and at the boxes of the declaration it feeds. Adding a régime is a row, not a
  release.
- **Every label is data, in every language a country pack publishes.**
  Identifiers stay English; what a person reads comes from the pack, in the
  language of the company or of the reader. See
  [`docs/languages.md`](docs/languages.md).
- **Every country a pack, out of the box.** United Arab Emirates (`ae`), Antigua and Barbuda (`ag`), Albania (`al`), Հայաստան (`am`), Angola (`ao`), Argentina (`ar`), Austria (`at`), Australia (`au`), Azərbaycan (`az`), Bosna i Hercegovina (`ba`), Barbados (`bb`), Bangladesh (`bd`), Belgium (`be`), Burkina Faso (`bf`), България (`bg`), البحرين (`bh`), Burundi (`bi`), Bénin (`bj`), Bermuda (`bm`), Brunei Darussalam (`bn`), Bolivia (`bo`), Brasil (`br`), The Bahamas (`bs`), Bhutan (`bt`), Botswana (`bw`), Canada (`ca`), République démocratique du Congo (`cd`), Centrafrique (`cf`), Congo (`cg`), Schweiz (`ch`), Côte d’Ivoire (`ci`), Chile (`cl`), Cameroun (`cm`), 中国 (`cn`), Colombia (`co`), Costa Rica (`cr`), Cabo Verde (`cv`), Cyprus (`cy`), Czechia (`cz`), Germany (`de`), Djibouti (`dj`), Danmark (`dk`), Dominica (`dm`), Dominican Republic (`do`), Algérie (`dz`), Ecuador (`ec`), Estonia (`ee`), مصر (`eg`), España (`es`), Ethiopia (`et`), Finland (`fi`), Fiji (`fj`), France (`fr`), Gabon (`ga`), United Kingdom (`gb`), Grenada (`gd`), საქართველო (`ge`), Guernsey (`gg`), Ghana (`gh`), The Gambia (`gm`), Guinée (`gn`), G

readme.markdown:
# atlassian-browser-mcp

MCP server that wraps the upstream [mcp-atlassian](https://github.com/sooperset/mcp-atlassian) toolset with browser-cookie authentication via Playwright, for Atlassian Server/Data Center instances behind corporate SSO (Okta, SAML, etc.) where API tokens are not available. It runs locally over stdio: you log in once with the bundled CLI, and the server reuses the cookies.

## Features

- Every mcp-atlassian Jira and Confluence tool, authenticated with your SSO browser session instead of an API token, with upstream's own network hardening (SSRF redirect checks, DNS pinning, retries, rate limits, proxy and TLS settings) kept in force.
- One login per service with the CLI; the server itself never opens a browser, so it never hangs waiting for one.
- `atlassian_auth_status` tells an agent which service needs a login before it fails mid-task.
- Optional one-time seeding of the automation profile from your real Chrome profile (`ATLASSIAN_SEED_FROM_CHROME_PROFILE`), so the first login is often one click.
- On macOS, reuses a live session from an installed Chromium-family browser (Arc, Brave, Edge, Chrome and others) without opening a window. It reads that browser's Keychain key, says so on stderr, and can be turned off.
- Separate cookie jars for Jira and Confluence, holding only that host's cookies, mode 0600. Jira-only or Confluence-only setups work.
- A command-line front-end (`atlassian-cli`) for scripts and agents: get and search issues and pages.
- Falls back to token auth with `ATLASSIAN_BROWSER_AUTH_ENABLED=false`.

## Quick start

From PyPI, with [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) installed:

```bash
JIRA_URL=https://jira.example.com uvx --from atlassian-browser-mcp atlassian-cli login jira   # once per service, opens your browser
CONFLUENCE_URL=https://confluence.example.com uvx --from atlassian-browser-mcp atlassian-cli login confluence
JIRA_URL=https://jira.example.com CONFLUENCE_URL=https://confluence.example.com uvx atlassian-browser-mcp
```

From a checkout, with the exact versions in `uv.lock`:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/GeiserX/atlassian-browser-mcp.git && cd atlassian-browser-mcp
UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=.venv-atlassian-browser uv sync --frozen   # installs the versions in uv.lock
JIRA_URL=https://jira.example.com CONFLUENCE_URL=https://confluence.example.com ./atlassian-cli login jira   # once per service
```

Needs Python 3.11+, [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/), Google Chrome and a display for the login. The server never opens a browser window. It reads the saved cookies; when they are missing or expired it returns an `AuthRequiredError` asking you to run the login again, and on macOS it also looks for a live session in your installed browsers in the background, so a retry a few seconds later may already work. Seeding from Chrome and every setting are in [Getting started](docs/getting-started.md).

## Add it to your client

Every client runs the server over stdio. Set only the URL of a service you use. The examples use the PyPI package through `uvx`; from a checkout, replace `uvx atlassian-browser-mcp` with `/path/to/atlassian-browser-mcp/run-atlassian-browser-mcp.sh`.

**Claude Code**

```bash
claude mcp add --transport stdio atlassian \
  --env JIRA_URL=https://jira.example.com \
  --env CONFLUENCE_URL=https://confluence.example.com \
  -- uvx atlassian-browser-mcp
```

**Claude Desktop** (`claude_desktop_config.json`) and **Cursor** (`~/.cursor/mcp.json` or `.cursor/mcp.json`)

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "atlassian": {
      "command": "uvx",
      "args": ["atlassian-browser-mcp"],
      "env": {
        "JIRA_URL": "https://jira.example.com",
        "CONFLUENCE_URL": "https://confluence.example.com"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

**VS Code** (`.vscode/mcp.json`)

```json
{
  "servers": {
    "atlassian": {
      "type": "stdio",
      "command": "uvx",
      "args": ["atlassian-browser-mcp"],
      "env": {
        "JIRA_URL": "https://jira.example.com",
        "CONFLUENCE_URL": "https://confluence.example.com"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

**Codex** (`~/.codex/config.toml`)

```toml
[mcp_servers.atlassian]
command = "uvx"
args = ["atlassian-browser-mcp"]
env = { JIRA_URL = "https://jira.example.com", CONFLUENCE_URL = "https://confluence.example.com" }
```

**Protocol.** Speaks MCP 2025-11-25, 2025-06-18, 2025-03-26 and 2024-11-05 over stdio, which covers clients that open with an `initialize` handshake (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor and VS Code today). MCP 2026-07-28 is not supported yet: upstream mcp-atlassian pins `mcp<2` and `fastmcp<4` (https://github.com/sooperset/mcp-atlassian/issues/1541), and this server follows as soon as upstream moves. It runs on stdio only and refuses to start with any other `FASTMCP_TRANSPORT`.

## Read-only mode

Write tools act as you, with your SSO identity. To hide all of them (create, update, delete, transition, upload, restrictions), set `READ_ONLY_MODE=true` in the server's `env`. Upstream enforces it when listing and when calling. `ENABLED_TOOLS` (a comma-separated allow-list of tool names) and `TOOLSETS` narrow the list further; see [Configuration](docs/configuration.md).

## Tools

| Tool | What it does | Hints |
|------|--------------|-------|
| `atlassian_auth_status` | Whether each service's saved session exists and works: jar age, cookie expiry, a live check, the next step | read-only |
| `atlassian_login` | The exact `atlassian-cli login <service>` command to show the user | read-only |
| `jira_*` (63) | Every upstream Jira tool: issues, search, comments, transitions, sprints, boards, versions, links, worklogs, attachments, service desk, forms | 38 read-only, 25 write |
| `confluence_*` (35) | Every upstream Confluence tool: pages, search, comments, labels, attachments, history, templates, restrictions | 20 read-only, 15 write |

Every tool carries a title and all four annotation hints (read-only, destructive, idempotent, open-world), so clients can auto-approve reads and confirm writes. The

readme.markdown:
# Memory.fit MCP

**Memory.fit** keeps your training, sleep, recovery and fuel in one place for the AI you already use. Your AI reads workouts from your watch and apps, sleep and HRV, and what you ate, then writes your week back: sessions, daily targets and meal plans, which show in the [Memory.fit app](https://memory.fit/app) on iPhone and Android.

This repository holds only the connection settings for Memory.fit MCP, a hosted server. There is nothing to run or build.

- **Address:** `https://api.memory.fit/mcp` (Streamable HTTP)
- **Sign-in:** OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration. Your AI opens the Memory.fit sign-in page; you choose what it may do. No key needed. AIs without sign-in can use a personal key from the app (Settings › AI agents › Use a key instead), sent as `Authorization: Bearer mem_pat_…`.
- **Needs:** a Memory.fit account, set up in the app first.

## Connect

| App | How |
|---|---|
| Claude | Settings › Connectors › Add custom connector, paste the address |
| ChatGPT | Settings › Apps and connectors › Create, paste the address |
| Grok, Grok Bot | Connectors › New connector › Custom, paste the address |
| Cursor | Install this plugin, or add `mcp.json` from this repo to `~/.cursor/mcp.json` |
| Claude Code | `claude mcp add --transport http memory-fit https://api.memory.fit/mcp` |
| Codex | `codex mcp add memory-fit --url https://api.memory.fit/mcp` |
| Gemini CLI | `gemini extensions install https://github.com/Fun-Management-SRL/memory-fit-mcp` |
| Cline | MCP Servers › Remote Servers: name `memory-fit`, URL `https://api.memory.fit/mcp`, transport Streamable HTTP (or the JSON below) |
| Anything else | Any MCP client: the address above, then sign in |

Step-by-step pages for each AI: [memory.fit/ai-coaches](https://memory.fit/ai-coaches).

### Cline, or any client with a JSON settings file

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "memory-fit": {
      "type": "streamableHttp",
      "url": "https://api.memory.fit/mcp",
      "disabled": false
    }
  }
}
```

The first call opens the Memory.fit sign-in (OAuth 2.1). A client without OAuth can use a personal key from the app (Settings › AI agents › Use a key instead) as a header:

```json
"headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer mem_pat_..." }
```

## What your AI can do

- Read: workouts (Garmin, Wahoo, COROS, Polar, Suunto, Apple Health, Health Connect and more), sleep, HRV and resting heart rate, body composition, what you ate and drank, your races and goals.
- Write, with your permission: training sessions (sent to your watch), daily targets, meal plans, logged meals, notes for your other AIs.
- Check in: `get_updates` returns only what arrived since it last looked.

Memory.fit recommends nothing itself: the plans are your AI's, the data is yours. It is not medical advice.

## Links

- Website: https://memory.fit
- Privacy: https://memory.fit/privacy
- Terms: https://memory.fit/terms
- Support: support@memory.fit

The connection settings in this repository are MIT licensed. Memory.fit, the server and the app are not.

readme.markdown:
# AiAkiv plugins

Official plugin marketplace for **AiAkiv** — long-term memory for AI agents
(MemoryWeft). AiAkiv stores your important conversation content as a knowledge
graph and recalls it across sessions, folders, and AI clients.

## Install

### Claude Code

```
/plugin marketplace add aiakiv/aiakiv-plugins
/plugin install aiakiv@aiakiv
```

On first use, Claude Code opens an OAuth login in your browser. Sign in / sign up
and approve — the `mweft_*` memory tools then appear.

### Cursor

One-click: use the **Add to Cursor** button in the [AiAkiv console](https://aiakiv.com),
or bundle the plugin from the [`aiakiv/`](./aiakiv) directory.

## What's inside

- [`aiakiv/`](./aiakiv) — the AiAkiv memory plugin: remote MCP server
  (`https://mcp.aiakiv.com/mcp`) + an onboarding skill. Carries manifests for
  Claude Code (`.claude-plugin/`) and Cursor (`.cursor-plugin/`).

## Trust & data

AiAkiv is a hosted service operated by **OnMinimum**. Content you save leaves your
machine and is stored on AiAkiv servers. Terms: <https://aiakiv.com/terms> ·
Privacy: <https://aiakiv.com/privacy>.

The plugin files in this repository are released under the **MIT License**
(see [`aiakiv/LICENSE`](./aiakiv/LICENSE)); the hosted service is governed
separately by the terms above.

readme.markdown:
# Playwright Workspaces

> ✅ **Playwright Workspaces is now Generally Available!**

[Playwright Workspaces](https://aka.ms/pww/docs) is a fully managed service for end-to-end web testing, built on top of [Playwright](https://playwright.dev). With Playwright Workspaces, you can significantly speed up test execution by running tests in parallel using managed cloud-based browers. The service takes care of the underlying infrastructure and complexity, allowing you to validate your web app across major browsers on both Linux and Windows—so you can ship features faster and with greater confidence.

👉 [Get started with the Quickstart](https://aka.ms/pww/docs/quickstart)

## Documentation

The full documentation is now available on [**learn.microsoft.com**](https://aka.ms/pww/docs)

There you’ll learn how to:

- Run and scale Playwright tests in the cloud
- Optimize test suite performance and reliability
- Test across multiple browsers and operating systems
- Set up secure, region-aware test environments
- Integrate with CI/CD

## Playwright Cloud Browsers remote MCP (preview)

The [Playwright Cloud Browsers remote MCP server](https://aka.ms/pww/mcp/docs)
gives AI agents managed cloud browsers over Streamable HTTP. Agents can create a
browser session, navigate and inspect pages, interact with elements, and close
the session without installing Playwright or a browser locally.

The remote MCP server is in **preview**, separately from the generally available
Playwright Workspaces service. Preview features do not have a service-level
agreement and are not recommended for production workloads.

### Prerequisites and authentication

You need an Azure subscription, a Playwright workspace with access to the remote
MCP preview, its region and workspace ID, and an identity with permission to use
browser sessions in that workspace.

Use the endpoint for your workspace's region:

```text
https://<region>.mcp.playwright.microsoft.com/playwrightworkspaces/<workspace-id>/mcp
```

Replace both placeholders with your workspace values. Use Microsoft Entra ID
with a client that supports OAuth discovery. The server publishes
protected-resource metadata; your signed-in identity must also have the required
workspace RBAC access. See the [authentication and setup guide](https://aka.ms/pww/mcp/docs)
for permissions and supported compatibility options. Never commit access tokens
or paste them into prompts.

### Connect from VS Code or the GitHub Copilot app

- **VS Code:** Run **MCP: Add Server** from the Command Palette, select **HTTP**,
  enter the resolved workspace endpoint, and choose a configuration destination.
  Follow the server trust and Microsoft Entra sign-in prompts. See
  [Add MCP servers in VS Code](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/agent-customization/mcp-servers).
- **GitHub Copilot app:** Open **Customize > MCP**, add a custom server using the
  resolved workspace endpoint, and follow the supported authentication prompts.
  See [Configuring MCP servers](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/github-copilot-app/customize-github-copilot-app#configuring-mcp-servers).

With the server connected, ask the agent to create a browser session, open
`https://example.com`, report the page's main heading, and close the session,
including on failure. Inspect the actual MCP tool calls and outputs to verify
the connection. See the [service guide](https://aka.ms/pww/mcp/docs) for session
limits, supported tools, and troubleshooting authentication, timeouts, and
expired sessions. Report service issues through this repository's
[issue tracker](https://github.com/Azure/playwright-workspaces/issues).

### Registry metadata

The server is published as `com.microsoft/playwright-cloud-browsers` in the
[Official MCP Registry](https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io/v0.1/servers/com.microsoft%2Fplaywright-cloud-browsers/versions/latest).
The root [`server.json`](./server.json) is a public copy of the published
metadata. Publication and metadata updates are managed by the service team;
changing this copy does not publish an update or establish a listing in
downstream client catalogs.

## Samples

Explore sample projects for different test runners:

- [Playwright Test with JavaScript/TypeScript](./samples/playwright-tests/)
- [NUnit with C#](./samples/.NET)
- [Python](./samples/playwright-python/)
- [Playwright Library projects](./samples/playwright-lib/)
- [Foundry Prompt Agents using Playwright Workspaces Remote MCP](./samples/remote-mcp/foundry-prompt-agents/)
- [Foundry Hosted Agents using Playwright Workspaces Remote MCP](./samples/remote-mcp/foundry-hosted-agents/)
- [App Verification Skills (verify skill)](./samples/app-verification-skills/)

## Migrating from Microsoft Playwright Testing

- See the [Migration Guide](./migration-guide.md) and [Troubleshooting Tips](./migration-troubleshooting.md)

## Issues

To report a bug, request a feature, or ask for a quote limit increase, please use the [Issues](https://github.com/Azure/playwright-workspaces/issues) section of this repository.

## More Resources

- [Documentation](https://aka.ms/pww/)
- [Pricing](https://aka.ms/pww/pricing)
- [Playwright](https://playwright.dev)

readme.markdown:
# Echo Memory

**Shared memory for AI agents, as a graph in your own database.** What Claude Code learns,
Cursor and Codex can recall. Every fact records who wrote it and when, and the server
never calls a model to store one.

<sub>Every line above is real output, captured from these commands against a throwaway
database. The transcript is at
[`.github/branding/demo-transcript.txt`](.github/branding/demo-transcript.txt).</sub>

> Your agents start every session from zero. The usual fix is a notes file you paste into
> context, which grows until it is mostly irrelevant to whatever you are asking. Echo
> Memory is the other shape: facts connected to each other, and a query that returns the
> few that matter. On the author's own 325 fact store that is **96.7% less context** for
> the same answer, with the answer still present 87.2% of the time across 1,190 queries
> the harness derived from their own answers.

```
write_episode                          query_memory
  billing ──uses──▸ Razorpay             "how do we take payments"
    │ written by claude-code               ▸ billing uses Razorpay, not Stripe
    │ supersedes ──▸ Stripe                  written by claude-code, 3 days ago
    └ no model invoked                     ▸ 1,372 tokens, not 41,838
```

## Install

**Requires:** Python 3.11+ and Docker (for the database).

```bash
pipx install echo-mem
echo-memory quickstart
```

`quickstart` starts the database, applies the schema, and prints the `claude mcp add`
line that registers it, filled in with the port it actually used. The Postgres image is
published, so nothing compiles.

Or use the hosted service and run no database at all:

```bash
pipx install echo-mem
echo-memory connect <key>          # a key from https://app.echo-mem.com
```

Then once per machine, so an agent knows *when* to record and recall rather than only
that the tools exist:

```bash
echo-memory install --global
```

> **Restart your client afterwards.** An MCP server is a long lived process that holds
> the code and config it started with, and an editable install does not change that.

> **The PyPI name is `echo-mem`, not `echo-memory`.** That name belongs to an unrelated
> hosted product. The import package and the CLI are both `echo_memory` / `echo-memory`;
> only the distribution name differs.

## Upgrading

```bash
pipx upgrade echo-mem
echo-memory init-db                # apply any new migrations
echo-memory reindex                # rebuild what the new code derives
```

Both steps, in that order, and neither is optional on a store that predates the version
you just installed.

**Skipping `init-db` fails loudly.** A read against a schema older than the code raises an
undefined column, which is the good case: it stops rather than answering from something it
half understands.

**Skipping `reindex` fails silently, which is worse.** Derived data that the new code reads
differently is still the old data, and nothing errors. Concretely, on an upgrade to 0.5.3
the lexical corpus statistics are treated as stale until rebuilt, so BM25 stays off and
your queries keep ranking by `ts_rank` while the setting reports as on. `reindex` rebuilds
the embeddings and those statistics together. `echo-memory health` tells you afterwards.

## Usage

```bash
echo-memory status                 # what each scope holds, and which agents have written
echo-memory health                 # a score, what is weak, and what to do about it
echo-memory dashboard --serve      # the graph, in a browser, localhost only

echo-memory why <fact_id>          # the full audit trail for one fact
echo-memory recall "<question>"    # query the store from a terminal
echo-memory export                 # everything, as JSON

echo-memory install --for cursor   # wire one client, project scoped
echo-memory adopt                  # wire every MCP client on the machine, each with its own id

echo-memory infer-causal-hints     # type the facts whose own sentence states a cause (dry run)

echo-memory eval                   # retrieval quality against your own store
echo-memory eval --context         # what a recall costs against injecting everything
echo-memory eval --context --sweep # the same, as a curve across corpus size
echo-memory eval-external locomo <path>       # LoCoMo, the corpus the published figures use
echo-memory eval-external longmemeval <path>  # LongMemEval, the same
echo-memory calibrate              # is entity resolution trustworthy on your data
echo-memory benchmark              # write, query and digest latency
```

### The seven MCP tools

| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `write_episode` | Store entities and the facts connecting them. No model call. |
| `query_memory` | Hybrid vector and full text retrieval, fused by reciprocal rank. Full text ranks by BM25. Takes `as_of` to read the store as it stood at an instant, and `about` to return the facts recorded against one or two named entities. |
| `trace_cause` | Causal chains through the entities a subject matches, not a ranked list. |
| `record_recall_save` | Mark that a recalled fact saved re explaining something. Refuses a fact no read returned. |
| `get_audit_log` | Every change to memory, with a plain language reason. |
| `pending_documents` | Memory files this project wrote that the graph has not heard about. |
| `mark_ingested` | Close one of those out. |

## What you get

**A graph, not a list.** Entities are nodes and a fact is an edge between two of them.
Two sessions that never knew about each other resolve onto the same entity by name, so
the second inherits what the first learned.

**Bounded retrieval, designed but not built.** The plan is that old, rarely read memory
demotes into higher level summaries over time, with nothing discarded and every summary
still edged back to the facts it came from. None of it exists yet: there is no tiering,
no summarisation, and retrieval today walks every active fact in the scope. It is
described in [`docs/designs/`](docs/designs/) and l

readme.markdown:
# Apiary Memory MCP

> **Also known as:** Apiary Memory · 记忆蜂巢 · Memory Hive · 蜂巢 ·
> `apiary-memory` on PyPI and `io.github.330899935/apiary-memory` on the MCP Registry (from v0.2.0) ·
> old names `memory-hive-mcp` / `hive-memory` (v0.1.9 and earlier) still install and still work.
> Not affiliated with [hive.com](https://hive.com) (team collaboration) or the `hive-mcp` Claude Code plugin.

**Local-first personal memory for AI agents, over MCP.** Your agents can search what you have
confirmed and propose what they think you should keep; **only you can confirm it.** Everything
lives in one file on your own disk, and nothing is sent anywhere.

It runs on its own. A working SQLite memory store ships inside this package — no account, no
cloud, no daemon, no dependencies.

```bash
pip install apiary-memory
```

**Desktop app, no terminal:** download [`apiary-memory-0.2.0.mcpb`](https://github.com/330899935/apiary-memory/releases/download/v0.2.0/apiary-memory-0.2.0.mcpb) and double-click it.

Measured on 2026-10-27, on one MacBook with the Hive running locally — script and raw output in [`bench/`](bench/):

| Measure | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Search latency | **p95 111 ms**, p50 76 ms (warm, includes HTTP) |
| Retrieval | correct entry in **top-5 for 97.5%** of 40 trials |
| Corpus | **1,303 entries · 2.39 M chars · 45 days**, plaintext only |

*Retrieval used each entry's own title as the query — an easy set. It shows the index is complete and ranks correctly on exact terms, not how well it answers a question asked in your own words. Run [`bench/bench_search.py`](bench/bench_search.py) on your own Hive.*

---

## What you get without the app

A complete, if modest, memory server. On a machine with nothing else installed:

| Call | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| `initialize` | answered locally, protocol `2024-11-05` |
| `tools/list` | answered locally, six tools |
| `propose` | **writes to a real database** on your disk |
| `recall` | **searches that database** and returns ranked entries |
| `get_context` | a digest of what you confirmed most recently |
| `manage` | read one entry, list what is pending, forget, restore |
| `say` / `board` | a shared message board for coordinating several agents |

Storage is SQLite at `~/.memory-hive/hive.db` by default. Search is lexical — character bigrams
for Chinese, words for Latin script — so it ranks well when the words overlap and finds nothing
when they do not. There are no embeddings and no vector index. Every response says
`"mode": "local"` so you can always tell which engine answered.

**Without the app, the database is plain SQLite: it is not encrypted.** That is stated here
rather than discovered later — see [Honest limits](#honest-limits).

## What the app adds

[Apiary Memory for macOS](https://apps.apple.com/app/id6806992983) is the same design with the
expensive parts built: eight vaults with four of them locked behind a PIN (Argon2id-wrapped key,
AES-256 at rest), a daily evolution log, multi-agent identity management, and a UI for reading
and confirming. It also answers MCP itself, with richer ranking.

If the app is running, this package uses it and leaves the local file alone. If it is not, the
local store answers. You do not have to choose up front:

| `HIVE_MODE` | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| `auto` (default) | Ask the app. Use the local store **only if the app is unreachable.** |
| `local` | Never touch the network. Always use the local store. |
| `remote` | Only the app. A connection failure is an error, not a reroute. |

One rule holds in every mode: **if the app is running and answers with an error, that error is
returned unchanged.** Falling back on a refusal would write your memory into a second database
while your client believed it had reached the app. Silent data forking is worse than an error
message, so a reply from the app is final. The fallback fires on a connection failure, and on
nothing else.

## Measured on the app

The numbers below come from the macOS app's local HTTP service on one MacBook — **not** from
this package's SQLite store, which is a different engine over a different dataset. Mixing the
two would be the usual benchmark trick, so they are kept apart.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Store size (four plaintext vaults) | **1,356 entries**, 2.52M chars, 47 distinct days |
| Retrieval hit rate | Top-5 **92.5%**, Top-20 **95.0%** (n=40) |
| Latency (local HTTP, incl. round trip) | p50 **90 ms**, p95 **127 ms** |

Measured 2026-10-29 against the live service. The hit-rate queries were each entry's own
title — the easy case. It shows the index is complete; it does not show that free-form
questions land. A separate pilot using plainly-phrased questions found the right entry in the
top 5 only twice out of roughly a dozen, which is the biggest known weakness of this version.

The four encrypted vaults are excluded from the count because they are unreadable by design.
A load test at 1,000,000 synthetic entries gave 0.6 s warm search, 5.3 GB RSS and a 1.0 GB
index — see [`bench/`](https://github.com/330899935/apiary-memory/tree/main/bench) for the
script and raw output.

## Install

```bash
pip install apiary-memory        # the server: apiary-memory (was memory-hive-mcp)
                                 # the human's CLI: apiary-memory-cli (was memory-hive-mcp-cli)
```

Python 3.8 or newer. There is nothing else to install — the package uses only the standard
library, and `sqlite3` is part of it.

From a checkout:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/330899935/apiary-memory
cd apiary-memory
PYTHONPATH=src python -m hive_mcp.stdio
```

## ⚡ Key Guarantees

* **0.00% Statistical Hallucination:** Fact recall is deterministic and geometric ($A_4$ Pentatope lattice memory). No language model exists in the fact retrieval path.
