# DiffCI Core

**Affected checks before push, for AI coding agents.** DiffCI tells Claude Code, Codex, Cursor (or you) which tests and checks a change affects, so they run before the push instead of failing at the full CI gate afterwards. MIT licensed, runs locally, sends nothing by default, and falls back to the full suite whenever the evidence is incomplete.

```sh
npx "@diffci.com/diffci@latest" check
```

Run it in any Git checkout with Node.js 22.5+. [What the output means](docs/using-diffci.md).

## Why

Coding agents pass the narrow check they picked and miss wider breakage, then rerun the whole suite when they are unsure. We measured this on our own agent-built production app (about 1,100 commits in two months, most of them co-authored by Claude):

- **104 pushes failed the full gates after push.** Each passed whatever the agent ran locally.
- **Agents chose their own test files 928 times and ran the full suite 282 times**, but asked a tool which tests were affected only 24 times.
- **When DiffCI could narrow the run, it selected 2.2% of test files**, cutting test time by 93%. None of those commits had a failing test, so this shows speed, not regression catching.
- **DiffCI still fell back to the full suite on 58% of commits**, mostly because a config file or `package.json` changed. Narrowing those safely is the main open problem, and [a good place to contribute](#contributing).

## Use it from your coding agent

The public [`integrations/agent-plugin`](integrations/agent-plugin) package
makes the published DiffCI CLI available as a checkout-aware local MCP plugin.
It contains only public marketplace metadata, skills, and a pinned npm
launcher; it does not include product services or private source. The
[cross-agent installation guide](docs/agent-installation.md) covers Codex,
Claude Code, Cursor, Grok, Meta Muse Code, and generic MCP hosts.

```sh
# Codex
codex plugin marketplace add DiffCI/core
codex plugin add diffci@diffci-local

# Claude Code
claude plugin marketplace add DiffCI/core
claude plugin install diffci@diffci-marketplace
```

Cursor Marketplace reads [`.cursor-plugin/marketplace.json`](.cursor-plugin/marketplace.json)
from this repository. Meta Muse Code reads the native root
[`marketplace.json`](marketplace.json). Before a public listing is approved,
use the local MCP configuration in the agent-plugin package or visit
https://diffci.com/mcp-server.

## GitHub Action

The public [`action.yml`](action.yml) is an observation-only GitHub Action
wrapper. It runs the pinned published DiffCI CLI outside the observed checkout,
retains existing CI jobs, and uploads an advisory report. See the
[observer Action guide](docs/github-action-observer.md) and
[workflow example](examples/github-actions-observer.yml).

The [v0.3.10 corresponding source](https://github.com/DiffCI/core/tree/4c76be14cec37d94eb7df93922f3c29d202f4e65/packages/diffci-cli)
remains publicly available at tagged Core commit `4c76be14` (`cli-v0.3.10-source`)
while distribution migrates to the Core-native CLI package.

`diffci check` compares full and selected runtime when safe to measure, writes reports outside the checkout, and sends nothing by default. Test commands can generate files; keep required CI authoritative.

**Measured example:** one controlled Cal.com sandbox replay measured **44.2% net reduction** in install + pretest + test runtime including analysis overhead. This is a job-equivalent comparison, not production savings or a forecast for your repository. [Method and limitations](https://diffci.com/case-studies/calcom).

[Star Core](https://github.com/DiffCI/core) · [Volunteer a pilot repository](https://diffci.com/#pilot) · [Find a first contribution](https://github.com/DiffCI/core/issues?q=is%3Aopen+label%3A%22good+first+issue%22).
Watch → Custom → Releases and Discussions for benchmark results and support updates. [Public roadmap](docs/roadmap.md).

This is the standalone Core engine. It analyzes local JavaScript/TypeScript repositories, supported Vue components, root Go modules and conventional Maven reactors, traces dependency impact, infers GitHub Actions structure and proposes test selections with evidence and full-run fallbacks. It works without a DiffCI account, hosted service or API key. See [the release boundary](docs/release-boundary.md) for support limits.

**Want to try DiffCI in an existing repository?** Use the published CLI: `npx @diffci.com/diffci@latest check`. See [the CLI quickstart](docs/using-diffci.md) for a no-execution analysis option, prerequisites, and result interpretation. The commands below build the standalone engine from source.

## Run locally

Requires Git and Node.js 22.5 or later.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/DiffCI/core.git
cd core
npm ci
npm run build
npm test
node dist/cli.js plan --repo /path/to/clean-checkout --base HEAD~1 --head HEAD
```

The target must be a clean Git repository root checked out at `--head`. Fetch the base commit beforehand if using a shallow clone. JSON goes to stdout; analysis errors exit nonzero and recommend full CI. Core does not execute repository scripts, contact a DiffCI backend or send telemetry. Installation requires the npm registry.

To evaluate the same command on pull requests without changing required jobs, copy the [advisory GitHub Actions example](examples/README.md).

**Plans are advisory.** This release does not execute, skip or cancel CI jobs. `SKIP_CANDIDATE` is a candidate, not permission to bypass a check. Keep full CI authoritative while evaluating Core. Missing command synthesis, unsupported configuration and incomplete evidence must not be treated as an empty test suite. Static analysis is not proof that a test can safely be omitted.

For Maven jobs whose CI runs a lifecycle goal or profiles other than `test`, declare them in `diffci.json` (or the `diffci` key in `package.json`):

```json
{ "maven": { "goal": "verify", "profiles": ["run-its"] } }
```

# Free Public REST APIs - AI SENSE AS

No API key | No sign-up | No cost

Provided by **[AI SENSE AS](https://aisenseapi.com)** (Oslo, Norway).
Full endpoint reference: [`API.md`](API.md) | Repo: [github.com/aisenseapi/aisense-free-public-rest-apis](https://github.com/aisenseapi/aisense-free-public-rest-apis)

**Base URL:** `https://aisenseapi.com/services/v1/`

## Free public MCP endpoints

The AI SENSE MCP server is at:

`https://aisenseapi.com/mcp`

The AI SENSE MCP server covers Heartbeat, Lease, Agent Wake tasks, Agent
Inbox, human approval, webhook capture, temporary storage, URL shortening,
time and UUIDs. It needs no account or API key. Heartbeat uses
`create_heartbeat`, `read_heartbeat` and `ping_heartbeat`. Lease uses
`create_lease_namespace`, `acquire_lease`, `renew_lease`, `release_lease` and
`complete_lease`. Agent Inbox uses `create_agent_inbox` and
`read_agent_inbox`. See
[`MCP.md`](MCP.md) for the tool list, data boundary and client examples.

The Agent Queue tools use separate read, write and worker tokens issued at
creation. The semantic search tools use a read token and a write token in
the same way.

Start with [AGENT-GUIDE.md](AGENT-GUIDE.md) to choose tools, then
[AGENT-QUICKSTART.md](AGENT-QUICKSTART.md) for a complete Queue workflow and
retry decisions.

The server reports version `1.15.0` and offers 73 tools: the workflow tools
and the REST utility endpoints below as tools, apart from AIQ, `ip_datetime`
and `ping`, which stay on REST. The official MCP Registry lists
`com.aisenseapi/free-public-tools` version `1.15.0` as active and latest,
published 30 October 2026 at 10:57 UTC.

aamio has its own MCP endpoint at `https://aamio.at/mcp`, eleven tools for
ephemeral agent rendezvous: a thread with a secret read key and a public write
address, a receipt of hashes that outlives it, presence, and the open board of
needs and offers at `https://board.aamio.at/`. No account and no API key. The
official MCP registry lists it as `at.aamio/aamio`. The AI SENSE endpoint does
not proxy these tools either.

Verifyum has its own dedicated MCP endpoint at
`https://api.verifyum.com/mcp`. It exposes the three Verifyum proof operations
without an account or API key. File hashing still happens on the agent's
machine. The browser flow, public HTTP API and published protocol remain
available. The official MCP registry lists it as `com.verifyum/mcp` version
`0.1.0`. Finalized proofs also join hourly and daily Merkle checkpoints in
the [Verifyum Witness Layer](https://verifyum.com/witness). Nine records
surround each finalized proof.

| Tier | Records |
| --- | --- |
| Primary evidence | One finalized Solana Mainnet Memo transaction per proof |
| Independent corroboration | Hourly OpenTimestamps on Bitcoin, daily qualified EU timestamp, daily witness-cosigned Sigsum and daily Certificate Transparency certificate |
| Operator records and availability redundancy | Verifyum Ed25519 signature, GitHub checkpoint log, Software Heritage and Internet Archive |

The Solana transaction is the primary evidence. Deep Solana history generally
requires an archival provider. Glasklar, Mullvad and Tillitis cosign the
Sigsum digest with a quorum of two out of three. The qualified timestamp uses
RFC 3161. Its eIDAS Article 41(2) presumption covers the daily checkpoint root
alone. A Verifyum user proof is not a qualified electronic timestamp. Verifyum
is not a qualified trust service. Software Heritage and Internet Archive show
what was stored. They do not establish when the original file existed. The
number of channels is not a quality score.

Every finalized proof is also announced on
[Telegram](https://t.me/verifyum) and in the
[Atom feed](https://verifyum.com/feed.xml). These are announcement channels.
They are excluded from the nine evidence records. Their timestamps date the
announcement. They say nothing about the original file date.

An agent can also assemble one decision record locally from its instructions,
prompt, model, parameters, tool calls and output, then anchor only the
commitment. The proof shows that the exact record existed unchanged by the
block time. It does not prove that the model actually ran with the recorded
settings.

---

## Free public Agent2Agent (A2A) endpoint

Agents that speak Agent2Agent can reach five of these capabilities at:

`https://aisenseapi.com/a2a`

JSON-RPC 2.0, protocol revision 1.0, no account and no API key. The agent card
is a plain GET at `https://aisenseapi.com/.well-known/agent-card.json`.

A2A is the protocol for delegating work to another agent. MCP is the protocol
for exposing tools. Most of this service is tools, so only the five task-shaped
capabilities are offered over A2A: `agent-wake`, `human-approval`,
`agent-inbox`, `webhook-capture` and `agent-queue`. The other tools are not
reachable through it. MCP stays the richer workflow surface with its own tool
schemas. Over A2A the queue skill creates a queue and returns its three role
tokens; enqueueing, claiming and acknowledging stay on REST and MCP.

A2A puts no skill id on the wire, so the caller names the skill in a data part
of the message, as `{"skill": "agent-wake", "arguments": { ... }}`. That is a
convention this service documents, not a field the protocol defines, and a
message without it is refused. The card declares `streaming` and
`pushNotifications` false, so those methods answer `-32004` and `-32003`.
`ListTasks` returns an empty page, because nobody is authenticated and a task ID
is the only credential there is. See [`API.md`](API.md#agent2agent-a2a) for the
skills, task states, response shapes and error codes.

---

Every serialization format marketed for LLM input ships a token-saving claim
measured against a single tokenizer. Agent traffic crosses vendors, so we
measured instead of assumed: six formats and 33 single-construct probes,
priced by five vocabulary families (OpenAI o200k, DeepSeek, Qwen,
SentencePiece, Tekken), with each p

# BillingEngine MCP server

Create customers and invoices, look up open invoices and record payments in
[BillingEngine](https://www.billingengine.com) by talking to Claude, Cursor or any other
[MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) client:

> "Create an invoice for Acme Painting over 100 euros."
>
> "Which invoices are overdue?"
>
> "Acme paid invoice 2610030028, record the payment."

BillingEngine is invoicing software for freelancers and small businesses with
[e-invoicing](https://www.billingengine.com/en/features) (EN 16931, XRechnung, ZUGFeRD / Factur-X).
The server is a thin layer over the [BillingEngine API](https://www.billingengine.com/en/api)
and runs on your computer.

## Requirements

- Node.js 20 or newer
- A BillingEngine account on a paid plan. The API is not available in the Free plan.
- Your API key from **Settings > API keys** in BillingEngine

## Setup

### Claude Desktop

Add this to `claude_desktop_config.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "billingengine": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "billingengine-mcp"],
      "env": { "BILLINGENGINE_API_KEY": "your-api-key" }
    }
  }
}
```

### Claude Code

```sh
claude mcp add billingengine --env BILLINGENGINE_API_KEY=your-api-key -- npx -y billingengine-mcp
```

### Cursor and other clients

Use the same `command`, `args` and `env` as above in the MCP settings of your client.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `find_customers` | Searches customers by company, name, email or identifier of another system |
| `create_customer` | Creates a customer |
| `update_customer` | Changes a customer |
| `create_invoice` | Creates a **draft** invoice for a customer |
| `update_invoice` | Changes a draft invoice |
| `list_invoices` | Lists invoices, filtered by status, type, customer, number, identifier or date |
| `get_invoice` | Returns one invoice with items, tax breakdown and status |
| `download_invoice` | Saves the PDF or the XML e-invoice to your Downloads folder |
| `record_payment` | Records a payment for sent invoices |
| `list_payments` | Lists payments, optionally for one invoice |

## What it does and does not do

- Invoices are created as **drafts**. Nothing is sent to your customers; you review and send
  the invoice in BillingEngine. Every result contains a link to open the draft.
- Prices are net or gross, as set in your account; every invoice says which. Amounts in results are decimal strings such as `"119.00"`. Number, language, texts, VAT treatment and payment terms come from your
  account settings, exactly as in the invoice form.
- **Nothing can be deleted** through this server.
- New invoices count towards the monthly invoice maximum of your plan.
- The API allows 60 requests per minute per key.
- Your key stays on your computer and is only sent to BillingEngine.

If a key is ever exposed, create a new one under **Settings > API keys**. The old key stops working
immediately. The settings also show when the key was last used.

## Configuration

| Variable | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `BILLINGENGINE_API_KEY` | Your API key (required) |
| `BILLINGENGINE_URL` | Base URL, defaults to `https://www.billingengine.com` |

## Development

```sh
npm install
npm run build
```

readme.markdown:
# gdharness

**An agent cannot see a running game.** It reads your scripts and guesses at the rest: whether the
button is on screen, whether the panel updated, whether that error mattered.

gdharness makes the engine answerable instead. What the screen says, where a control is, what a
property reads right now, what the console printed, what broke and on which line.

## Install

Hand this to your agent:

```text
Install gdharness here by following https://aureliolo.github.io/gdharness/agent.md,
then tell me what it asked you to recommend back to me.
```

Or do it yourself, and pick your harness:
[aureliolo.github.io/gdharness](https://aureliolo.github.io/gdharness).

## The loop it exists for

```jsonc
editor_run      { "op": "start", "projectPath": "C:/games/hall" }
runtime_inspect { "op": "find", "says": "Buy" }              // the button, by the word on it
runtime_input   { "op": "click", "nodePath": "/root/Hall/Ledger/BuyButton" }
runtime_inspect { "op": "text", "nodePath": "/root/Hall/Ledger" }   // what the panel says now
editor_output   { "projectPath": "C:/games/hall" }           // errors and warnings, with backtraces
```

The open editor plays the game, so its debugger holds it, which is what lets you set a breakpoint
and read the variables in scope when it stops.

Every answer is read back out of the engine after the fact, never echoed from the request. A tool
that cannot answer says which state it is in and what would change it, rather than answering
emptily, so a call that succeeded is a call that was understood.

## At a glance

|           |                                                                                      |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Needs     | Godot 4.7 or newer, Node 22 or newer. Runs under Bun 1.4 too.                        |
| Surface   | 30 tools named `domain_verb`, 4 `godot://` resources and 3 prompts                   |
| Reaches   | The editor that is open, a game it is playing, and the project on disk               |
| Harnesses | 35, written inside the project wherever the harness has a project config             |
| Skill     | Written to `.agents/skills`, which every major harness reads                         |
| Install   | npm, or a Sigstore-signed archive with an SBOM, SLSA Build Level 3                   |
| Proven    | Every tool driven against Godot 4.7.2 in CI, on Windows, Linux and macOS             |
| Status    | 1.0: every release is a patch. [What a bump means](.github/CONTRIBUTING.md#versions) |

Older 4.x is likely to work and is not tested.

## Documentation

[aureliolo.github.io/gdharness](https://aureliolo.github.io/gdharness): installing it, how the
parts connect, and every tool, op and argument.

[SECURITY.md](.github/SECURITY.md) is how to report something.
[CONTRIBUTING.md](.github/CONTRIBUTING.md) is what a change has to clear.

## Project

Fork of [GoPeak](https://github.com/HaD0Yun/Doyunha-Gopeak) v2.3.9, September 2026, MIT: the
original MCP server [godot-mcp](https://github.com/Coding-Solo/godot-mcp) by
[Solomon Elias](https://github.com/Coding-Solo), GoPeak by [HaD0Yun](https://github.com/HaD0Yun),
and completely reworked since to be hardened, condensed and more streamlined.

Not affiliated with the Godot Foundation.

# Bugasura MCP Server **Connect AI assistants directly to your test management workspace.** Bugasura MCP Server enables AI tools like Claude, VS Code Copilot, and Cursor to interact with your Bugasura projects—manage test cases, track issues, plan sprints, and more—all through natural language. --- ## ⚠️ Breaking changes in 3.3 | What changed | 3.2 | 3.3 | |--------------|-----|-----| | Requirement ↔ test case links | `bugasura_link_unlink_requirement_testcases` with `is_delete` | `bugasura_link_requirement_testcases` and `bugasura_unlink_requirement_testcases` (destructive); both take comma-separated `testcase_ids` | | Coda, Jira, Confluence and Figma imports (10 tools) | Offered on every transport | Local (STDIO) only. They take that service's API token as an argument, so the hosted server no longer lists them and refuses calls to them | ## ⚠️ Breaking changes in 3.0 Authentication moved to OAuth 2.0 sign-in. If you're upgrading from 2.x: | What changed | 2.x | 3.0 | |--------------|-----|-----| | Hosted (HTTP) authentication | `X-Bugasura-API-Key` header or `Authorization: Basic ` in the client config | Sign in from the MCP client: it opens the Bugasura login + consent page once, then refreshes tokens silently. No key in any config file. | | `api_key` tool parameter | Present on every tool | Removed. Tools never accept a key; the assistant must not ask for one. | | STDIO (local subprocess) | `BUGASURA_API_KEY` env var | Unchanged — the env var is the only credential source for STDIO. | | Prompt | `setup_api_key` | `connect_bugasura` | | Server requirements (HTTP) | none | `MCP_PUBLIC_BASE_URL`, `BUGASURA_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID`, `BUGASURA_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET` (see *Deploying the OAuth sign-in*) | ## ⚠️ Breaking changes in 2.0 If you're upgrading from 1.x, update your client configuration: | What changed | 1.x | 2.0 | |--------------|-----|-----| | Tool names | `create_issue`, `list_teams`, … | `bugasura_create_issue`, `bugasura_list_teams`, … (prefixed to coexist with other MCP servers) | | Default HTTP endpoint | `/sse` (SSE) | `/mcp` (streamable HTTP) | | List/find responses | `{status, project_list, …}` (upstream shape) | Standard pagination envelope `{status, total, count, offset, items, has_more, next_offset}` — legacy keys remain as extras for one release | 1.x clients pointed at `/sse` must migrate to `/mcp` — SSE has been removed. --- ## Features - 📋 **Test Case Management** - Create, update, delete, and search test cases - 💬 **Test Case Comments** - Add, update, delete, and list comments on test cases with pagination and filtering - 🐛 **Issue Tracking** - Report, manage, and delete bugs with rich context - 💬 **Issue Comments** - Add, update, delete, and list comments on issues with pagination and filtering - 📝 **Requirements Management** - Create, organize, and manage product requirements with folder structure - 📚 **Knowledge Base** - Upload, list, star, and delete documents in a project's knowledge base, with folders created on demand; import from a website, Coda, Jira, Confluence or Figma - 🏃 **Sprint Planning** - Create, update, delete, and manage agile sprints - 🏁 **Test Runs** - Create one-time or scheduled (recurring) runs, edit/rerun/delete them, pick environments and app builds, and add test cases — all by name or ID - 🧪 **Test Data** - Manage a project's test data environments (create, rename, duplicate, delete), their variables and the Globals scope, plus test data files (upload, read, download, delete), app builds and file categories — all by name or ID - 🤖 **Testpert Sprints** - Full AI-driven test enrichment flow: upload specs, answer requirement questions, edit the test plan, and generate test cases automatically - 👥 **Team Collaboration** - Assign work using names or emails (auto-resolves to user IDs) - 👤 **Team Member Management** - Add, update roles, and remove team members using team names or IDs - 🔍 **Smart Discovery** - Find projects and teams without memorizing IDs - 🤖 **Interactive Workflows** - Guided context selection for all operations --- ## Quick Start ### 1. Have a Bugasura account That's all the hosted server needs. On first use your AI tool opens the Bugasura sign-in page in your browser; approve once and you're connected. Tokens refresh automatically for 30 days. An API key is only needed for the local STDIO setup described under *Local Development*. ### 2. Install the MCP Server Add the server URL to your AI tool. No headers, no keys: the client discovers the OAuth sign-in from the server and walks you through it.
Claude Desktop Open Claude Desktop → Settings → Connectors → Add Custom Connector - Name: `Bugasura` - URL: `https://mcp.bugasura.io/mcp` Click **Connect**, sign in to Bugasura, and click **Allow** on the consent page.
VS Code [Install in VS Code](https://insiders.vscode.dev/redirect/mcp/install?name=bugasura&config=%7B%22type%22%3A%22http%22%2C%22url%22%3A%22https%3A//mcp.bugasura.io/mcp%22%7D), or add to your VS Code MCP config: ```json { "servers": { "bugasura": { "type": "http", "url": "https://mcp.bugasura.io/mcp" } } } ``` VS Code detects the OAuth sign-in and opens the browser the first time a tool is used. [VS Code MCP Documentation](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/copilot/chat/mcp-servers)
Claude Code ```bash claude mcp add --transport http bugasura https://mcp.bugasura.io/mcp ``` Then run `/mcp` inside Claude Code, choose **Bugasura → Authenticate**, and complete the sign-in in the browser. [Claude Code MCP Documentation](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code/mcp)

# GuardBee MCP

**🇬🇧 English** | [🇹🇷 Türkçe](TR.md) | [🇨🇳 中文](ZH.md) | [🇯🇵 日本語](JA.md) | [🇰🇷 한국어](KO.md) | [🇧🇷 Português](PT-BR.md) | [🇪🇸 Español](ES.md) | [🇩🇪 Deutsch](DE.md)

**Security for AI agents and MCP.** GuardBee puts a gateway between your agents and their tools and models that masks personal data and secrets, blocks prompt injection and toxic data flows, asks before risky calls and keeps a tamper-evident audit log, plus scanners that check your code and configs against the OWASP MCP Top 10. Open source (MIT), runs on your machine, no account needed.

The gateway and every server speak MCP **2026-07-28** and **2025-11-25** (MCP TypeScript SDK v2), so they work with clients and servers on either revision.

```bash
# Put your existing MCP servers behind the gateway (backs up your client config first)
npx -y @guardbee/mcp-security-proxy@^1 init --client claude-desktop   # or cursor, claude-code

# Check a codebase against the OWASP MCP Top 10
npx -y @guardbee/mcp-owasp-scan scan . --fail-on=high
```

<sub>Run it yourself: [`examples/demo`](examples/demo) (`npm install && npm start`).</sub>

## Which package should I use?

| You want to… | Install | How |
|---|---|---|
| Protect agents at runtime: mask personal data, block injection and toxic flows, approve risky calls, keep an audit log | [`@guardbee/mcp-security-proxy`](packages/security-proxy) | Put it in front of your MCP servers (`guardbee-proxy init` imports your client config) |
| Check a codebase against the OWASP MCP Top 10 in one pass, in CI | [`@guardbee/mcp-owasp-scan`](packages/owasp-scan) | `npx @guardbee/mcp-owasp-scan scan . --format=sarif --fail-on=high` |
| Give an agent many GuardBee checks from one MCP server | [`@guardbee/security-suite`](packages/security-suite) | `guardbee serve` (recommended set), `--tools=code,network` or `all` |
| Find leaked keys in files, git history or agent transcripts | [`@guardbee/mcp-secret-scanner`](packages/secret-scanner) | `npx @guardbee/mcp-secret-scanner scan . --history` |
| Audit the MCP servers configured on developer machines | [`@guardbee/mcp-config-auditor`](packages/mcp-config-auditor) | `npx @guardbee/mcp-config-auditor discover` |
| Let an agent query a database without seeing raw personal data | [`@guardbee/mcp-db-gateway`](packages/db-gateway) | Point it at your database with a policy |
| Use the detectors in your own code | [`@guardbee/guard-core`](packages/guard-core) | `import { maskPiiInText } from "@guardbee/guard-core"` |

Every other package is a single check (one OWASP risk, one protocol, one file type); each is in `security-suite` too. `npx @guardbee/security-suite list` shows them with what they check.

## Benchmarks

Detection is measured, not claimed: [`packages/pii-bench`](packages/pii-bench) is a reproducible benchmark for Turkish and international personal data, with bootstrap 95% intervals and the datasets in the repo.

| Benchmark | Result |
|---|---|
| Identifiers (TC Kimlik, IBAN, card, phone, e-mail, …), 400 documents + 160 clean | **F1 97.1**, recall 100%, false alarms on clean documents 8.1%, 0.04 ms per document |
| Person names with the optional NER model, same set | **F1 99.5** |
| Hand-written hard cases for names ([tr-names-challenge](packages/pii-bench/README.md#dataset-tr-names-challenge)) | **F1 97.1**, 0 false alarms |
| KVKK Art. 6 special categories with NER ([tr-special-challenge](packages/pii-bench/README.md#dataset-tr-special-challenge)) | **F1 97.5**, 0 false alarms |
| Bypass suite: 5 identifiers × 16 disguises (base64, hex, URL/HTML/`\u` escapes, other scripts' digits, separators) | **80 / 80 masked**, 0 of 16 look-alike strings changed |

The identifier detectors were tuned after reading this set's misses, so the challenge sets are the fairer measure; the [pii-bench README](packages/pii-bench/README.md) lists the limits. Any other detector can be run on the same data through its `System` interface.

## Examples

Ready-to-copy proxy policies (minimal, KVKK, coding agent, LLM gateway), client configs for Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor and VS Code, and CI templates for GitHub Actions and GitLab: [`examples/`](examples).

## Packages

| Package | npm | Description |
|---|---|---|
| [`packages/ai-code-scanner`](packages/ai-code-scanner) | `@guardbee/mcp-ai-code-scanner` | Scans a codebase for insecure LLM/AI integration patterns (client-exposed keys, unsafe output handling, excessive agency, PII→prompt, prompt injection) |
| [`packages/compliance-checker`](packages/compliance-checker) | `@guardbee/mcp-compliance-checker` | KVKK/GDPR/CCPA compliance checks |
| [`packages/dependency-auditor`](packages/dependency-auditor) | `@guardbee/mcp-dependency-auditor` | CVE scanning for npm/pip/cargo dependencies (OSV) |
| [`packages/dns-intelligence`](packages/dns-intelligence) | `@guardbee/mcp-dns-intelligence` | DNS record enumeration, misconfiguration and dangling-subdomain detection |
| [`packages/db-gateway`](packages/db-gateway) | `@guardbee/mcp-db-gateway` | KVKK/GDPR-compliant gateway between an LLM and a database (PII masking, RBAC, rate limiting, queryable audit log; Prisma/Postgres/MySQL/SQLite/MongoDB adapters; optional insert/update/delete support) |
| [`packages/mcp-server-auditor`](packages/mcp-server-auditor) | `@guardbee/mcp-server-auditor` | Scans other MCP servers' tool definitions for insecure patterns (excessive agency, shell/eval/SQL/SSRF sinks, loose schemas, hardcoded secrets, wildcard CORS) |
| [`packages/prompt-injection-scanner`](packages/prompt-injection-scanner) | `@guardbee/mcp-prompt-injection-scanner` | Scans RAG content/scraped pages for indirect prompt injection (instruction override, spoofed role/chat-template tokens, hidden text, "Dear AI" direct address, data-exfiltration instructions) |
| [`packages/llm-redteam`](packages/llm-redteam) | `@guardbee/mcp-llm-redteam` | Actively red-teams a live LLM endpoint/chatbot with canary-based jailbreak/extraction/obfuscation probes (OpenAI/Anthropi

# GuardBee MCP

**🇬🇧 English** | [🇹🇷 Türkçe](TR.md) | [🇨🇳 中文](ZH.md) | [🇯🇵 日本語](JA.md) | [🇰🇷 한국어](KO.md) | [🇧🇷 Português](PT-BR.md) | [🇪🇸 Español](ES.md) | [🇩🇪 Deutsch](DE.md)

**Security for AI agents and MCP.** GuardBee puts a gateway between your agents and their tools and models that masks personal data and secrets, blocks prompt injection and toxic data flows, asks before risky calls and keeps a tamper-evident audit log, plus scanners that check your code and configs against the OWASP MCP Top 10. Open source (MIT), runs on your machine, no account needed.

The gateway and every server speak MCP **2026-07-28** and **2025-11-25** (MCP TypeScript SDK v2), so they work with clients and servers on either revision.

```bash
# Put your existing MCP servers behind the gateway (backs up your client config first)
npx -y @guardbee/mcp-security-proxy@^1 init --client claude-desktop   # or cursor, claude-code

# Check a codebase against the OWASP MCP Top 10
npx -y @guardbee/mcp-owasp-scan scan . --fail-on=high
```

<sub>Run it yourself: [`examples/demo`](examples/demo) (`npm install && npm start`).</sub>

## Which package should I use?

| You want to… | Install | How |
|---|---|---|
| Protect agents at runtime: mask personal data, block injection and toxic flows, approve risky calls, keep an audit log | [`@guardbee/mcp-security-proxy`](packages/security-proxy) | Put it in front of your MCP servers (`guardbee-proxy init` imports your client config) |
| Check a codebase against the OWASP MCP Top 10 in one pass, in CI | [`@guardbee/mcp-owasp-scan`](packages/owasp-scan) | `npx @guardbee/mcp-owasp-scan scan . --format=sarif --fail-on=high` |
| Give an agent many GuardBee checks from one MCP server | [`@guardbee/security-suite`](packages/security-suite) | `guardbee serve` (recommended set), `--tools=code,network` or `all` |
| Find leaked keys in files, git history or agent transcripts | [`@guardbee/mcp-secret-scanner`](packages/secret-scanner) | `npx @guardbee/mcp-secret-scanner scan . --history` |
| Audit the MCP servers configured on developer machines | [`@guardbee/mcp-config-auditor`](packages/mcp-config-auditor) | `npx @guardbee/mcp-config-auditor discover` |
| Let an agent query a database without seeing raw personal data | [`@guardbee/mcp-db-gateway`](packages/db-gateway) | Point it at your database with a policy |
| Use the detectors in your own code | [`@guardbee/guard-core`](packages/guard-core) | `import { maskPiiInText } from "@guardbee/guard-core"` |

Every other package is a single check (one OWASP risk, one protocol, one file type); each is in `security-suite` too. `npx @guardbee/security-suite list` shows them with what they check.

## Benchmarks

Detection is measured, not claimed: [`packages/pii-bench`](packages/pii-bench) is a reproducible benchmark for Turkish and international personal data, with bootstrap 95% intervals and the datasets in the repo.

| Benchmark | Result |
|---|---|
| Identifiers (TC Kimlik, IBAN, card, phone, e-mail, …), 400 documents + 160 clean | **F1 97.1**, recall 100%, false alarms on clean documents 8.1%, 0.04 ms per document |
| Person names with the optional NER model, same set | **F1 99.5** |
| Hand-written hard cases for names ([tr-names-challenge](packages/pii-bench/README.md#dataset-tr-names-challenge)) | **F1 97.1**, 0 false alarms |
| KVKK Art. 6 special categories with NER ([tr-special-challenge](packages/pii-bench/README.md#dataset-tr-special-challenge)) | **F1 97.5**, 0 false alarms |
| Bypass suite: 5 identifiers × 16 disguises (base64, hex, URL/HTML/`\u` escapes, other scripts' digits, separators) | **80 / 80 masked**, 0 of 16 look-alike strings changed |

The identifier detectors were tuned after reading this set's misses, so the challenge sets are the fairer measure; the [pii-bench README](packages/pii-bench/README.md) lists the limits. Any other detector can be run on the same data through its `System` interface.

## Examples

Ready-to-copy proxy policies (minimal, KVKK, coding agent, LLM gateway), client configs for Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor and VS Code, and CI templates for GitHub Actions and GitLab: [`examples/`](examples).

## Packages

| Package | npm | Description |
|---|---|---|
| [`packages/ai-code-scanner`](packages/ai-code-scanner) | `@guardbee/mcp-ai-code-scanner` | Scans a codebase for insecure LLM/AI integration patterns (client-exposed keys, unsafe output handling, excessive agency, PII→prompt, prompt injection) |
| [`packages/compliance-checker`](packages/compliance-checker) | `@guardbee/mcp-compliance-checker` | KVKK/GDPR/CCPA compliance checks |
| [`packages/dependency-auditor`](packages/dependency-auditor) | `@guardbee/mcp-dependency-auditor` | CVE scanning for npm/pip/cargo dependencies (OSV) |
| [`packages/dns-intelligence`](packages/dns-intelligence) | `@guardbee/mcp-dns-intelligence` | DNS record enumeration, misconfiguration and dangling-subdomain detection |
| [`packages/db-gateway`](packages/db-gateway) | `@guardbee/mcp-db-gateway` | KVKK/GDPR-compliant gateway between an LLM and a database (PII masking, RBAC, rate limiting, queryable audit log; Prisma/Postgres/MySQL/SQLite/MongoDB adapters; optional insert/update/delete support) |
| [`packages/mcp-server-auditor`](packages/mcp-server-auditor) | `@guardbee/mcp-server-auditor` | Scans other MCP servers' tool definitions for insecure patterns (excessive agency, shell/eval/SQL/SSRF sinks, loose schemas, hardcoded secrets, wildcard CORS) |
| [`packages/prompt-injection-scanner`](packages/prompt-injection-scanner) | `@guardbee/mcp-prompt-injection-scanner` | Scans RAG content/scraped pages for indirect prompt injection (instruction override, spoofed role/chat-template tokens, hidden text, "Dear AI" direct address, data-exfiltration instructions) |
| [`packages/llm-redteam`](packages/llm-redteam) | `@guardbee/mcp-llm-redteam` | Actively red-teams a live LLM endpoint/chatbot with canary-based jailbreak/extraction/obfuscation probes (OpenAI/Anthropi

# bowmark skill

<sub>**LM Studio** — GitHub strips a raw `lmstudio:` link, so this one is a paste, not a button. Copy it into your browser's address bar:</sub>

```
lmstudio://add_mcp?name=bowmark&config=eyJ1cmwiOiJodHRwczovL2FwaS5ib3dtYXJrLmFpL21jcC9iYWRnZS1sbXN0dWRpbyJ9
```

The skill for [Bowmark](https://bowmark.ai) — the web as callable functions. The agent reads a typed function library, writes a short script against it, and Bowmark runs it on the live sites.

```sh
npx skills add bowmark-ai/skill
```

Works on any host that supports the `SKILL.md` standard — **Claude Code, Codex** (which adopted the standard natively), Cursor, GitHub Copilot, OpenCode, and others.

The skill calls Bowmark's MCP server — wire that up at [bowmark.ai/#install](https://bowmark.ai/#install) or via [Smithery](https://smithery.ai/servers/bowmark-ai/bowmark).

**Want both in one step?** On Claude Code and Codex, install the plugin instead — it bundles this skill *and* auto-wires the MCP:

```sh
# Claude Code
claude plugin marketplace add bowmark-ai/plugin && claude plugin install bowmark@bowmark-ai
# Codex
codex plugin marketplace add bowmark-ai/plugin   # then `codex /plugins` to install
```

## Tools

| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `get_library` | Read the typed function library for a task or a site. Read-only, touches no site, and an unrecognized query returns the index rather than an error. |
| `run` | Execute a short async JavaScript script against the live sites and return `{ ok, result, logs, error, ms }`. |
| `report` | Tell Bowmark what it could not do, or which run came back wrong. Recorded as feedback; retries nothing. |

**No MCP client?** The same two calls are plain HTTP — `GET https://api.bowmark.ai/v1/library?query=…` and `POST https://api.bowmark.ai/v1/run`, both taking `Authorization: Bearer $BOWMARK_API_KEY`. The reference is [bowmark.ai/docs/api](https://bowmark.ai/docs/api); worked examples are at [bowmark.ai/docs/scripting#no-install-at-all](https://bowmark.ai/docs/scripting#no-install-at-all).

## OpenAI Apps (ChatGPT plugin) variant

The [ChatGPT Apps](https://platform.openai.com/plugins) submission takes a skill as a **ZIP or folder**, and its needs differ slightly from the general skill: the plugin always ships the MCP alongside the skill, and ChatGPT exposes the tools under bare names. So there's a tailored variant, **generated from this same canonical skill** — never hand-maintained:

- **Folder:** [`openai/bowmark/`](./openai/bowmark) — a content mirror of `bowmark/SKILL.md` with the trailing "Your API key" section and everything after it dropped (ChatGPT signs in by OAuth and cannot send a key), tool names rewritten to bare `get_library` / `run`, Claude-only frontmatter/tool-name references trimmed, and the three secret tools (`list_secrets`, `request_secret`, `get_secret_link`) replaced by the dashboard — the plugin's MCP is the ChatGPT directory connector, which does not offer them. That step refuses to build if the canonical wording moves out from under it. `build-openai.mjs` is the authority on what it cuts; this line described sections that have never existed in `bowmark/SKILL.md`, and a newcomer went looking for one.
- **ZIP:** [`openai/bowmark-openai-skill.zip`](./openai/bowmark-openai-skill.zip) — the same folder zipped, ready to drop straight into the ChatGPT "Skills" uploader. A **committed artifact** (not built in CI: the release runner has no `zip` binary), so it rides the mirror to `bowmark-ai/skill` at a stable raw URL like any other file.

Both are **generated** by [`build-openai.mjs`](./build-openai.mjs). Edit `bowmark/SKILL.md`, then regenerate and commit — never edit the `openai/` copies directly (CI's `check:openai` fails a PR whose text mirror is stale):

```sh
pnpm -F @bowmark/skill sync:openai        # regenerate openai/bowmark/SKILL.md
pnpm -F @bowmark/skill build:openai-zip    # rebuild openai/bowmark-openai-skill.zip (commit it)
```

## License

[MIT](./LICENSE) © Bowmark AI

Getting started · Supported tools · Security & admin · Troubleshooting --- The **official Orangescrum MCP Server** is a cloud-based bridge between your Orangescrum workspace and compatible AI tools. Once connected, it lets those tools work with **projects, tasks, users, the epic, feature, and story hierarchy, sprints, timelogs, Test Case Management, versions and releases, Scaled Agile, risk management, resource management, attendance, leave, checklists, Knowledge Base (Wiki) pages, saved project context, and uploaded documents** in real time. Authentication uses **OAuth 2.1 with PKCE**, so every action runs as the signed-in user and respects their existing Orangescrum roles and permissions. With the Orangescrum MCP Server, you can: * **Summarize and search** projects, tasks, sprints, defects, releases, Wiki pages, and documents without switching tools. * **Create and update** tasks, stories, defects, test cases, timelogs, releases, and Knowledge Base pages from natural language. * **Plan and track** sprints, program increments, and release readiness with live data. * **Automate repetitive work**, like turning meeting notes into tasks or a spec into a backlog. Connect once, then describe what you want. There is no tab switching and no copy-pasting: your AI selects and runs the right actions. It's built for project managers, developers, QA teams, and delivery leads who work in AI assistants or IDEs and want to use Orangescrum data without constantly switching context. > [!IMPORTANT] > **The recommended endpoint is `https://mcp.orangescrum.com/mcp/partner`.** It uses OAuth 2.1, so you never paste an API key into a config file. Your client registers itself, opens a browser for you to sign in, and asks you to pick one workspace. readme.markdown:
# ZopDev MCP

Cloud cost, inventory and governance on AWS, Azure and GCP — **read-only by default, with
optional scoped writes.**

A hosted, remote Model Context Protocol server that gives an AI assistant grounded access to
your ZopDev organisation's cloud estate: what is running, what it costs, what is wasted, what is
scheduled, who owns it, and what shipped.

Point Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor or Codex at it and ask questions that previously took
six browser tabs and a spreadsheet — *which non-production databases ran all weekend*, *what is
our month-to-date Azure spend*, *show me every open recommendation over $500 a month we can
apply without stopping anything.*

One server covers both ZopDev products:

- **ZopNight** — cloud cost and FinOps: resource discovery, spend analysis, recommendations, budgets, and scheduled start/stop.
- **ZopDay** — build and deploy: projects, services, environments, deploys, rollbacks, databases, and cluster provisioning.

**Remote and hosted — there is nothing to install, build or run.**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Endpoint** | `https://api.zop.dev/mcp-server` |
| **Transport** | `streamable-http` (JSON-RPC 2.0 over HTTP POST) |
| **Auth** | OAuth 2.1 (recommended) or a personal access token |
| **Tools** | 353 — 193 read, 160 write |
| **Default access** | Read-only. Writes are opt-in per organisation and scoped per token |
| **Privacy policy** | https://zop.dev/legal/privacy-policy |
| **Terms of service** | https://zop.dev/legal/website-terms-of-service |

- **Learn more** — https://zop.dev/learn/mcp-server
- **Protocol reference** — https://zop.dev/developer-docs/integrations/mcp-server/overview
- **Claude setup guide** — https://zop.dev/learn/how-to/set-up-zopnight-mcp-for-claude

---

## Before you connect

**MCP is enabled per organisation and is off by default.** An admin (anyone with the
*Organisation Update* permission) turns it on in **Settings → Organisation → MCP Server**, and
chooses a [write access](#write-access) level. That is the one step you may need to ask someone
else for.

Once it is on, most clients will sign you in — there is nothing to copy by hand.

---

## Install

### OAuth — recommended, and no token to copy

Any client that can open a browser discovers the sign-in flow by itself. Add the URL and approve
the consent screen; the client handles registration, PKCE and token refresh.

**Claude Code**
```bash
claude mcp add zopdev https://api.zop.dev/mcp-server -t http
```

**Cursor / Claude Desktop / Codex**
```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "zopdev": {
      "url": "https://api.zop.dev/mcp-server"
    }
  }
}
```

**VS Code**
```json
{
  "servers": {
    "zopdev": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://api.zop.dev/mcp-server"
    }
  }
}
```

The `-t http` flag on Claude Code is required — it selects Streamable HTTP transport. Without
it, Claude Code treats the URL as a command to execute rather than a server to call.

On first use you are sent to a ZopDev consent screen listing the scopes requested (`mcp:read`,
`mcp:write`) and the exact write tools each admits. Approve, and you are connected. The client
then appears under **Connected Apps**, where you can revoke it at any time.

### Personal access token — for CI, scripts and non-browser clients

Create one under your profile → **[Developer Settings](https://zop.dev/zopnight/app/developer)
→ Create Token**, ticking the write capabilities it should carry. It is shown once and starts
`zn_pat_`.

```bash
claude mcp add zopdev https://api.zop.dev/mcp-server -t http \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN"
```

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "zopdev": {
      "url": "https://api.zop.dev/mcp-server",
      "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" }
    }
  }
}
```

A PAT carries **your** identity — it can do what you can do, and no more. Every call resolves
your live role, so a role change or removal takes effect on the next request with no re-mint.

### Cline

Open the **MCP Servers** icon → **Remote Servers** tab, enter the URL and pick **Streamable
HTTP**. If you prefer editing the config directly, note that Cline wants an explicit `type`, and
spells it in camelCase:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "zopdev": {
      "type": "streamableHttp",
      "url": "https://api.zop.dev/mcp-server",
      "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" }
    }
  }
}
```

### Continue

Continue is configured in YAML rather than JSON, and the auth header goes under
`requestOptions`:

```yaml
mcpServers:
  - name: zopdev
    type: streamable-http
    url: https://api.zop.dev/mcp-server
    requestOptions:
      headers:
        Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN
```

Omit `requestOptions` if you would rather sign in through OAuth.

### Other clients

Any MCP client supporting a remote server and bearer-token auth works with the same URL.
Per-client guides: [ZopNight](https://zop.dev/docs/zopnight/integrations/mcp) ·
[ZopDay](https://zop.dev/docs/zopday/integrations/mcp)

---

## Verify the connection

Ask your assistant:

```
List my organisations
```

This calls `list_organisations` — the only tool that takes no arguments, which makes it the
cleanest test of the connection itself. Every other tool needs an `org_id` that this one
returns.

Then ask **"What are my ZopDev permissions?"** to see exactly what your session can reach.

---

## Example prompts

Once connected, these work against your own estate. Each one is read-only — nothing below
changes a resource:

- Which non-production databases ran all weekend?
- What is our month-to-date Azure spend, broken down by service?
- Show me every open recommendation over $500 a month we can apply without stopping anything.
- Which resources violate our tagging policy?

---

## What it exposes

Reads cover your estate end to end:

- **Inventory** — resources and parent/child topology, filters, discovery status, per-account permission verdicts, live Kubernetes objects, manifests, pod logs, blast-radius analysis
- **Cost** — overview,

name: SuprSend
description: Hosted SuprSend MCP server: users, lists, workflows, templates, and notification data.

readme.markdown:
# SuprSend MCP Server

The official hosted **Model Context Protocol (MCP)** server for [SuprSend](https://www.suprsend.com). Connect an AI agent — Claude, ChatGPT, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, or any MCP client — to your SuprSend account and operate your notification stack in natural language.

- **Endpoint:** `https://mcp.suprsend.com/mcp`
- **Transport:** Streamable HTTP (remote MCP server — nothing to install or host)
- **Auth:** OAuth 2.1 — you sign in with your SuprSend account

> This repository is the public description of the hosted server, for the MCP registries and Copilot surfaces. The server runs at the endpoint above.

## What it does

SuprSend is a notification infrastructure platform. The MCP server lets an agent operate your SuprSend workspaces:

- **Users & preferences** — look up users, their channels, subscriptions, and notification preferences, and update them.
- **Lists & objects** — manage subscriber lists and objects (teams, accounts) and their members.
- **Workflows** — read, draft, and publish notification workflows.
- **Templates** — read, edit, validate, and publish multi-channel templates (email, SMS, push, Inbox, WhatsApp, Slack, Teams).
- **Delivery data** — query delivery logs, workflow runs, and analytics with read-only SQL to answer questions like "why did user X not get Y?".
- **Events, schemas, translations, vendors, tenants, and broadcasts** — and more.

It also ships **skills** (packaged guidance for authoring workflows, templates, and SQL) and interactive **MCP Apps** (a chart view for query results and a message-content preview).

## Connect it

Add the remote MCP server URL in your client and sign in when prompted:

- **Claude (web, desktop, or Code):** add a custom connector with the URL `https://mcp.suprsend.com/mcp`.
- **ChatGPT and other MCP clients:** add `https://mcp.suprsend.com/mcp` as a remote (Streamable HTTP) MCP server.
- **Scope to one workspace:** connect to `https://mcp.suprsend.com/mcp/<workspace>` to pin a single workspace, or use `.../mcp` for all workspaces you can access.

You authenticate with your SuprSend login, and the agent gets only the access your role allows (admins get write tools; members get reads).

## Learn more

- SuprSend: https://www.suprsend.com
- Documentation: https://docs.suprsend.com

name: Australian Economic Data (ABS, RBA & APRA)
description: Australian economic data from the ABS, RBA, and APRA: CPI, GDP, cash rate, labour, and more.

readme.markdown:
ausecon is a Model Context Protocol server that gives an AI assistant structured access to Australia’s official economic and financial data, straight from the ABS, RBA, and APRA. Open source, free, and no API key. Every series comes back fresh & fully source-traceable, and all three sources share one response shape. Documentation  ·  Getting started  ·  Tool reference  ·  Changelog --- ## Why this exists Australian economic data is authoritative but awkward to reach. It sits behind three different portals with three different formats, and each one expects you to already know its identifiers. ausecon puts that data in front of an AI assistant with nothing to sign up for and no key to manage. Every series is fetched from the source, cached for up to an hour, stamped with when it was actually retrieved, and returned in the same `metadata · series · observations` shape whether it came from the ABS, the RBA, or APRA. Ask for "the cash rate" or "quarterly real GDP growth" and the assistant works out the right call. 14read-only tools 83economic concepts 16derived indicators 8prompt templates 3data sources ## What you get Fresh & source-traceable Every value is fetched from the source, cached for up to an hour, and stamped with its provenance (retrieved_at, source, server_version). If a source is down after the cache expires, the old copy is returned flagged stale and never served silently. Three sources, one shape ABS, RBA and APRA all return the same metadata · series · observations structure, so anything written against one source works for the other two. Transparent derived series Formula-based indicators like real_cash_rate, with the formula and its input series returned alongside the numbers. Source-native control Drop down to get_abs_data, get_rba_table or get_apra_data when you need a specific dataflow, table, or series ID. Convenience tools Latest observations, top movers, and the release calendar, each in a single call. Works with your client Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, VS Code, Codex or Smithery. stdio locally, Streamable HTTP when hosted. ## Data sources | Source | Coverage | | :----- | :------- | | **ABS**  ·  Australian Bureau of Statistics | National accounts, prices, labour force, population | | **RBA**  ·  Reserve Bank of Australia | Cash rate, monetary & financial aggregates, exchange rates | | **APRA**  ·  Aust. readme.markdown:
memo Local knowledge for your AI agents. Your notes, documents, mail and messages in one local store — linked to people, tagged, and searchable with a reference to every source. Docs · Examples · WireCat `memo` is a command-line tool. It imports a folder of notes such as an Obsidian vault, the documents in it, and your mail; it reads the messages that [tg-cli](https://github.com/WireCatLabs/tg-cli) and [max-cli](https://github.com/WireCatLabs/max-cli) keep. Then you, or your AI agent, ask: what do I know about this person, where did we discuss this, what did I promise. Every answer points back to its source. **Example** — search two invented notes in a notes folder: ```text $ memo search notes budget Friday Searched by words only: e5-small is not downloaded — install it with a WireCat CLI that has `models download` (tg, max or wa); they share the model folder Projects/Harbour budget.md Review the Harbour budget by Friday. people/Alice Example.md Asked for the revised budget by Friday. ``` Each hit names its file and shows a matching excerpt. The diagnostic line goes to stderr: the local model is missing, so this search used words only. `--json` returns structured results for an agent or script. ## Quick start You need Node.js 22.16+ or 24+ (not 23). memo is tested on Linux; macOS and Windows are not tested yet. ```sh npm install -g @wirecat/cli-memo memo skill install --for all # puts memo's skill where your agents read it memo folders add /path/to/notes # your notes folder; Obsidian format by default memo sync --only notes # reads the notes, their links and tags; run again after edits memo search notes "budget" ``` A global install does not install the agent skill; run `memo skill install --for all` above. npm 11.17 and later warn about install scripts not covered by `allowScripts`; with npm 11 the scripts still run. npm 12 blocks them instead. Run the `npm install -g --allow-scripts=…` command npm prints under the warning; it allows only the packages it names, once. On Windows, open a new terminal if `memo` is not found. That is all notes need. Then add more context: - **Messages:** install [tg-cli](https://github.com/WireCatLabs/tg-cli) or [max-cli](https://github.com/WireCatLabs/max-cli); memo reads the same local store. - **Search by meaning:** needs a local model of about 135 MB, downloaded once with: `memo models download e5-small`. Without it, memo searches by words. - **Mail:** set up [Himalaya](https://github.com/pimalaya/himalaya), run `memo mail add
`, then `memo sync --only mail`. - **Stay current:** `memo jobs start` runs `memo sync` every five minutes (Linux, systemd). - **Your agent:** `memo skill install --for all` puts memo's skill where Claude Code, Codex and Gemini CLI read it; `memo skill show` prints it. Or ask your agent: "Help me install memo with `npm install -g @wirecat/cli-memo` and `memo skill install --for all`, read `memo --help`, then help me connect a notes folder I choose." More: [installation](https://github.com/WireCatLabs/cli-memo/blob/main/docs/installation.md) · [install memo on wirecat.dev](https://wirecat.dev/en/docs/memo/installation) ## What can you do? **"What do I need to know about Alice before the call?"** ```sh memo context telegram:"Alice Example" --json ``` Every identity linked to her, the last message each way, chats in common, linked mail, the notes about her and the open tasks — each with a link to its source. **"Where did we discuss the Harbour budget?"** ```sh memo search all 'harbour budget' --json ``` Messages, imported mail and notes, ranked together. When you know the kind, `search notes`, `search mail` and `search messages` read every field. **"What did I promise people this week?"** ```sh memo answers create 'What did I promise this week?' 'promised OR "by Friday"' --all --json ``` An evidence bundle for your agent: the matching sources with their references, what was searched, and the instruction to cite them. Your agent writes the answer; memo calls a model only when you ask it to. More: [search](https://github.com/WireCatLabs/cli-memo/blob/main/docs/search.md) · [ask for the context you need](https://wirecat.dev/en/docs/memo/people#everything-about-a-person) ## Built for AI agents - **Any agent with a terminal** — Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and others run `memo` commands; `--json` gives them structured output. - **Evidence, not guesses** — `memo answers create` hands over sources with references, and says what it could not search. - **MCP** — `memo mcp serve` lets MCP apps such as Claude Desktop or Cursor read your messages, mail and notes, and propose memories, directly recorded facts and outbound actions. Project proposals can also be decided by the agent when allowed; you can require owner decisions instead. Apps on the web or phone use [authenticated HTTP MCP](docs/remote.md) through your HTTPS tunnel, with the same saved permissions. More: [connect your AI agent](https://wirecat.dev/en/docs/agents) · [memories and facts](https://github.com/WireCatLabs/cli-memo/blob/main/docs/memories.md) · [the MCP server](https://github.com/WireCatLabs/cli-memo/blob/main/docs/mcp.md) ## Why memo? 1. **Local first.** Everything lives in a local store; search by meaning uses a local model. 2. **Every answer has a source.** Hits carry a reference you or your agent can open: a note, a file page, an email, a message. 3. **Links, not guesses.** Notes link to people and records; identities are never merged because a name matches. 4. **Imports leave your sources untouched.** Separate [Gmail cleanup commands](docs/mail.md#clean-up-gmail) move selected mail to Trash or restore it only with `--yes`. Tags and your own notes live in the store. 5. **Review and delegation are recorded.** Memories and outbound actions an agent suggests wait for your confirmation. readme.markdown:
# zoom-cli

**Zoom meetings and transcripts for your AI agent.** Know the context before the call. Remember the
commitments after it.

`zm` keeps your Zoom meetings, transcripts and AI summaries in a local database and gives them to
Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI or any MCP client. Ask what you discussed with someone last time, or
what you promised in yesterday's call, and get the answer with a reference to the exact passage.

[Documentation][docs/index.md] ·
[Commands][docs/commands.md] ·
[WireCat](https://wirecat.dev)

**Example** — invented people, illustrative output:

> **You:** I have a call with Bob Sample at three. What did we agree last time, and what do I owe him?

```sh
zm personal remote-meetings list --json                      # your upcoming meetings
zm personal meetings people "Bob Sample" --json              # him among past participants
zm personal search meetings "quote" --since-time 2026-09-01 --json
zm personal meetings passage meeting:1/42/57/118 --format markdown  # the line and its context
```

> **Agent:** You last spoke on 2 October in "Pricing review". You promised Bob a revised quote by
> Friday (`meeting:1/42/57/118`), and he asked whether the annual plan includes onboarding
> (`meeting:1/42/57/131`). I found no later update in the stored meetings I searched; missing
> history may change that.

## Quick start

You need Node 22.16+ (22.x) or 24+, a system keyring and **a configured user-managed Zoom app**. Reuse one you already created or one your team
has made available to your user; otherwise [create your own][docs/zoom-app.md]. Use its Public
Client ID, not its regular Client ID or secret. The [installation guide][docs/installation.md]
walks through app settings, browser approval and callback completion.

```sh
npm install -g @wirecat/zoom-cli
zm config set zoom.client_id <public-client-id>
zm personal session start                 # "personal" is the profile; approve in your browser
zm personal meetings sync --lookback-days 7
zm personal meetings list
```

Check Zoom's transcript generation and retention settings first: the API reads available hosted
meeting text, and permission does not create a transcript. For an attended meeting, obtain a VTT
file from the host or download one if allowed, then run `zm personal meetings import <folder>`. Full guide:
[installation][docs/installation.md].

More: [installation][docs/installation.md] · [your Zoom app][docs/zoom-app.md] ·
[Zoom on wirecat.dev][wirecat/en/docs/zoom]

## What you can do

**Prepare for a call.** *"I meet Bob Sample tomorrow. What did we talk about last time?"*
`meetings scheduled` finds candidate series; `meetings prepare <series-id>` checks the selected
series’ next occurrence and gathers cited context. `meetings people`, `search meetings` (word
search that also matches English, Spanish and Russian word forms) and `meetings context person:<id>`
bring back past meetings with the same people. Inventory date hints alone do not prove the next call.
Participant discovery accepts `--limit`, `--scan-limit`, `--max-read-bytes` and `--cursor`;
follow `item.page.next_cursor` even after an empty scan page. It returns observed `identity_id` candidates,
never inferred person links. Stored meeting lists accept metadata queries, for example
`zm personal meetings list 'started_at:[2026-09-01 TO 2026-10-01]' --json`.

**Find the project behind a call.** *"Which of my saved projects might this meeting concern?"*
`meetings projects scan <ref>` compares one bounded page of local meeting evidence with existing
project names, keys and aliases. It returns cited suggestions and ambiguity for review, saving no
project link. The agent can check proposed labels against Memo's existing vocabulary too.

**Follow up after it.** *"What did I promise in today's call?"* The agent reads
`meetings transcript` and `meetings summary`, cites passages with `meetings evidence`, and
`meetings task-proposal --type promise` previews a follow-up task tied to that passage.

**Keep the whole history.** *"Back up every recording since January."*
`recordings download --since-time 2026-01-01 --until-time 2026-10-10 --output-dir ./zoom-archive --jsonl` downloads
video, audio, transcripts and chat with SHA-256 manifests; `recordings schedule` runs it daily.

More: [the local archive][docs/archive.md] · [search and evidence][docs/search.md] ·
[Zoom on wirecat.dev][wirecat/en/docs/zoom]

## Built for AI agents

- **Command line + skill.** `zm skill install` adds the packaged guide for Claude Code, Codex and
  Gemini CLI. Every command speaks `--json` or `--jsonl`, and `zm commands --json` describes them all.
- **MCP.** `zm personal mcp serve` serves zm's commands to Claude Desktop, Cursor and other MCP clients, as
  far as the profile's permissions allow; `zm mcp serve --profiles all` serves every profile from one server.
  [Connecting a client][docs/mcp.md].

Your agent. Your meetings. Your rules.

More: [MCP and skills][docs/mcp.md] · [connect your AI agent][wirecat/en/docs/agents]

## Why zm

- **Context across meetings.** Search available hosted meetings and imported transcripts in the shared
  store. Read archived transcripts separately or import them before searching them together.
- **Local-first.** Meetings live in a SQLite database on your machine. Archived transcripts can be read
  and searched offline, without login.
- **Every answer has a source.** References such as `meeting:1/42/57/118` point to one passage of one
  transcript revision, and corrected transcripts keep their history.
- **Made for agents.** JSON output, bounded reads with explicit completeness, a skill and an MCP server.
- **Safe by default.** Your own Zoom app, tokens only in the keyring, permissions per profile, and every
  change to Zoom asks first at the terminal. Over MCP there is no terminal, so `ask` runs without a question;
  use `deny` or `readonly` to stop a change.

More: [security][docs/security.md] · [Zoom on wirecat.dev][wirecat/en/docs/zoom]

readme.markdown:
# tg — Telegram CLI for AI agents

  Your whole Telegram account in the terminal, searchable on your computer, and ready for Claude Code,
  Codex, Cursor or any agent — within limits you set.

  Docs ·
  Examples ·
  WireCat

  
  
  
  
  
  

An example conversation (invented people, illustrative output):

```text
You:    Use tg CLI. What did I promise anyone in the last three days?
Agent:  (runs tg personal review 'date>3d': 12 chats)
        I owe
        · Alice Example — the invoice by Friday. "Alice Example", 24.09
        Waiting on others
        · Bob Sample — the mock-up by 25.09. Not in "Design" yet
You:    Remind Bob about the mock-up.
Agent:  Draft: "Hi Bob, how is the mock-up going?" Send it?
You:    Yes.
```

## Quick start

```sh
npm install -g @wirecat/tg-cli    # or: bun add -g @wirecat/tg-cli; pnpm: see docs/installation.md
tg skill install --for all        # the agent skill, for Claude Code, Codex and Gemini CLI
tg personal setup                 # app registration and login
tg personal inbox                 # other people's unread messages, in every chat; nothing is marked read
```

A global install does not install the agent skill: `tg personal setup` offers it, or run `tg skill install --for all`. npm may warn that install scripts are blocked or "not yet covered by allowScripts" (`@wirecat/tg-cli`,
`better-sqlite3`); that is harmless, and you need not allow them — [why](https://github.com/WireCatLabs/tg-cli/blob/main/docs/installation.md#install).
On Windows, if `tg` is not found, open a new terminal, or use the PowerShell installer in
[the installation guide](https://github.com/WireCatLabs/tg-cli/blob/main/docs/installation.md#windows-one-install-command).

Allow about five minutes. `tg personal setup` registers your own Telegram app at
[my.telegram.org](https://my.telegram.org/apps), logs in by QR code, checks your first chats and installs
the agent skill. Downloading older history is a separate step.

It needs **Node 22.19+ or 24+**, or **Bun**, on macOS, Linux or Windows. Try it without installing:
`npx @wirecat/tg-cli --help`.

More: [installation guide](https://github.com/WireCatLabs/tg-cli/blob/main/docs/installation.md) · [on wirecat.dev](https://wirecat.dev/en/docs/tg/installation)

## What can you do?

**Catch up.** *"Use tg CLI. What came in since this morning, and who is waiting for my answer?"*

```sh
tg personal inbox
tg personal review 'date>1d'
```

**Find anything.** *"Use tg CLI. When did we agree on the venue with Alice?"* — an answer with the date
and the message itself.

```sh
tg personal search all "venue"                # messages and notes on this computer, and Telegram's own search
```

By default the words also go to Telegram's server search; add `--offline` to keep the query on this computer.

**Keep your promises.** *"Use tg CLI. What did I promise, and what am I still waiting on?"* `tg personal review`
hands over everything said since the last review in one call, your own messages too.

```sh
tg personal review --new                      # what changed since the last review --new
```

**Run your groups.** *"Use tg CLI. Which questions in Hiking has nobody answered?"*

```sh
tg personal review chat:Hiking --unanswered
tg personal chats events "Hiking" "time>=7d"  # who joined, left, was added or removed
```

More: [recipes, with a schedule and limits for each](https://github.com/WireCatLabs/tg-cli/blob/main/docs/recipes.md) · [on wirecat.dev](https://wirecat.dev/en/docs/tg/recipes)

## Built for AI agents

Your agent. Your Telegram. Your rules.

- **Agents with a terminal** (for example Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI) run `tg` commands
  themselves. The bundled [skill](https://github.com/WireCatLabs/tg-cli/blob/main/skills/tg-cli/SKILL.md)
  tells them how: `tg personal setup --agent …` or `tg skill install` puts it in place, and `tg skill show`
  prints it before login.
- **Apps without a terminal** (for example Claude Desktop, Cursor and other MCP clients) connect to
  `tg personal mcp serve`. It comes with ready prompts: `/catch-up`, `/review`, `/reply`, `/find`, `/open-tasks` and `/link-conversations`.

```sh
tg personal mcp add claude-code  # or: tg personal mcp add codex
tg personal mcp config      # the entry for Claude Desktop, Cursor and others
```

The profile can send by default, so `mcp add` stops first. Check the profile's permissions, then run
it again with `--allow-writes`.

More: [the MCP server](https://github.com/WireCatLabs/tg-cli/blob/main/docs/mcp.md) · [on wirecat.dev](https://wirecat.dev/en/docs/tg/mcp)

## Why tg?

- **Your whole account, not only bots.** Every chat, group, channel and contact, with its history —
  `tg` is one more of your devices.
- **Local-first search.** Everything read is kept on your computer. Search reads that copy and, by default,
  asks Telegram's own search too; `--offline` keeps the query on your computer.
- **Made for agents.** One operation per call, the same JSON shape every time with `--json`, a fixed
  exit code for each kind of failure, an MCP server and a skill.
- **Safe by default.** Reading marks nothing read. A profile decides which actions an agent may take,
  which chats it may send to, and how many messages an hour (30 by default). When a send's outcome is
  unknown, `tg` says so and gives a repeat command that Telegram does not deliver twice.
- **The full Bot API too.** All 185 methods, next to the convenient bot commands.

More: [compared with other tools](https://github.com/WireCatLabs/tg-cli/blob/main/docs/compare.md) · [on wirecat.dev](https://wirecat.dev/en/docs/tg/compare)

## Your account

`tg` works in your name, as one more of your devices. It is not a bot: it talks to Telegram over
MTProto, Telegram's own API for client apps, with an app you register yourself. It sees your chats,
their history, groups, channels and contacts.

tg personal messages list "Book club" --limit 20
tg personal messages send "Book club" "Call at 3?" -

readme.markdown:
# desktop-touch-mcp

[日本語](README.ja.md)

> **Computer-use MCP server for Windows.** Lets Claude, Cursor, or any MCP client see and operate your Windows 10/11 desktop — screenshots, UI Automation, Chrome CDP, keyboard / mouse, terminal — with **semantic discover-then-act targeting** that avoids pixel-coordinate guessing, and **per-action perception guards** that catch wrong-window typing before it happens.

```bash
npx -y @harusame64/desktop-touch-mcp
```

32 tools, native Rust engine (UIA in 2 ms), zero-config PowerShell fallback, full CJK support, MIT licensed. Add the snippet above to your Claude / Cursor / VS Code Copilot config and Claude can drive Notepad, Excel, Chrome, Windows Terminal, and any other app on your machine.

> **Why this over pixel-clicking?** Two ideas run through every tool: **discover-then-act** — `desktop_discover` returns interactive entities with short-lived leases instead of raw coordinates, so `desktop_act` operates on *what* you mean, not *where* it was — and **per-action perception guards** that verify the target window's identity and bounds before input lands, catching wrong-window typing and stale-coordinate clicks before they happen.
>
> **2.1** reads UI Automation by element count instead of depth: Chrome, Edge and VS Code pages, Explorer and Settings values, and Word's body are read and can be acted on, and what UIA still cannot see falls back to OCR and Set-of-Marks as before. `desktop_act` also types into Word's body, and into Windows Terminal after asking the user. **2.0** refuses an action that cannot be done, with a reason, instead of reporting it done, and an action aimed by `hwnd` reaches that window only. See the [CHANGELOG](CHANGELOG.md).

---

## Features

- **🔁 Every act reports what it did** — `desktop_act` answers with what changed: elements that appeared or disappeared, a modal, a focus move, the screen's repaint (`observation`), and with `narrate:"rich"` the values and names that changed. The agent reads the result of its click from the reply instead of taking another screenshot. On UIA-blind targets it can also attach a PNG of just the region that changed (`roiCapture`; on by default for a visible change, `returnCapture:"never"` to suppress, `"always"` to force).
- **🛑 An act that cannot be done is refused, not reported as done** — input that would not reach the field, a window blocked by a dialog, a closed window, a window on another virtual desktop: nothing is sent, and the reply names the reason and what to do next. An act aimed by `hwnd` never lands in another window with the same title.
- **🌐 Reads deep windows (2.1)** — The UI Automation read goes to depth 64 and 500 elements. Chrome, Edge and VS Code pages, which 2.0 called blind, Explorer and Settings values it left out, and Word's body are read and can be acted on (a Chrome page: 6 elements in 387 ms → 45 in 186 ms).
- **🎯 Set-of-Marks (SoM) visual fallback** — Games, RDP sessions and apps with no accessibility tree still return clickable elements: when UIA is blind, `desktop_discover` and `screenshot(detail="text")` switch to a Hybrid Non-CDP pipeline — Rust-powered grayscale + bilinear upscale → Windows OCR → clustering → red bounding boxes with numbered badges (`[1]`, `[2]`…). Two representations come back: a PNG for spatial orientation and an `elements[]` list with `clickAt` coords — no CDP required.
- **⌨️ Types where background input does not reach** — Windows Terminal, after asking the user each time (needs an MCP client with elicitation, over stdio), and Word's body, at Word's caret whether it is in front or behind.
- **🔐 Key Locker — the terminal autofills your SSH / sudo passwords** — Save a credential once into the locker's own secure dialog (stored encrypted on your machine with Windows DPAPI; never shown to the assistant), then run `ssh` / `sudo` in a console opened by `key_locker(action='launch_console')` — the password is filled in automatically when the hidden prompt appears, with a per-fill confirmation prompt by default. See [Key Locker](docs/guide.md#key-locker-terminal-credential-autofill).
- **⚡ Rust native core** — The UIA bridge and image diffing are a Rust native addon (`napi-rs` + `windows-rs`): UIA is called over COM from a dedicated thread instead of spawning PowerShell, and image diffs use SSE2 SIMD. Without the addon, every function falls back to PowerShell transparently. The npm launcher fetches only the GitHub Release matching its version and verifies the Windows runtime zip before extracting it.
- **LLM-native design** — Built around how LLMs think, not how humans click. `run_macro` batches multiple operations into a single API call; `diffMode` sends only the windows that changed since the last frame. Minimal tokens, minimal round-trips.
- **Reactive Perception Graph** — Register a `lensId` for a window or browser tab, pass it to action tools, and get guard-checked `post.perception` feedback after each action. It reduces repeated `screenshot` / `desktop_state` calls and prevents wrong-window typing or stale-coordinate clicks.
- **Full CJK support** — Uses Win32 `GetWindowTextW` for window titles, avoiding nut-js garbling. IME bypass input supported for Japanese/Chinese/Korean environments.
- **3-tier token reduction** — `detail="image"` (~443 tok) / `detail="text"` (~100–300 tok) / `diffMode=true` (~160 tok). Send pixels only when you actually need to see them.
- **1:1 coordinate mode** — `dotByDot=true` captures at native resolution (WebP). Image pixel = screen coordinate — no scale math needed. With `origin`+`scale` passed to `mouse_click`, the server converts coords for you — eliminating off-by-one / scale bugs.
- **Browser capture data reduction** — `grayscale=true` (~50% size), `dotByDotMaxDimension=1280` (auto-scaled with coord preservation), and `windowTitle + region` sub-crops help exclude browser chrome and other irrelevant pixels. Typical reduction for heavy captures: 50–70%.
- **Chromium smart fallback** — `detail="text"` on Chro
