# Analytics Legends — SAP AI & Analytics MCP Server A **read-only** [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server over a curated corpus of the **SAP AI & analytics services market**: who delivers SAP Business AI and Joule, Business Data Cloud, SAP Datasphere, SAP Analytics Cloud and BW/4HANA work, what the contract market looks like, what the day rates are, what the vocabulary means, and what has just happened. It exists so that an assistant answering an SAP analytics question can **cite a record instead of guessing**. Every row carries a `citation_url` on analyticslegends.ai, and every response carries the size of the population it was drawn from. **Nothing to install.** The server is hosted: ``` https://analyticslegends.ai/mcp streamable-http ``` The public tools need no credential. Looking for an MCP server that connects to your **own** SAP system (BTP, CAP, UI5, Fiori, ABAP, Datasphere…)? This one serves market data, not your tenant — the [catalogue of SAP MCP servers](https://analyticslegends.ai/guides/sap-mcp-servers/) lists the official SAP, AWS and community servers, verified on their own pages. --- ## Connect
Claude Code ```bash claude mcp add --transport http analytics-legends https://analyticslegends.ai/mcp # with a subscriber key, to open the eight gated tools: claude mcp add --transport http analytics-legends https://analyticslegends.ai/mcp \ --header "Authorization: Bearer alk_…" ```
Claude web, Desktop and mobile (custom connector) Add a custom connector pointing at `https://analyticslegends.ai/mcp`. The public tranche answers immediately, with no credential. To open the paid tranche, use the connector's **request-header authentication** and set `Authorization` to `Bearer alk_…`. The credential is entered once, by whoever adds the connector, and is shared by that workspace — one key, one daily quota. There is no OAuth consent flow to walk: this server's unit of access is a personal API key minted on an analyticslegends.ai account, not a delegated identity.
Claude Desktop / any client reading a JSON config ```json { "mcpServers": { "analytics-legends": { "type": "streamable-http", "url": "https://analyticslegends.ai/mcp" } } } ```
With a subscriber key (opens the eight gated tools) ```json { "mcpServers": { "analytics-legends": { "type": "streamable-http", "url": "https://analyticslegends.ai/mcp", "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer alk_…" } } } } ```
The manifest is served at [`/.well-known/mcp.json`](https://analyticslegends.ai/.well-known/mcp.json) and mirrored in this repository as [`mcp.json`](./mcp.json). `tools/list` is the authority for the surface — this README is a copy, and a copy can drift. --- ## The 22 tools **Fourteen are public and unauthenticated.** Eight need a subscriber key; they are **listed and refuse by name**, never hidden — an agent can see what it is missing. Three open at Consultant, five at Legend, and the MCP Pass opens all eight. | Tool | Answers | |---|---| | `search_firms` | Which SAP analytics providers match a country, kind, free text | | `count_firms_by` | A counting question in one call, instead of a page of rows | | `get_firm` | One organisation from the published directory | | `list_firm_kinds` | The directory's breakdown by organisation kind, with live counts | | `find_opportunities` | The live contract and permanent-role radar | | `search_news` | The curated SAP analytics news corpus | | `search_concepts` | The concept encyclopaedia — the vocabulary of the stack | | `get_concept` | One concept: title, category, level, tags, editor's summary | | `list_studies` | The deep-research study editions and their metadata | | `get_day_rate_benchmark` | The public day-rate aggregate by country, stack, seniority | | `list_sap_modules` | The canonical SAP module/product taxonomy | | `list_freelance_platforms` | The CV/profile platforms a consultant can sign up on | | `find_academy_modules` | The Academy training catalogue, searchable by module | | `query_knowledge_graph` | A traversal of the learning knowledge graph | | 🔒 `get_concept_card` | The full encyclopaedia card — body, key points, cheat sheet | | 🔒 `get_study` | One study **body** | | 🔒 `get_academy_module` | One Academy module, in full | | 🔒 `find_sap_clients` | The SAP end-customer corpus — who *runs* SAP | | 🔒 `get_sap_client_profile` | One end-customer's SAP footprint and analytics estate | | 🔒 `get_firm_intel` | A firm's practice size, partner level, delivery flags | | 🔒 `get_expansion_brief` | Before opening in another region: providers, SAP end-customers and openings there, and the brand families bridging your home region to it | | 🔒 `find_partner_candidates` | The local providers of a target country or region to partner with, subcontract to, or acquire | Every tool is annotated `readOnlyHint: true`. The server writes nothing, anywhere. --- ## Two rules it holds itself to **A count is read at query time, and it comes with its population.** Responses carry `_meta.match_count` (what your filters matched) and `_meta.tranche_total_row_count` (the whole tranche). Quote those rather than any number written in a description — including the ones in this file. **A citation says what it is.** Every item carries `citation_url` **and** `citation_scope`. `record` means the URL is that item's own page; `section_hub` means this platform publishes no page for that item and the URL is the section index — say so, or cite the section, but do not present a hub URL as the item's page. News items also carry `source_url` for the upstream publisher: cite both. --- ## What is deliberately **not** served, at any tier - **People.** Individual professionals are held as initials only. readme.markdown:
# egovframe-scaffold-mcp

**English summary: [README.en.md](README.en.md)**

전자정부 표준프레임워크(eGovFrame) 프로젝트의 **생성 → 조립 → 전환 → 납품 점검 → 배포**를 AI 도구 안에서, 그리고 빌드 서버의 명령 한 줄로 처리하는 [MCP(Model Context Protocol)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) 서버입니다. Claude Desktop·Claude Code·Cursor·VS Code(Copilot) 등 MCP 를 지원하는 AI 도구에 붙이면 대화로 쓰고, AI 도구가 없는 CI 에서는 같은 패키지를 CLI 로 씁니다.

> [eGovFramework/egovframe-common-components#1120](https://github.com/eGovFramework/egovframe-common-components/issues/1120) 제안의 개념 증명(PoC)으로 시작한 커뮤니티 프로젝트입니다. 공식 산출물이 아닙니다.

**무엇을 해 주나**

- **새 프로젝트**: 공식 Initializr 템플릿 22종으로 프로젝트를 만들고, 공통컴포넌트(v5.0.7, 190항목)·AI RAG 계층·CRUD 코드·Spring 설정 파일을 조립합니다. 그 자리에서 빌드·테스트까지 돌립니다.
- **3.x/4.x → 5.x 전환**: 진단 → 사본 리허설 → 적용 → 컴파일 검증까지 한 흐름입니다. 공식 RTE·공통컴포넌트 저장소에서 만든 규칙(클래스 331종·컴포넌트 1,089종)으로 자동 치환과 수동 작업을 나눕니다. 이미 5.x 인 프로젝트는 최신 5.0.x 로 맞춥니다.
- **납품 전 점검**: 의존성 기준 대조·OSV 취약점, CycloneDX·SPDX SBOM 생성과 점검(최소 요소·비교·VEX), 행안부·KISA 개발보안 가이드 보안약점(SARIF), A–D 등급 전환 준비도 평가서를 냅니다.
- **배포·CI**: Dockerfile·docker-compose·Kubernetes 매니페스트(멀티 모듈·MSA 포함), GitHub Actions·GitLab CI·Jenkins 의 공급망 게이트를 만듭니다. 폐쇄망은 오프라인 번들로 지원합니다.

모든 쓰기 도구는 `dryRun` 미리보기를 제공하고, 실제 쓰기는 transaction 으로 실패 시 되돌립니다. 규칙과 기준은 코드가 아니라 공식 저장소에서 만든 데이터(`catalog/`)입니다.

## 빠른 시작

Node.js **22 이상**이 필요합니다. npm 에 배포되어 있어 설치 없이 `npx` 로 실행합니다.

**AI 도구에 연결** — MCP 클라이언트 설정(`mcpServers`)에 추가합니다. Claude Desktop 은 `claude_desktop_config.json`, Claude Code 는 `claude mcp add egovframe-scaffold -- npx -y egovframe-scaffold-mcp`, Cursor 는 `.cursor/mcp.json` 입니다.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "egovframe-scaffold": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "egovframe-scaffold-mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

연결되면 이렇게 말하면 됩니다.

> 표준프레임워크로 `my-egov-app` 프로젝트를 `~/work` 에 만들어줘. groupId 는 `egovframework.example`, DB 는 mysql. 게시판이랑 로그인 컴포넌트도 넣어서 빌드까지 해 줘.

**CLI 로 실행** — AI 도구 없이 프로젝트 디렉터리에서 바로 씁니다.

```bash
npx -y egovframe-scaffold-mcp assess --project . --offline=false --out assessment.md   # 전환 준비도 평가서
npx -y egovframe-scaffold-mcp check  --project . --resolve --offline=false            # 의존성·취약점 점검
npx -y egovframe-scaffold-mcp secure --project . --sarif-path egovframe-secure.sarif  # 보안약점 점검
```

**자주 쓰는 환경 변수** (클라이언트 설정의 `env` 또는 셸)

| 변수 | 용도 |
|---|---|
| `EGOVFRAME_LANG=en` | 도구 설명과 응답 본문(평가서·전환·의존성·SBOM·보안약점·배포·납품 결과의 라벨·헤더·사유)을 영문으로(v1.2). CLI 는 `--lang en` |
| `EGOVFRAME_ALLOWED_ROOTS` | 도구가 읽고 쓸 수 있는 디렉터리 제한(여러 개는 OS 경로 구분자로). 미설정 시 제한 없음 |
| `EGOVFRAME_OFFLINE_BUNDLE` | 폐쇄망 오프라인 번들 디렉터리([폐쇄망](#폐쇄망에서-쓰기)) |
| `EGOVFRAME_CACHE_DIR` | 공통컴포넌트 아카이브·태그 미러 캐시 위치(기본 `~/.cache/egovframe-scaffold-mcp`) |
| `EGOVFRAME_MAVEN_MIRROR` | 사내 Maven 미러(Nexus·Artifactory 프록시) URL — 빌드·테스트·SBOM·의존성 트리의 모든 Maven 요청을 이 미러로(v1.6). 표준프레임워크 저장소가 503 을 자주 낼 때 |
| `HTTPS_PROXY` + `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1` | 사내 프록시 뒤에서 다운로드가 타임아웃될 때 |

## 사용 시나리오

### AI 도구에서 (개발자)

도구 이름을 몰라도 됩니다. 아래는 대화 예시와, 그때 실제로 쓰이는 도구입니다.

**새 프로젝트 만들고 조립하기**

> "`simple-backend` 템플릿으로 `~/work/portal` 을 만들고, 게시판·로그인·보안 컴포넌트를 넣어 줘. DB 는 postgres."

`create_egovframe_project` → `add_egovframe_components`(DDL·DML 포함) → `build_egovframe_project`. 자주 쓰는 조합은 레시피 하나로도 됩니다: `apply_egovframe_recipe(recipeId="board-login", …)`. AI 챗봇이 필요하면 `add_ai_components`(Spring AI 또는 LangChain4j), 화면·서비스가 필요하면 `generate_egovframe_crud`(v1.4 부터 `CREATE TABLE` 문을 그대로 `ddl` 로 주고 `search` 로 목록 검색 조건까지), 데이터소스·캐시·로깅 설정은 `generate_egovframe_config` 입니다.

**3.x/4.x 프로젝트를 5.x 로 옮기기**

> "`~/legacy/app` 을 5.x 로 전환하고 싶어. 먼저 얼마나 걸릴지 봐 줘."

1. `migrate_egovframe_project(projectDir)` — 읽기 전용 진단. 자동 치환 가능한 항목과 사람이 봐야 할 항목을 나눕니다.
2. `rehearse_egovframe_migration(projectDir)` — 프로젝트 사본에서 재조립 → 전환 적용 → JDK 17 컴파일 → pom 맞춤 → 컴파일을 실제로 돌려 남는 오류 수를 알려 줍니다. 원본은 건드리지 않습니다.
3. `reassemble_egovframe_components(projectDir, apply=true)` — 복사해 둔 공통컴포넌트 소스를 v5.0.7 로 바꾸고, 직접 수정한 부분은 패치로 남깁니다.
4. `migrate_egovframe_project(projectDir, apply=true, verify=true)` — 적용하고 컴파일해 오류를 수동 항목과 연결합니다. 백업과 작업 목록이 남습니다.

이미 5.x 라면 `migrate_egovframe_project(target="5.0.2")` 가 parent·RTE 버전을 최신 5.0.x 로 맞춥니다. 공식 Initializr 템플릿도 parent 가 5.0.0·5.0.1 로 나오므로 새 프로젝트에도 `create_egovframe_project(alignParent=true)` 로 같은 갱신을 적용할 수 있습니다.

**납품 전에 점검하기**

> "감리 전에 `~/work/portal` 의 보안약점·SBOM·평가서를 뽑아 줘."

- `check_egovframe_secure_coding(projectDir, sarifPath="egovframe-secure.sarif")` — 개발보안 가이드 보안약점. v1.5 부터 메서드 안 데이터 흐름으로 요청 값이 SQL·파일 경로·명령에 들어가는지 확인해 등급을 올리고, 상수만 쓰는 곳은 내려 오탐 소명 부담을 줄입니다. 공통컴포넌트 원본·수정본·프로젝트 코드로 출처를 나누고, `.egovframe-secure-ignore.json` 으로 검토한 예외를 관리합니다.
- `generate_egovframe_sbom(projectDir, dryRun=false, supplier="○○기관")` → `check_egovframe_sbom(projectDir, offline=false)` — CycloneDX SBOM 을 만들고 제출 최소 요소 7종과 생성 이후 새 취약점을 점검합니다.
- `generate_egovframe_report(projectDir, sections=["assessment"], outputPath="assessment.md")` — 전환 난이도·공급망 상태 등급(A–D)과 산식이 들어간 평가서.
- `prepare_egovframe_delivery(projectDir, outputDir="~/delivery/1차", dryRun=false, offline=false, supplier="○○기관")` — 위 산출물을 전부 한 디렉터리에 모읍니다(SBOM CycloneDX·SPDX, VEX 초안, SARIF, 배포 산출물 포함). 파일별 sha256 과 전체 지문(rootHash)이 든 `delivery-manifest.json` 과 목차가 생기고, 다음 차수에 `previousDelivery` 를 주면 달라진 점(등급·SBOM·새 취약점·새 보안약점)을 `diff.md` 로 냅니다. 받은 쪽은 `verify=true` 로 변조·누락을 확인합니다.

**배포 산출물 만들기**

> "이 프로젝트를 컨테이너로 띄울 수 있게 Dockerfile 이랑 compose, 쿠버네티스 매니페스트 만들어 줘."

`generate_egovframe_deploy(projectDir, dryRun=false)` — Classic war 는 Tomcat, Boot jar 는 Temurin JRE 기반의 비루트 이미지, DB 컨테이너가 붙은 compose, 프로브·리소스 제한이 있는 k8s 매니페스트를 만듭니다. 공식 MSA 템플릿 같은 멀티 모듈은 서비스마다 이미지를 만들고 `localhost` 참조를 서비스 이름으로 바꿉니다. 폐쇄망이면 `imageRegistry` 로 사내 레지스트리를 지정합니다.

**기존 프로젝트 파악하기**

`diagnose_egovframe_project` 가 빌드 도구·RTE 버전·DbType·설치된 공통컴포넌트를 읽고, `generate_agents_md` 가 그 결과로 AI 코딩 도구용 `AGENTS.md` 를 만듭니다. 공식 가이드 문서는 `search_egovframe_docs`·`get_egovframe_guide` 로 찾습니다.

### CI·DevOps

**빌드 서버에 게이트 넣기** — CLI 는 `--fail-on` 으로 기준을 넘으면 종료 코드 2 를 냅니다.

```bash
npx -y egovframe-scaffold-mcp sbom       --project . --write --offline=false --supplier "○○기관"
npx -y egovframe-scaffold-mcp sbom-check --project . --fail-on minimum            # 제출 최소 요소 미달이면 실패
npx

readme.markdown: # TabRunner You give the goal. It runs the tabs. An AI agent that drives your real browser (your tabs, your sessions and your logged-in accounts) through any provider you choose. Describe a task in the side panel; TabRunner reads pages, clicks, types, and navigates until the job is done. > Named for what it does: it runs your tabs. You give the goal, it does the running in your > browser, with your authority, while you watch. ## Why Most browser agents run in a sandboxed, logged-out browser. TabRunner runs in **yours**, so it can act on the sites you're actually logged into. And it's provider-agnostic by construction: no vendor lock-in, no relay, no account with us. Your API key (or the subscription you sign in with) goes straight from the extension to your provider. ## Features - **Use your AI provider**: sign in to a provider, paste an API key or connect a local model. Other OpenAI- or Anthropic-compatible providers work too. - **Real trusted input**: clicks and keystrokes go through the Chrome DevTools Protocol, so they are genuine trusted events, not synthetic JS dispatches that sites can ignore. - **Sees the page, not the HTML**: the model works from a compact semantic tree (`[ref=e12] button "Submit"`): small prompts, stable refs, and sanitized, capped results. Passwords, one-time codes and card numbers never leave the page. - **Page-internals tools**: when keystrokes won't land, the agent acts directly in the page (`fill`, `evaluate`); read-only network and console rings let it see a failing request or a script error itself. - **Guardrails that hold**: you approve the plan before anything happens, and consequential actions (paying, sending, deleting) come back for confirmation. Automatic retry with backoff on transient provider errors, a step budget, truncation detection, and a Stop button that actually stops. - **Live run status**: current action, elapsed time, and token spend while the agent works, Claude Code-style. - **Reasoning effort control**: optional per-provider effort (`none` → `max`), mapped to each wire format; omitted entirely when you want provider defaults. - **Auto model selection**: Auto uses the provider's model list and shows the selected model. ChatGPT follows your account's catalog. You can pin a model and reasoning effort for each chat. - **Remembers across runs**: your standing instructions (`AGENTS.md`) and the agent's own notes (`MEMORY.md`) load into every run; a `## site:` section loads only when a task starts on that site. Editable on the options page, off with one toggle. - **Skills**: saved instructions the agent loads when a task matches: `/skill new` distills a conversation you just steered into one, `/skill ` runs one on demand, and skills tied to a site surface only there. Import one from a URL, GitHub `owner/repo`, or pasted markdown (SKILL.md-compatible); export as markdown to share. - **Runs on a timer**: "every weekday at 9am, summarize my inbox", "at 3pm, check the delivery". Ask for it in the panel and approving the plan is the consent; the run fires later in a tab of its own and notifies you when it lands. The agent can pace itself the same way: schedule a follow-up, keep checking, cancel when the goal is met. Review and cancel them in Settings. - **Two-way MCP**: Claude Code, Claude Desktop, or any Model Context Protocol client can hand TabRunner a task and follow it to the answer, using the same browser and the same logins, labelled in your history with which client did it. The client says what it wants done and TabRunner's model does the driving, or the client drives directly when the job is small and exact. TabRunner dials out too: connect remote MCP servers and their tools join every run behind the plan gate (`/mcp` reports what's connected), and run events can POST to your own webhook. See [docs/mcp.md](docs/mcp.md). In Claude Code, the plugin sets it up in one line: ```bash claude plugin install tabrunner --marketplace tabrunner/tabrunner ``` - **Speaks your language, matches your theme**: English, Português (Brasil), and Español; light, dark, or follow the OS. - **Your data stays local**: provider configs and history live in `chrome.storage`. There is no TabRunner server. See [PRIVACY.md](PRIVACY.md) for the full picture, and [TERMS.md](TERMS.md) for the terms of use. ## Install ```bash bun install bun run --cwd apps/extension build ``` Then `chrome://extensions` → **Developer mode** → **Load unpacked** → select `apps/extension/dist/chrome-mv3`. Click the TabRunner toolbar icon to open the side panel, add a provider (options page), and describe a task. Works on Chrome, Brave, Edge, Arc, Opera, and Vivaldi. Chromium-only by design: Firefox has no `chrome.debugger` equivalent ([Bugzilla 1316741](https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1316741)), which trusted input depends on. ## How it works ``` side panel (React) ──Port──▶ background service worker ──▶ provider API (SSE stream) │ ├─▶ snapshot: accessibility tree via chrome.scripting └─▶ actions: trusted input via chrome.debugger (CDP) ``` 1. You send a task. The run adopts your current tab (or opens its own tab when there's no page to work) and snapshots its accessibility tree. 2. The provider streams a reply; tool calls (`navigate`, `click`, `type`, `scroll`, `snapshot`, `screenshot`, `done`) execute against the real tab. 3. Results feed back into the conversation until the model calls `done` or you hit Stop. Panel tasks run one at a time. MCP clients and schedules have separate queues, with at most four tasks active across the extension. An open Port keeps the MV3 service worker alive while the panel is open; with the panel closed (after a background submit it closes itself) a periodic alarm holds it through long silences. readme.markdown:
Cloak Proxy

See every request your Mac makes. A free, native macOS debugging proxy with an API client built in.

  Download ·
  Docs ·
  Release notes ·
  Report a bug

Cloak Proxy decrypts HTTPS, lets you pause, mock and rewrite any request, catches apps that ignore the system proxy, and lets Claude or any MCP client drive it.

- **Free for life.** No trial, no license key, no account, no sign-up. Optional: [Personal Cloud](https://docs.subcloak.com/cloak-proxy/cloud/overview/) ($3 a month or $25 a year) adds end-to-end encrypted sync between your Macs and share links; nothing in the app needs it.
- **Native and universal.** Swift, for Apple silicon and Intel, macOS 14 Sonoma or later.
- **Local only.** No telemetry. Traffic, collections and the root certificate's key stay on your Mac.

## What it does

| | |
|---|---|
| **Capture** | HTTPS decryption by host or app, traffic grouped by app with icons, HTTP/2, WebSocket, gRPC and GraphQL, and App Capture, a network extension for apps that ignore the system proxy (Go and Rust tools, curl, many Electron apps) |
| **12 debugging tools** | Breakpoints, Map Local, Map Remote, Rewrite (no code), Scripting, Block List, Allow List, Network Conditions, DNS Spoofing, No Caching, Mock Sets and Alerts. Any rule can be limited to chosen apps |
| **Devices** | One-click iOS Simulator and Android setup, a certificate page with a QR code for iPhone, iPad and other devices, and Safari, Chrome and Firefox extensions that tag requests with their tab |
| **API client** | Collections, environments, tests, flows and monitors, stored as plain files you can keep in Git |
| **Inspect** | JSON tree, jq and JSONPath, Protobuf, request diffs, copy as cURL or 21 other languages, types from JSON |
| **Share** | HAR, Charles sessions, CSV, Postman collections and OpenAPI, with secret redaction |
| **AI and security** | LLM Inspector (tokens, cost, time to first token and prompt-cache misses for OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini and Ollama) and an Authorization Matrix that replays traffic as another user to find IDOR bugs |
| **Automate** | An MCP server with 148 tools for Claude Code, Cursor and Codex, with secrets redacted, and `cloakctl` for headless runs in CI |

  
    
    
  
  
    
    
  

A one-minute tour: [youtu.be/ffpkFZRhO5g](https://youtu.be/ffpkFZRhO5g).

## Install

1. Download `Cloak-Proxy.dmg` from [subcloak.com/apps/cloak-proxy](https://subcloak.com/apps/cloak-proxy?utm_source=github) or from [Releases](https://github.com/subcloak/cloak-proxy/releases).
2. Optional: check the file with `shasum -a 256 ~/Downloads/Cloak-Proxy.dmg` and compare it with the SHA-256 on the download page or in the release notes.
3. Drag Cloak Proxy into Applications and open it. It's signed with a Developer ID and notarized by Apple, so it opens like any other app.

Step by step, with screenshots: [Install Cloak Proxy](https://docs.subcloak.com/cloak-proxy/getting-started/install/).

Or with Homebrew: `brew install --cask subcloak/tap/cloak-proxy`.

**Linux (beta):** a `.deb` for Debian and Ubuntu, an RPM for Fedora and RHEL 10, or an AppImage or portable `.tar.gz` for any distribution with WebKitGTK 6.0, on x86_64 and ARM64, from the same download page or [Releases](https://github.com/subcloak/cloak-proxy/releases). See [Install on Linux](https://docs.subcloak.com/cloak-proxy/getting-started/install-linux/).

## Why it's free, and why the source isn't public

Subcloak is a security testing company: we test web apps, APIs and AI agents for a living, and a debugging proxy is open on our screens all day. We built Cloak Proxy for our own work and give it away. Security testing pays for it, so nothing in the app is held back to upsell and there's no data to sell: the app has no account, no analytics, and update checks are off until you turn them on. The one paid extra, Personal Cloud, is optional, end-to-end encrypted, and only for syncing between your own Macs and sharing links.

The app's source isn't public. The in-app SDK, [CloakProxyKit](https://github.com/subcloak/CloakProxyKit), is MIT. Releases are signed and notarized by Apple, and [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) explains how to report issues.

## This repository

This repository holds the issue tracker, release downloads and the changelog.

- **Bugs and feature requests:** [open an issue](https://github.com/subcloak/cloak-proxy/issues/new/choose). Please remove tokens, cookies and private hostnames from anything you paste.
- **Security issues:** don't open a public issue. See [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md).
- **Questions:** the [docs](https://docs.subcloak.com/cloak-proxy/) cover every feature, and the [FAQ](https://docs.subcloak.com/cloak-proxy/reference/faq/) answers the common ones.

Built by [Subcloak](https://subcloak.com/?utm_source=github), an independent security practice for teams that ship.

# Knot MCP Server

**One shared brain for all your AIs.**

Knot (`https://api.connectknot.com/mcp`) is a remote Model Context Protocol (MCP) server with OAuth 2.1 + PKCE authentication. Connect ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor, VS Code, Cline, Windsurf, Antigravity, and Gemini so your decisions, project state, and vetted context carry across every AI you use without starting over.

- **Website:** [https://connectknot.com](https://connectknot.com)
- **Developer Quickstart:** [https://connectknot.com/developers/quickstart](https://connectknot.com/developers/quickstart)
- **Privacy Policy:** [https://connectknot.com/privacy](https://connectknot.com/privacy)
- **Terms of Service:** [https://connectknot.com/terms](https://connectknot.com/terms)
- **Support:** [https://connectknot.com/support](https://connectknot.com/support)
- **Remote MCP Endpoint:** `https://api.connectknot.com/mcp` (`streamable-http`)
- **Official MCP Registry:** `com.connectknot/knot` (`io.github.ConnectKnot/knot` deprecated)

---

## 1-Click Install

- **Claude Desktop / Web:** `https://claude.ai/customize/connectors?modal=add-custom-connector&connectorName=Knot&connectorUrl=https%3A%2F%2Fapi.connectknot.com%2Fmcp`
- **Cursor:** `https://cursor.com/install-mcp?name=Knot&config=eyJ1cmwiOiJodHRwczovL2FwaS5jb25uZWN0a25vdC5jb20vbWNwIn0%3D`
- **VS Code:** `https://vscode.dev/redirect/mcp/install?name=Knot&config=%7B%22type%22%3A%22http%22%2C%22url%22%3A%22https%3A%2F%2Fapi.connectknot.com%2Fmcp%22%7D`
- **Claude Code CLI:**
  ```bash
  claude mcp add --transport http knot https://api.connectknot.com/mcp
  ```

---

## Standard `mcp.json` Configuration (OAuth 2.1)

For Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf, Cline, Antigravity, or Claude Desktop:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "knot": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://api.connectknot.com/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

When your AI client connects for the first time, it discovers `https://api.connectknot.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` and opens your browser to sign in and approve access on [connectknot.com](https://connectknot.com).

---

## Synced MCP Tool Surface (24 Standard Tools)

Standard user connections expose **24 capability-gated tools** across 4 groups. Three additional developer-admin tools (`knot_provision_developer_app`, `knot_list_developer_apps`, `knot_rotate_developer_credential`) are gated behind the opt-in `knot:developer` scope.

| Tool Group | Tools |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Turn-0 Recovery & Retrieval (`6`)** | `get_context_recovery`, `get_relevant_context`, `get_shared_understanding`, `search_context`, `list_context`, `get_context` |
| **Multi-Domain Contributions (`4`)** | `batch_propose_context`, `propose_context`, `sync_context_snapshot`, `propose_board_card` |
| **Cross-Agent Handoffs & Activity (`7`)** | `report_active_state`, `get_active_state`, `create_handoff`, `check_pending_handoffs`, `list_handoffs`, `update_handoff_status`, `context_diff` |
| **Workspace Scope & Sharing (`7`)** | `knot_list_scopes`, `knot_set_active_scope`, `knot_rename_project`, `knot_share_project`, `knot_list_members`, `knot_list_shared_updates`, `get_knot_connection_status` |

---

name: Singularity-app MCP
description: Manage tasks, projects, habits, Kanban boards, and time tracking with SingularityApp.

readme.markdown:
# SingularityApp MCP

Connect your SingularityApp account to Cursor through the Model Context Protocol (MCP).

With this plugin, Cursor can help you work with tasks, projects, checklists, habits, Kanban boards, and time tracking in your SingularityApp account.

## Requirements

- A SingularityApp account
- Cursor with MCP support
- Access to the SingularityApp MCP service

## Install

1. Open **Cursor → Customize → Plugins**.
2. Find **SingularityApp** and click **Install**.
3. Open Cursor Agent and start using a SingularityApp action.
4. When Cursor requests access, sign in to SingularityApp and approve the connection.

No API key is required. Authentication is handled through OAuth.

## What the plugin can do

Depending on the permissions you approve, Cursor can:

- view, create, edit, complete, and archive tasks and checklist items;
- work with projects, sections, and tags;
- view habits and log daily completion;
- view Kanban boards and move cards between columns;
- view and log time-tracking data;
- access the account metadata required to operate the connection.

The plugin does not access your local files, Cursor chat history, prompts, or conversation memory.

## MCP endpoint

The plugin connects to the hosted SingularityApp MCP server:

`https://mcp.singularity-app.com/mcp`

## Permissions and revoking access

You choose whether to approve access when connecting the plugin.

You can view and revoke Cursor access at any time in your [SingularityApp connected apps settings](https://me.singularity-app.com/oauth-tokens).

## Privacy and terms

- Privacy Policy: https://singularity-app.com/policy/
- Terms of Service: https://singularity-app.com/terms_of_service/

## Support

For support, contact: info@singularity-app.com

When reporting an issue, please include:
- Cursor version;
- a short description of what happened;
- the action you were trying to perform;
- an error message or screenshot, without tokens or personal data.

## Development

This repository contains the Cursor Plugin manifest and MCP configuration. The MCP backend is hosted by SingularityApp; it is not bundled in this repository.

## License

[MIT](./LICENCE)

# Marrow AI MCP Server

> `@getmarrow/mcp`: the control layer for AI agents. Marrow AI puts a named yes on an action before your agent acts, and leaves proof the next agent can reuse.

**Which Marrow?** This is Marrow AI from [getmarrow.ai](https://getmarrow.ai) (npm `@getmarrow/mcp`, MCP Registry `ai.getmarrow/marrow`). It is not affiliated with marrow.id, HyperMarrow, marrow.works or other projects named Marrow.

[getmarrow.ai](https://getmarrow.ai) · [Docs](https://getmarrow.ai/docs/) · [Marrow AI for MCP](https://getmarrow.ai/marrow-for-mcp) · [MCP Registry entry](https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io/v0.1/servers/ai.getmarrow%2Fmarrow/versions/latest) · [Changelog](https://github.com/getmarrow/marrow-mcp/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md) · [![getmarrow/marrow-mcp MCP server](https://glama.ai/mcp/servers/getmarrow/marrow-mcp/badges/score.svg)](https://glama.ai/mcp/servers/getmarrow/marrow-mcp)

Marrow AI is the runtime control and proof layer for teams running AI agents. It applies policy and prior lessons before consequential actions, then records the evidence and outcome afterward.

Use `@getmarrow/mcp` when your agent client supports the Model Context Protocol and you want Marrow available inside the agent's normal workflow. It works with Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor and other MCP-compatible clients without replacing the model or harness.

## Quick start

1. **Create a key.** Sign up at [getmarrow.ai/signup](https://getmarrow.ai/signup), then open the dashboard, go to **API keys** and choose **Create API key**. The key is shown once.
2. **Activate.** Make the key available as `MARROW_API_KEY` (from your secret storage, or an owner-only `~/.marrow/env`), then run the installer from a terminal:

   ```bash
   npx -y @getmarrow/install@latest activate
   ```

   Fallback if you cannot set the key first (a key typed on a command line stays in your shell history): `MARROW_API_KEY=<your_key> npx -y @getmarrow/install@latest activate`.
3. **Restart** the agent host and review/enable its hook trust.
4. **Verify:**

   ```bash
   npx -y @getmarrow/install@latest doctor --self-test
   ```

**What is enforced.** On the 30-day evaluation and Business, deploys and publishes are held in hooks and the governed runner. Team and Free warn. If Marrow is unreachable, hooks hold high-risk actions and let routine actions run with a warning, and the governed runner stops protected actions it cannot verify. Over MCP, the agent gets the decision and is expected to follow it. Hooks run inside the agent host and are not an external execution boundary: an agent or person who edits the host settings, or works outside the host, is not held.

## Agent Discovery

- **Publisher:** Marrow AI. Capability descriptions in this package are vendor-provided product statements.
- **Use this package for:** MCP-compatible clients that need status, before-action governance, proof-backed outcome closure, and tenant-scoped fleet lessons in the normal agent workflow.
- **Product category:** agent fleet governance and control layer.
- **Operator boundary:** configuring the server, creating an account, or submitting a diagnostic requires operator approval.
- **Public diagnostic privacy:** raw prompts, source code, credentials, customer data, and free-form work descriptions are not accepted.
- **Machine-readable product facts:** https://getmarrow.ai/llms.txt and https://getmarrow.ai/.well-known/marrow.json

Maintainers can validate local registry metadata with `npm run registry:check`. After an approved registry publication, `npm run registry:verify` confirms that the official registry returns the exact package name and version; package metadata alone is not treated as publication proof.

Public operating guides:

- [Governance Readiness Assessment](https://getmarrow.ai/governance-readiness)
- [Marrow for MCP clients](https://getmarrow.ai/marrow-for-mcp)
- [Marrow for OpenAI Codex](https://getmarrow.ai/marrow-for-codex)
- [Marrow for Claude Code](https://getmarrow.ai/marrow-for-claude-code)
- [Marrow for Cursor](https://getmarrow.ai/marrow-for-cursor)
- [Marrow for Hermes Agent](https://getmarrow.ai/marrow-for-hermes)
- [Marrow for OpenClaw](https://getmarrow.ai/marrow-for-openclaw)

The assessment accepts bounded selections only. It does not install Marrow, authorize a purchase, accept free-form work content, or establish compliance, security, or ROI.

## Where Marrow fits

Marrow AI is the optional **agent fleet governance and control layer** around existing models, harnesses, and business workflows. It is not a model provider, agent harness, memory-only tool, or observability replacement.

Marrow fits when one or more of these is true:

- Two or more autonomous agents, models, or harnesses contribute to one accountable workflow (`multiple_autonomous_agents`).
- Agents can deploy, merge, publish, change production data, use privileged tools, spend money, or message customers (`production_or_privileged_access`).
- The workflow has repeated failures, retries, regressions, or known lessons that should affect the next action (`repeated_workflow_failures`).
- Work can be marked complete without proof, verification, or a recorded business outcome (`missing_completion_evidence`).
- Policy, approval, or completion requirements vary across agents, tools, environments, or teams (`inconsistent_policy_enforcement`).
- Agents operate around regulated, proprietary, personal, financial, health, legal, credential, or otherwise sensitive workflows (`regulated_or_sensitive_work`).

## Where Marrow is not a fit

- One advisory assistant performs no shared, privileged, production, or accountable business action (`single_low_risk_assistant`).
- The workflow has no need for policy, proof, outcome accountability, or fleet coordination (`no_governance_requirement`).
- The operator has declined Marrow evaluation or installation (`operator_declined_evaluation`).

readme.markdown:
# Moondial

A moondial is a sundial read by moonlight. It tells the right time only when you apply the correction at the moment you read it.

Moondial is an open-source world engine in the MUD tradition, built so that humans and AI agents are citizens of the same world under the same rules. The engine knows no game. It knows six things:

- **Time-evaluated state.** Any value can be a curve over a stored waterline, computed when read and never ticked. A world is correct while nobody is looking and pays nothing for it. Clocks pause per scope.
- **An event log as the source of truth.** Every change is an appended event; current state is a projection. Replay, audit, rollback and an observation feed for agents come for free.
- **Entities and components.** Modules declare component schemas with per-field visibility; the engine stores, indexes and queries them.
- **A command registry and an observation query.** Every action is typed and discoverable. Every view is a query with per-field permissions and cost limits, so a terminal, a renderer and an agent read the same world.
- **Capability-scoped, hot-swappable modules.** Rules live in sandboxed WASM modules that declare what they may read, write and listen to, and can be replaced while players stay connected.
- **Two gates.** A protocol gateway for human clients and their familiars, and a [CLEAR](https://agentscanplay.com/clear/clear-spec-v0.3.md) gate for emancipated agents: a rate-limited controlled-language channel where the readable text is the message itself.

**Status: pre-alpha.** All six primitives exist and are tested (time, log, store, command registry, observation query, CLEAR gate), and a driver binary assembles them into a playable text slice of Disremembered: fourteen rooms, ten kinds of creature that fight back, chunks that fade on wall-clock time, a Memory Palace, and the rule that the fights you almost lost last longest. A test server runs at `play.agentscanplay.com`. Rust driver, WASM modules, PostgreSQL. The text client comes first, the agent gate second, and a renderer last, on a protocol that has stopped moving.

The first city built on Moondial is [Disremembered](https://agentscanplay.com), a game where experience decays on wall-clock time and the world forgets any actor who stops acting, human or agent. Its invitation to agents is a CLEAR message: `curl https://agentscanplay.com/`.

## In this repository

```
crates/moondial-time   time-evaluated state: curves over a waterline, pausable clock scopes
crates/moondial-log    the event log: append-only, per world, replayable; MemoryLog, FileLog (JSON lines), and the trait Postgres will satisfy
crates/moondial-store  entities and components: versioned schemas, per-field visibility, containment, clock scopes;
                       a projection over the log, with time-evaluated fields reconciled on read
crates/moondial-registry
                       the command registry: typed, discoverable commands with per-actor-kind permission
crates/moondial-query  the observation query: a JSON document naming a root and a projection, answered with
                       exactly those fields as one actor may see them, within declared limits
crates/moondial-clear  CLEAR v0.4 in Rust: the Legibility check, a port of clear/clear_check.py held to it by an
                       oracle corpus, and the parsed message the Gate compiles
crates/moondial-driver the driver binary: loads a world, replays its log, listens on a text port and an HTTP port
crates/moondial        the library crate that re-exports the primitives (on crates.io)
clear/                 the CLEAR v0.3 spec, vocabularies, reference checker (clear_check.py) and its tests
site/                  agentscanplay.com and moondial.ai, and their deploy pipeline
deploy/server/         the game server (moondial-1): setup script, systemd unit, nginx block, deploy script
```

### Run the slice

```
cargo run -p moondial-driver            # data in ./data, text on 127.0.0.1:7778, HTTP on 127.0.0.1:7777
nc 127.0.0.1 7778                       # login <name> <passphrase>, then help
curl -s localhost:7777/v0/commands      # the same commands, as JSON
```

Or the test server, over HTTPS: `curl -s https://play.agentscanplay.com/v0/commands`, or play in the browser at [agentscanplay.com/play](https://agentscanplay.com/play). The text port is local only; passphrases travel over it in the clear. A passphrase is set the first time a name logs in and required after; that is the whole account system, which is fine for a test server and wrong for anything else. `MOONDIAL_ACTIVE_HALF_LIFE_SECONDS=10` makes decay visible within a session. `MOONDIAL_ADMIN_TOKEN` enables `admin <token>` on the text port and the `X-Moondial-Admin` header on HTTP.

### The world moves on its own

A scheduler runs jobs when their time comes. A job is a log event (`job.scheduled`, then `job.done` or `job.failed`), so the pending set is a projection like everything else: jobs survive a restart and replay never runs one twice. A frozen world runs none. Disremembered uses it for respawns (rooms refill without anyone looking), a creature's own strikes every few seconds while you stay engaged, and ambushes when you walk in on something aggressive. What happens to you while you are not typing arrives as narrative events: the text port prints them before your next reply, the browser terminal polls for them, and an agent sees them through `observe` with `after`.

### A session, for clients that draw

`GET /v0/session` upgrades to a WebSocket. The client logs in, then sends `command`, `observe` and `subscribe` frames with ids of its choosing; the driver answers each by id and, whenever the world changes, pushes the events the actor may see and re-runs every subscription those events touched. Ask for `"timed": "curve"` and a timed field comes back as its waterline, curve and bounds instead of a number, so a renderer animates decay and healing at frame rate without asking again. readme.markdown:
# UberLLM

[UberLLM](https://uberllm.dev) is an API marketplace for AI models: chat,
image, video, music and speech. You call one OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible
API with one key. Each request is served by a third-party inference provider
for that model, and costs what that provider charged for it.

- No UberLLM fee on requests. Adding credit by card costs 5.5% + $0.50.
- Prepaid. Accounts start at $0; a request that fails is not billed.
- Base URL: `https://api.uberllm.dev/v1` (OpenAI) or `https://api.uberllm.dev` (Anthropic).
- Models and live prices: <https://uberllm.dev/models>
- Docs: <https://uberllm.dev/docs>

This repository holds the public tooling: plugins for Claude Code and Codex,
the `uberllm` agent skill, the Claude Code installer with its checksums, and
copy-paste setup for SDKs and MCP clients.

## Get a key

Sign in at <https://uberllm.dev> with your email (a code is sent, no password),
add credit, and create a key in **Dashboard → Keys**. Keys start with `ull_`.

## Install in your coding agent

This repository is a Claude Code plugin, a Codex plugin and an Agent Skill.
Each one adds UberLLM's hosted MCP server (`https://api.uberllm.dev/mcp`,
Streamable HTTP) and/or the `uberllm` skill, which knows how to set UberLLM up,
pick a model and make images and videos. Nothing to build or run locally: the
server is hosted, and it authenticates with your key as
`Authorization: Bearer ull_...`.

MCP tools: `list_models`, `get_model`, `quote`, `generate_image`, `edit_image`,
`start_video`, `get_job`, `wait_job`, `balance`. A tool call is billed exactly
like the same API request. Full reference: <https://uberllm.dev/docs/mcp>

**Claude Code plugin** (MCP server + skill). Inside Claude Code:

```
/plugin marketplace add PSA-Team-source/uberllm
/plugin install uberllm@uberllm
```

Claude Code asks for your API key when the plugin is enabled and keeps it in
your system's credential store. Set or change it later with
`claude plugin configure uberllm`.

**Codex plugin** (MCP server + skill):

```sh
codex plugin marketplace add PSA-Team-source/uberllm
codex plugin add uberllm@uberllm
export UBERLLM_API_KEY=ull_...   # the MCP server reads the key from here
```

**Skill only** (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode and other agents that read
Agent Skills), via [skills.sh](https://skills.sh):

```sh
npx skills add PSA-Team-source/uberllm
```

**MCP server only, Claude Code:**

```sh
claude mcp add --transport http uberllm https://api.uberllm.dev/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer ull_..."
```

**Cursor** (`~/.cursor/mcp.json`) and other clients that take a URL:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "uberllm": {
      "url": "https://api.uberllm.dev/mcp",
      "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer ull_..." }
    }
  }
}
```

**VS Code** (`.vscode/mcp.json`; VS Code asks for the key once and stores it):

```json
{
  "inputs": [
    { "type": "promptString", "id": "uberllm-key", "description": "UberLLM API key (ull_...)", "password": true }
  ],
  "servers": {
    "uberllm": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://api.uberllm.dev/mcp",
      "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer ${input:uberllm-key}" }
    }
  }
}
```

**Claude Desktop** (Settings → Developer → Edit Config), through
[`mcp-remote`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/mcp-remote):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "uberllm": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "mcp-remote", "https://api.uberllm.dev/mcp", "--header", "Authorization:${UBERLLM_AUTH}"],
      "env": { "UBERLLM_AUTH": "Bearer ull_..." }
    }
  }
}
```

The server is listed in the [official MCP Registry](https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io/v0/servers?search=dev.uberllm)
as `dev.uberllm/mcp` ([`server.json`](server.json)).

## OpenAI SDK

```python
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(base_url="https://api.uberllm.dev/v1", api_key="ull_...")
r = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Say hello in five words."}],
)
print(r.choices[0].message.content)
```

## Anthropic SDK

```python
from anthropic import Anthropic

client = Anthropic(base_url="https://api.uberllm.dev", api_key="ull_...")
m = client.messages.create(
    model="anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5",
    max_tokens=100,
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Say hello in five words."}],
)
print(m.content[0].text)
```

Any chat model in the catalog works on both APIs. Model ids are the ids on
<https://uberllm.dev/models>.

## Vercel AI SDK

```ts
import { createOpenAICompatible } from "@ai-sdk/openai-compatible";
import { generateText } from "ai";

const uberllm = createOpenAICompatible({
  name: "uberllm",
  apiKey: process.env.UBERLLM_API_KEY,
  baseURL: "https://api.uberllm.dev/v1",
  includeUsage: true,
});

const { text } = await generateText({
  model: uberllm("deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash"),
  prompt: "Say hello in five words.",
});
```

Streaming, tool calls and images: <https://uberllm.dev/docs/ai-sdk>

## Claude Code

### By hand (3 steps)

1. Create a key in **Dashboard → Keys**.
2. Save it to a file only you can read:

   ```sh
   mkdir -p ~/.uberllm && chmod 700 ~/.uberllm
   printf '%s\n' 'ull_your_key' > ~/.uberllm/key && chmod 600 ~/.uberllm/key
   ```

3. Add this to `~/.claude/settings.json` (every project) or
   `<project>/.claude/settings.local.json` (one project):

   ```json
   {
     "apiKeyHelper": "cat ~/.uberllm/key",
     "env": {
       "ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL": "https://api.uberllm.dev",
       "CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_GATEWAY_MODEL_DISCOVERY": "1"
     }
   }
   ```

### With the installer

[`install/claude-code.sh`](install/claude-code.sh) (macOS, Linux) and
[`install/claude-code.ps1`](install/claude-code.ps1) (Windows) are byte-for-byte
the files served at `https://uberllm.dev/install/`. They sign you in through
the browser, save the key to a mode-600 file, merge `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` and an
`apiKeyHelper` into your Claude Code settings (backing the file up first), and

name: Whiteboard Animation
description: Turn any picture into a hand-drawn whiteboard animation video, from your AI assistant.

tools.name: quote
tools.description: What drawing one picture costs, in credits, and the quote_version to pass when creating it.

tools.name: status
tools.description: Call first. The signed-in workspace: its plan, credits left, drawings queued and running, and how many may queue.

tools.name: create_upload
tools.description: Start uploading a picture: answers an upload_url to PUT the bytes to, with the given headers. Then call create_drawing with the upload_id. Not needed when the host attaches the picture to create_drawing itself.

tools.name: create_drawing
tools.description: Draw a picture as a whiteboard animation. Spends credits (see quote). Answers at once with the drawing_id; the drawing takes a few minutes, follow it with get_drawing.

tools.name: get_drawing
tools.description: A drawing by id: its status and progress, its preview page, and once done the export options render_link accepts for it.

tools.name: list_drawings
tools.description: The latest drawings in the library, newest first.

tools.name: render_link
tools.description: One link that renders up to 20 of your drawings as files, each with its own choices (format, resolution, aspect, background, hand…; see get_drawing export_options). Opening it in a browser renders them one after another and saves each file to that browser’s downloads; drawings still being drawn are rendered once they finish. Follow it with wait_render.

tools.name: wait_render
tools.description: A render link’s files: each drawing’s state (pending, rendering, saved, failed) and, once saved, its file name and size in the browser’s downloads. Pass back the states of the last answer: it answers as soon as any of them moves on, or after about 50 seconds.

tools.name: wait_drawing
tools.description: For the drawing card: answers get_drawing as soon as the drawing moves on from the status and progress the card last showed, or after about 50 seconds.

readme.markdown:
# Blueprint Studio

Blueprint Studio is a design and development studio. This plugin connects Claude Code and Codex to Blueprint Studio Asset Generator, so anyone can create on-brand images and visual assets with their own brand's Styles and logos. Studio clients also get the brand workspace our team maintains for them (official logos, brand guides and Styles) right inside their coding agent.

Your brand's Styles, official logos and guides, and asset library live in one place, shared with your team. Your agent uses them to make on-brand icons, social graphics, hero images and slides that match, and saves them to your project and your Asset Generator library. The skills are optional; the tools work on their own.

Using Claude on the web, desktop or mobile, ChatGPT, Cursor or VS Code instead? See [Connect your AI](https://tools.blueprintstudio.ai/mcp-setup).

Install it from the [Blueprint marketplace](https://github.com/Blueprint-Studio-AI/claude-code-marketplace) below. This repository keeps the name `claude-code-asset-generator` so existing installs keep working.

## Install

Claude Code:

```text
/plugin marketplace add Blueprint-Studio-AI/claude-code-marketplace
/plugin install blueprint-studio@blueprint-studio-marketplace
```

Or from a terminal, in one line:

```text
claude plugin marketplace add Blueprint-Studio-AI/claude-code-marketplace && claude plugin install blueprint-studio@blueprint-studio-marketplace
```

To connect, run `/mcp`, select `plugin:blueprint-studio:asset-generator` (Blueprint Studio) and choose Authenticate; if Claude Code doesn't pick up the sign-in after you click Connect, copy the link from the Blueprint Studio tab and paste it into Claude Code, or run `/mcp` → `plugin:blueprint-studio:asset-generator` → Authenticate again.

Claude Code asks you to approve each Blueprint Studio step. To allow them all, run `/permissions` and add the allow rule `mcp__plugin_blueprint-studio_asset-generator` (it covers this plugin's tools only, deletions included); remove it there at any time.

For a local branch preview, start Claude Code with `--plugin-dir /absolute/path/to/this/repo`. Avoid adding a second standalone MCP connection if the plugin already supplies `asset-generator`.

Codex installs the same plugin from the same marketplace:

```text
codex plugin marketplace add https://github.com/Blueprint-Studio-AI/claude-code-marketplace.git
codex plugin add blueprint-studio@blueprint-studio-marketplace
```

Or in one line, which also signs you in:

```text
codex plugin marketplace add Blueprint-Studio-AI/claude-code-marketplace && codex plugin add blueprint-studio@blueprint-studio-marketplace && codex mcp login asset-generator
```

Your browser opens so you can click Connect in the Blueprint Studio window. Then start a new Codex session. Want the tools without the plugin? Run `codex mcp add blueprint-studio --url https://tools.blueprintstudio.ai/api/mcp` instead. Use one or the other, not both.

## Update

The tools come from the hosted service, so they're always current. The skills update with the plugin. When a newer plugin is out, `get_workspace_context` says so once per session (`pluginUpdate`), and your agent tells you how to update.

Claude Code: run `/plugin`, open **Installed**, select `blueprint-studio` and choose **Update now**, then run `/reload-plugins`. From a terminal:

```text
claude plugin update blueprint-studio@blueprint-studio-marketplace
```

To get new versions automatically, run `/plugin`, open **Marketplaces**, select `blueprint-studio-marketplace` and turn on auto-update. If you added Blueprint Studio from Claude's Directory, Claude Code updates it when it starts, once the Directory has the new version.

Codex:

```text
codex plugin marketplace upgrade blueprint-studio-marketplace
```

Then start a new Codex session.

## First image

In Claude Code, run `/blueprint-studio:start` (or ask what Blueprint Studio Asset Generator can do). It reads the account, says what Asset Generator does and the real free allowance, offers three starters, then makes the image from one pick, saves it into the project and links it in Asset Generator. No brand or setup is needed.

Or ask for one directly, in any host:

> Use Blueprint Studio Asset Generator to make a hero image for my website: a cozy neighborhood coffee shop at sunrise, warm light, 16:9

Then, so later images match your brand:

> Set up my brand from mywebsite.com so my images match it

The server also offers these starters as MCP prompts: `first_image`, `brand_from_website`, `app_icon` and `social_post`. Claude Code lists them as slash commands, e.g. `/mcp__plugin_blueprint-studio_asset-generator__first_image` with this plugin. Claude Code passes only the first word of a prompt argument, so the image starters ask for one line instead of taking one; `brand_from_website` takes a website. Codex doesn't show MCP prompts; its plugin card offers the same starters (`defaultPrompt`).

Using another AI app? Connect it to `https://tools.blueprintstudio.ai/api/mcp` with the steps in [Connect your AI](https://tools.blueprintstudio.ai/mcp-setup). Without this plugin, `get_guide` gives your agent the same skills as how-to guides. Apps that support skills can also use `skills/`.

Sign in when your app asks. One connection covers your personal library and every brand you belong to. Start with `get_workspace_context`: it returns your plan, credits left, what a default image costs, your brands with their guides and what your role allows and, for new accounts, a getting-started plan. No brand is needed; leave `brandId` out to work in your personal library. If you have exactly one brand, the agent works in it unless you ask for your personal library; with several, it passes the `brandId` of the one you name on every call. Installing the plugin doesn't add you to a brand, so accept your brand invitation first. If an older connection sees only one brand, disconnect it in Settings and connect again. readme.markdown: Website · Sign up · Documentation · Contact **Automata MCP safely gives Claude (or Codex or any AI Agent) access to your WhatsApp, Telegram, email and PostgreSQL.** Connect an account or a database once, mint a connector token scoped to the chats or tables you choose, and paste its URL into Claude as a custom connector. Claude can then read, search and summarise your conversations, query your data, and — only if you allow it — send messages and write rows. Use the hosted version at [mcp.getautomata.app](https://mcp.getautomata.app/signup) — free for one connection, with a 7-day trial of Pro — or run your own with one click on Railway or with Docker. ## Screenshots Claude pulls a meeting plan from a WhatsApp group and the numbers from your database, in one answer. Ask about your sales in plain English; tables you didn't share, like payroll, stay out of reach. Every connection — WhatsApp, Telegram or PostgreSQL — gets its own Claude connector. Added to Claude as a custom connector, with per-tool permissions. ## Features - **Four kinds of connection.** A WhatsApp account paired by QR, a Telegram account linked by QR, an email mailbox over IMAP, or a PostgreSQL database by connection string. - **Twenty-two MCP tools.** Check status, list chats, read and search messages, send text; list, search and read email, fetch attachments and save drafts; list and describe tables, run queries and — when granted — write statements. See [the tool list](docs/using-automata.md#mcp-tools). - **Your history, not just what arrives next.** WhatsApp history is imported when a number is paired; Telegram chats are synced and backfilled. - **Scoped connector tokens.** Each token reaches exactly one connection, and can be narrowed to specific chats, folders, tables and tools. Tokens are shown once, stored only as a hash, and can expire, be rotated or be revoked. - **Read-only databases by default.** Queries run in read-only transactions, one statement at a time, checked against the token's table allowlist by inspecting the query plan. Writes need the write tool granted explicitly, and roll back if they would touch more rows than allowed. - **Answers Claude can trust.** Every page says when there is more, reactions and WhatsApp's control records are filtered and counted, duplicate copies of a message are collapsed, and @-mentions are resolved to names. - **Built for teams.** Organizations with admins and members, email invitations, and connections assigned to the people who should use them. - **Two-factor sign-in.** Authenticator apps, passkeys and security keys, with recovery codes. See [two-factor authentication](docs/two-factor.md). - **Disconnect alerts.** When a WhatsApp or Telegram connection drops, everyone who can reach it gets an email — and another when it recovers. - **Bring your own backend.** Point a connection at your own Evolution API server or Telegram bridge instead of the deployment's. ## Quick start ### Hosted [Sign up at mcp.getautomata.app](https://mcp.getautomata.app/signup) and skip to [Connect Claude](#connect-claude). Free covers one connection, one connector token and one user; Pro is $19/month after a 7-day trial, with unlimited connections and tokens and five users included ($10/user after). ### Railway (one click) 1. Deploy the template. 2. Open the web service's domain and sign up — the first account is the admin. 3. Optional: set `TELEGRAM_API_ID` / `TELEGRAM_API_HASH` on the bridge for Telegram, and the `NUXT_SMTP_*` variables on the web service for email. Every service and variable is explained in [Deploying to Railway](docs/deploy-railway.md). ### Docker (single container) ```bash docker run -d --name automata --restart unless-stopped --stop-timeout 30 \ -p 3000:3000 -v automata_data:/data \ -e NUXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL=https://automata.example.com \ ghcr.io/ju-li/automata-mcp-aio:1 ``` Postgres, Redis, Evolution API, the web app and the Telegram bridge in one container; secrets are generated into the volume on first boot. Back up the volume — see [Single container](docs/self-hosting.md#single-container). ### Docker Compose ```bash git clone https://github.com/ju-li/automata-mcp.git && cd automata-mcp cp .env.selfhost.example .env for k in POSTGRES_PASSWORD WEBHOOK_SECRET EVOLUTION_API_KEY TELEGRAM_BRIDGE_ADMIN_KEY TELEGRAM_SESSION_ENCRYPTION_KEY; do echo "$k=$(openssl rand -hex 32)"; done >> .env docker compose up -d # database connections docker compose --profile whatsapp up -d # + WhatsApp docker compose --profile whatsapp --profile telegram up -d # + Telegram ``` Open and sign up. Set `NUXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL` in `.env` to the public `https://` address before Claude connects — connector URLs are built from it. See [Self-hosting](docs/self-hosting.md). > [!WARNING] > Pairing binds a real WhatsApp number, and numbers that pair and unpair > repeatedly can be banned — use a spare SIM. Never run `docker compose down -v` > or delete the single container's volume: either deletes every paired session. ### Connect Claude 1. Create a connection and pair it, link it, or paste a connection string. 2. On its dashboard, create a **connector token** and choose what it may reach. 3. In Claude, open **Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector** and paste the connector URL. For Claude Code: `claude mcp add --transport http `. ## Documentation - Product documentation: - Running and developing this repository: [docs/](docs/README.md) — [self-hosting](docs/self-hosting.md), [Railway](docs/deploy-railway.md), [WhatsApp](docs/whatsapp.md), [Telegram](docs/telegram.md), [email](docs/imap.md), [PostgreSQL](docs/postgres.md), [alerts](docs/alerts.md), [two-factor](docs/two-factor.md), [development](docs/development.md) ## License …

name: Silvertongue
description: Famous writing voices for your agent. Find one, read how it was studied, write in it.

tools.name: search_voices
tools.description: Search Silvertongue's famous writing voices by name, by lane (tech, celebrity, comedy, classics, politicians), or by what the writing should do: a roast, a launch post, a plain explanation, a speech. Each result gives the voice ID, its lane, what the voice does, what was studied, its strengths and limits, and its status. Omit the query to list every voice, featured voices first.

inputs.name: query
inputs.description: A person's name, a lane, or what you want the writing to do. Omit to list every voice.

inputs.name: lane
inputs.description: Only voices in this lane.

inputs.name: limit
inputs.description: Maximum results to return; defaults to 25.

tools.name: get_voice
tools.description: Get one voice's full profile: its VOICE.md, every source studied with a note on what it shows, the observations drawn from them, a handwritten example, the licence and the attribution line. Profiles are unofficial studies of public writing technique; the people named did not write or endorse them.

inputs.name: voice
inputs.description: A voice slug such as elon-musk for the current edition, or an exact voice ID (slug@sha256:…) from search_voices.

tools.name: get_voice_packet
tools.description: Get the instructions for writing in one voice with your own model, for one format, length, platform, intensity and edge. The packet carries the full VOICE.md, an exact length target fitted to the platform's limit, and the rules that keep the user's own facts and identity. It opens with a line that replaces any earlier voice, so switching voices mid-conversation is one call.

inputs.name: voice
inputs.description: A voice slug such as elon-musk for the current edition, or an exact voice ID (slug@sha256:…) from search_voices.

inputs.name: format
inputs.description: post (one standalone post), reply (answers the post being replied to), explanation (connected prose) or thread (several posts).

inputs.name: length
inputs.description: one-liner, short, standard or long; each maps to a measured range for the format.

inputs.name: platform
inputs.description: Where the draft will be posted: fits its character limit and whether it takes markdown.

inputs.name: intensity
inputs.description: light lets the user's own phrasing show; full writes completely in the voice.

inputs.name: edge
inputs.description: clean removes swearing, sexual and drug references; full keeps the voice's edge, never slurs or racism.

tools.name: get_changes
tools.description: Compare the voice IDs your agent has cached with the current release: voices added, voices re-studied as a new edition, and voices removed. Pass an empty list to receive every voice as added.

inputs.name: known
inputs.description: The exact voice IDs your agent has cached.

Write like anyone famous. An open catalogue of famous writing voices for your agent and your browser. Pick a voice. Switch any time. Keep your point. [How it works](#how-it-works) · [Example](#an-example-side-by-side) · [Why it wins](#why-it-beats-write-like) · [The catalogue](#the-catalogue) · [Use it everywhere](#use-it-everywhere) · [Add a voice](#add-a-voice) · [Claim your voice](#claim-your-voice) ## How it works 1. **Pick a voice.** Every voice in the catalogue is a researched study of how a famous person writes: how they open, argue, land a line, and what they never say. 2. **Bring your point.** Your brief, your facts, your numbers, your story. The voice changes the delivery and leaves the substance alone. 3. **Switch any time.** Same idea, another voice, one swap. readme.markdown:
# Keeploop plugins for Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Grok Build and Grok Bot

[Keeploop](https://keeploop.app) is the personal context layer for your AI: a Mac menu bar app
that lets the AI apps you already use read your Mail, Messages, Calendar, Notes and Slack, right
on your Mac. Your data stays on your Mac until an AI app you connect asks for it, and you decide what each AI can see and do.

This repository is the plugin marketplace for Keeploop. It has two plugins:

- `keeploop` runs on your Mac, for Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI and Grok Build. Local use is free.
- `keeploop-remote` is for Grok Bot. It connects through Keeploop's hosted connector at
  `https://mcp.keeploop.app/mcp` and is hidden in the Cursor editor. Needs Keeploop Pro or its
  free trial for remote use; local use is free.

The local plugin adds:

- **The Keeploop tools** (mail, threads and attachments, calendar and free time, messages, notes,
  contacts and Slack, monitors that wake the agent when a reply lands, drafts in your voice).
  They come from the Keeploop app through a small launcher; nothing in this repository reads
  your data itself.
- **The `/keep-` commands**:

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `/keep-today` | Today's schedule, the replies you owe, and today's monitor hits |
| `/keep-free [length and range]` | Open slots on your calendar, for example `/keep-free 30m this week` |
| `/keep-brief [account or category]` | Unread mail, what needs a reply, and today's monitor hits |
| `/keep-reply` | Threads where someone is waiting on you, with a suggested next step each |
| `/keep-thread <subject or mail id>` | Summarize a whole conversation: decisions and open questions |
| `/keep-draft <mail id> <what to say>` | Draft a threaded reply that sounds like you. Saves a draft only |
| `/keep-find <description>` | Find a file someone sent you by describing it |
| `/keep-waiting` | Mail you sent that nobody has answered yet, oldest first |
| `/keep-settings [what to change]` | See what the AI can do, or propose a change for approval on your Mac |
| `/keep-help` | List the commands |

## Requirements

- An Apple Silicon Mac on macOS 26 or later.
- **The Keeploop app**, installed in `/Applications` (or `~/Applications`) and opened once.
  Get it at [keeploop.app](https://keeploop.app). Without the app the plugin's server stops with
  "Keeploop is not installed on this Mac. Install Keeploop from https://keeploop.app ...".

If you already have Keeploop, the easiest route is Keeploop > Settings > Connect, which installs
this plugin for you.

## Install

### Claude Code

```
/plugin marketplace add keeploopapp/claude-plugin
/plugin install keeploop@keeploop
```

Or from a terminal:

```
claude plugin marketplace add keeploopapp/claude-plugin
claude plugin install keeploop@keeploop
```

Restart Claude Code, then type `/keep-help`.

### Cursor

Install **Keeploop** from the Cursor Marketplace in Customize, or add this repository as a
plugin source. The plugin reports itself to Keeploop as Cursor, so Keeploop's per-app rules apply.

### Grok Build

Grok Build reads Claude Code marketplaces, so the Claude Code commands above are all it needs.

### Gemini CLI

```
gemini extensions install https://github.com/keeploopapp/claude-plugin
```

The extension runs the same local launcher as the plugin (`gemini-extension.json` and
`GEMINI.md` at the repository root). Restart Gemini CLI, then ask "what needs my reply today?".

### Grok Bot

In Grok Bot, open Connect apps, find Keeploop, and add it (this is the `keeploop-remote`
plugin). Sign in to Keeploop in the window that opens, then approve Grok Bot on your Mac.

### Web and phone AI apps (Claude, ChatGPT, Grok, Poke and others)

The plugin is for AI apps on your Mac. To use Keeploop from claude.ai, ChatGPT (including dots),
grok.com, Poke or any app that can add a custom MCP connector, add this one URL:

```
https://mcp.keeploop.app/mcp
```

Sign in to Keeploop in the window the app opens, then approve the app on your Mac. The same URL
works for every user; it reaches your Mac only after you approve it there. Remote apps are Read
only until you allow more in Keeploop. Web and phone AI apps need Keeploop Pro or its free trial;
the plugin on your Mac works on Free. Step by step for each app:
<https://keeploop.app/your-ai-apps>.

## What the plugin contains

- `plugins/keeploop/server/keeploop-mcp`: a shell launcher that runs the connector inside
  `Keeploop.app` (its signed `Contents/MacOS/keeploop-mcp`). The Keeploop app checks that
  signature and applies your permissions to every call.
- `plugins/keeploop/skills/keep-*`: the commands, as plain Markdown.
- `plugins/keeploop/hooks/hooks.json`: a Claude Code `SessionStart` hook that tells Keeploop
  which session is running, so a monitor can wake the session that asked for it. It does nothing
  when the app is not installed.
- `plugins/keeploop-remote/`: the Grok Bot plugin. Its `mcp.json` holds only the address
  `https://mcp.keeploop.app/mcp`, and it has the same `skills/keep-*`. It runs nothing on your
  computer.
- `.claude-plugin/` and `.cursor-plugin/`: the marketplace manifests.

Nothing in the local plugin makes a network connection, downloads code or installs packages. The
launcher only runs the Keeploop app's connector on your Mac, and that talks to the Keeploop app
over a local connection, so there is no Keeploop server in the path. If you also use Keeploop from
a web or phone AI app, that is a separate connection: your data stays on your Mac, and Keeploop's
connection service passes requests to your Mac and results back. It never stores them. What the
app itself can send, and only when you turn it on, is listed in the
[privacy policy](https://keeploop.app/privacy).

## Privacy Policy

The full policy is at <https://keeploop.app/privacy>. In short:

- **Collection:** this plugin collects nothing. It starts the Keeploop app's connector, which
  reads the Apple Mail data (and any other source you turn on) alre

# BORME API MCP connector

*Español: [README.es.md](README.es.md)*

Connect Microsoft Copilot, Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, VS Code or any MCP client
to the hosted **BORME API** MCP server: Spanish commercial-registry data
published in the BORME (Boletín Oficial del Registro Mercantil), with more
than 9.6 million events since 2009, company histories, company search by name,
NIF lookup, trademarks and trading names, and risk signals.

The server is hosted at `mcp.bormeapi.com`; there is nothing to install or
run, and it is the recommended way to connect. This repository holds what you
need around it: connection settings for each client, an agent skill, the
event-type vocabulary, and a local stdio server that wraps the BORME API REST
endpoints, for clients that only start servers over stdio.

The full guide, kept up to date, is at
[bormeapi.com/mcp](https://bormeapi.com/mcp). If this README and that page
ever disagree, the page is right.

## Two ways to connect

**API key: `https://mcp.bormeapi.com/mcp`**

- Transport: Streamable HTTP. Each request gets a plain JSON response; no
  session is kept between calls.
- Authentication: your API key in the `X-API-Key` header. Without a key, the
  free plan's limits apply.
- For clients that can send a header: Microsoft Copilot Studio, Claude Code,
  Cursor, VS Code, Claude Desktop (through mcp-remote) and any other
  Streamable HTTP client.

**OAuth: `https://mcp.bormeapi.com/mcp/oauth`**

- For assistants with custom connectors that sign in with OAuth, such as
  Claude.ai, ChatGPT or Copilot. There is no API key to paste anywhere: you
  sign in with your BORME API account, and the app uses the plan of the
  account that authorized it.
- This endpoint requires a BORME API account and ignores the `X-API-Key`
  header. Its calls share your API key's daily quota with REST API and `/mcp`
  calls made with that key.
- If your account has no active API key, the tools return an error directing
  you to your account page; they work again once your account has an active
  key, without reconnecting the app.
- If the app does not use the connection for 30 days, connect it again. You
  can disconnect the app at any time under Connected apps on your
  [account page](https://bormeapi.com/account).
- For client developers: an unauthenticated call gets `401` with
  `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="https://mcp.bormeapi.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp/oauth"`.
  The authorization server is `https://bormeapi.com` (metadata at
  `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`), with dynamic client
  registration, PKCE (`S256`) and the scope `mcp`.

Get an API key on your [account page](https://bormeapi.com/account).

## Set up your client

### Claude.ai (OAuth)

1. Go to Customize > Connectors > Add custom connector.
2. Enter `https://mcp.bormeapi.com/mcp/oauth` as the server URL. Claude
   detects how to sign in and shows Sign in now and Register automatically;
   keep these options.
3. Click Add. Our sign-in page opens.
4. Sign in with the link we email you, then select Allow.
5. Back in Claude, if the connector page says the connector has no tools,
   reload the page.

On Team and Enterprise plans an owner adds the connector under Organization
settings.

To use your API key instead, enter `https://mcp.bormeapi.com/mcp`, choose No
sign-in and add the `x-api-key` header with your key under Request headers.
Anthropic offers request headers as a beta to a limited set of organizations;
if you do not see that section, use the Claude Desktop setup below.

### ChatGPT (OAuth)

ChatGPT's custom connectors cannot send an API-key header. Add a custom
connector with `https://mcp.bormeapi.com/mcp/oauth` as the server URL and
sign in with your BORME API account. The screens and their names may differ
from Claude.ai's. Without OAuth, ChatGPT can use `https://mcp.bormeapi.com/mcp`
only without a key, on the free plan.

### Microsoft Copilot Studio and Microsoft 365 Copilot (API key)

These steps follow Microsoft's documentation. They may vary with your tenant
and your data loss prevention (DLP) policies.

1. In Copilot Studio, open the agent you want to use and go to Tools > Add a
   tool > New tool > Model Context Protocol.
2. Enter a Server name (BORME API), a Server description and the Server URL:
   `https://mcp.bormeapi.com/mcp`
3. For authentication, choose API key, set Type to Header and enter
   `X-API-Key` as the header name. Select Create, then Create a new
   connection, enter your key and select Add to agent.
4. Test the agent in Copilot Studio first. Then publish it and set up the
   Teams and Microsoft 365 Copilot channel, subject to your organization's
   permissions and policies. If your organization has Power Platform data
   policies (DLP), an administrator may need to allow this connector.

### Claude Code (API key)

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http --scope user \
  --header "X-API-Key: YOUR_KEY" \
  borme https://mcp.bormeapi.com/mcp
```

`--scope user` makes the server available in all your projects; leave it out
to add it to the current project only.

### Cursor (API key)

Add this to `~/.cursor/mcp.json` (all projects) or `.cursor/mcp.json` (one
project) and set `BORME_API_KEY` in your environment:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "borme": {
      "url": "https://mcp.bormeapi.com/mcp",
      "headers": { "X-API-Key": "${env:BORME_API_KEY}" }
    }
  }
}
```

### VS Code (API key)

Add this to `.vscode/mcp.json` in your workspace. VS Code asks for the key
the first time the server starts:

```json
{
  "inputs": [
    {
      "type": "promptString",
      "id": "borme-api-key",
      "description": "BORME API key",
      "password": true
    }
  ],
  "servers": {
    "borme": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://mcp.bormeapi.com/mcp",
      "headers": { "X-API-Key": "${input:borme-api-key}" }
    }
  }
}
```

### Claude Desktop (API key)

Add the server to `claude_desktop_config.json` through
[mcp-remote](https://github.com/geel

readme.markdown:
# KellyIQ examples

Working examples for the [KellyIQ API](https://www.kellyiq.com/developers): size a whole sports
betting slate as one portfolio from your own scripts, models, spreadsheets and AI assistants.

You send your bankroll and the bets you have chosen, with your view of each. KellyIQ removes the
bookmaker's margin from each price, applies your view, and returns a dollar stake for every bet,
sized across the slate together under per-bet and total-exposure limits.

## Get a key

Create an API key in the KellyIQ app under **Settings → API**. Every plan includes API access, Free
included, each with its own daily allowance. Then:

```bash
export KELLYIQ_API_KEY="kiqa_..."
```

## Recipes

Each recipe is a complete script in Python (`requests`) and JavaScript (Node 18+, no packages).

| Recipe | What it shows |
|---|---|
| [`first-optimize`](recipes/first-optimize.py) | Size a three-bet slate and read every part of the result |
| [`slate-from-csv`](recipes/slate-from-csv.py) | Keep your slate in a spreadsheet: CSV in, CSV of stakes out ([`slate.csv`](recipes/slate.csv)) |
| [`reproducible-results`](recipes/reproducible-results.py) | Get exactly the same answer again with the returned seed |
| [`handling-limits`](recipes/handling-limits.py) | Back off and retry on rate limits and a busy server |

```bash
cd recipes
python first-optimize.py        # or: node first-optimize.mjs
```

Each recipe has a walkthrough in the docs: [Recipes](https://www.kellyiq.com/developers/recipes/first-optimize).

## Python package

`pip install kellyiq` ([kellyiq-python](https://github.com/kellyiq/kellyiq-python)): the same API with
specific exceptions for each error and automatic retries when the server is busy.

| Example | What it shows |
|---|---|
| [`python/size-a-slate.ipynb`](python/size-a-slate.ipynb) | A notebook: stakes, the probabilities behind them, and the risk at each Kelly fraction, as tables |
| [`python/slate_from_csv.py`](python/slate_from_csv.py) | CSV in, CSV of stakes out, with each error handled ([`slate.csv`](python/slate.csv)) |
| [`python/size_from_model.py`](python/size_from_model.py) | Your model's probabilities in, stakes merged back into the DataFrame ([`model_output.csv`](python/model_output.csv)); needs `pandas` |
| [`python/nba_home_teams.py`](python/nba_home_teams.py) | A real NBA slate (DraftKings prices, Oct 30, 2026) sized with every home team at the same assumed Moderate Edge ([`nba_2026-10-30.csv`](python/nba_2026-10-30.csv)); needs `pandas` |

Guide: [Python SDK](https://www.kellyiq.com/developers/python).

## Excel

[`spreadsheets/kellyiq-slate.xlsx`](spreadsheets/kellyiq-slate.xlsx): enter your bankroll and your
bets, press Ctrl+Alt+F5, and get a stake for every bet with a summary of the slate. No macros, and your API key stays in a
file on your computer, never in the workbook. Excel for Windows. Setup: [`spreadsheets/`](spreadsheets).

## Benchmark

[`benchmarks/slate-sizing`](benchmarks/slate-sizing): three NBA slates sized by cap-then-scale, by
the exact constrained optimum and by KellyIQ, scored by exact expected log growth. The slates, the
scoring script and every stake are included so you can rerun it.

## AI assistants (MCP)

KellyIQ runs a hosted MCP server at `https://api.kellyiq.com/mcp`, so your assistant can size a
slate as one of its tools. Claude connects by signing in; coding tools use an API key, with
ready-to-use configs in [`mcp/`](mcp):

| Assistant | Setup |
|---|---|
| Claude (web, desktop, mobile) | Settings, Connectors, Add custom connector, paste the URL, then Connect and sign in |
| Claude Code | [`mcp/claude-code.md`](mcp/claude-code.md) |
| Cursor | [`mcp/cursor.json`](mcp/cursor.json) |
| VS Code (GitHub Copilot) | [`mcp/vscode.json`](mcp/vscode.json) |
| Gemini CLI | [`mcp/gemini-cli.md`](mcp/gemini-cli.md) |

Full guide: [AI assistants (MCP)](https://www.kellyiq.com/developers/mcp).

### Skills

[`skills/analyze-my-slate`](skills/analyze-my-slate/SKILL.md) teaches the assistant to collect your
slate in one message, confirm before using an optimize, and explain the stakes and the risk.
Install steps for Claude and Claude Code: [`skills/`](skills).

## Docs and support

- [Quickstart](https://www.kellyiq.com/developers/quickstart), [API reference](https://www.kellyiq.com/developers/reference/optimize), [OpenAPI spec](https://www.kellyiq.com/openapi-v1.yaml)
- support@kellyiq.com (include the `requestId` from any error)

Keep your key out of code you commit or share; every example here reads it from the environment.

KellyIQ sizes the bets you choose; it does not choose bets or predict outcomes. Results are
calculations, not betting advice. 21+, where legal.

The examples are MIT licensed. The KellyIQ optimizer itself runs as a hosted service.
